### RD.3.8 Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra

**Lemma.** Let `X = Spec A_0` be a smooth affine `k`-scheme, `A` a smooth `O`-algebra lifting `A_0` with a presentation `A = O[t_1`..`t_n]/I, 𝔛 = Spec A ⊂ A^n_O ⊂ P^n_O, 𝔛̄` the projective closure of `𝔛` in `P^n_O`, `P` its formal completion, and `Y=𝔛̄_k` its entire special fibre, with `Z=Y∖X`. Then for `λ < 1, U_λ = 𝔛_K^an ∩` {closed ball of radius 1/`λ`}, and `Γ(]Y[_P, j†O) = lim_{λ→1} Γ(U_λ, O) = A† ⊗ K`, the weak completion of A tensored with `K` (the Monsky-Washnitzer dagger algebra). More generally the direct limit of `Γ(V, O_V)` over strict neighbourhoods `V` of `]X[` is a dagger algebra of MW type with reduction `A_0`.

*Hypotheses.* The frame `(X, Y, P)` has `P` smooth near `X` but possibly singular along `Y ∖ X` (Berthelot 2.3 remark).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Writing `𝔛̄` for the projective closure of `𝔛`, identify `]Y[_P=P_K` with `𝔛̄_K^an` and `]Z[_λ` with the complement of the ball of radius 1/`λ` by an exercise in projective coordinates (Berthelot 2.1).
2. `Γ(U_λ, O)` is the ring of functions on the affinoid `𝔛_K^an ∩ B(0, 1/λ)`; their union is `A† ⊗ K` by the definition of weak completion (AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.5, weak completions, and §F1.3, radius-indexed presentations; Kedlaya, Finiteness, §2.2 and Remark 4.2.5).
3. The identity `Γ = A† ⊗ K` is Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.2.4), p. 50; the module-level statement (coherent `j†O`-modules and overconvergent isocrystals on the Monsky–Washnitzer frame are determined by their global sections over `A†_K`) is [§RD.3.29](#rd-3-29), proved in (2.5.2) without Theorem `B` for the frame.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide à supports propres, première partie*, §2.1.2, pp. 49–50, especially (2.1.2.4); Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Remark 4.2.5, p. 26.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) *Berthelot's functor `j†` of overconvergent sections*; [§RD.3.7](#rd-3-7) *Exactness of `j†` on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of `j_{λ*}`*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *The module of (universally finite) differentials `Ω^1_A` of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivative*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product `A_1 ⊗†_B A_2`*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *Rational localisation `A⟨f/g⟩†` of a dagger algebra and its universal property*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*.

**Checks.**

- For every prime `p`, `PowerSeries.mk (fun n => p^⌊√n⌋)` satisfies `PowerSeries.IsRestricted 1`, but satisfies `PowerSeries.IsRestricted ρ` for no `ρ > 1`; thus closed-disc convergence does not imply overconvergence.

- For `A=ℤ_p[t,u]/((pt−1)u−1)`, the projective lift `(pT−Z)U−Z²=0` has special fibre `Y=V(Z(U+Z))`. The closure of `X≅𝔸¹_k` is only `V(U+Z)`. The point `[p+1:1:p]` reduces outside that line. Under `r↦[r+p:r²:pr]` its tube is `|r|<1`, which has no finite subcover from `|r|≤|p|^(1/n)`. Using all of `Y` gives the proper, quasi-compact tube `P_K`.

- `X = A^1_k, A = O[t]: Γ`(`]P^1[, j†O`) `= K⟨t⟩†` ([§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) test).
- `X = G_m: A† ⊗ K = K⟨t, t^{-1}⟩†`, the functions overconverging near `|t| = 1` on both sides.
- For `𝔛=𝔸¹_O`, the whole projective tube is `ℙ¹_K^an`, whereas `U_λ` is the bounded disc inside `𝔸¹_K^an`; the affine analytification omits infinity.

### RD.3.9 Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a `k`-scheme of finite type, `i: X → P` and `i′: X → P′` immersions into formal `O`-schemes of finite type, and `u: P′ → P` a morphism with `u∘i′ = i` which is étale on a neighbourhood of `i′(X)`. Then `u_K` restricts to an isomorphism of rigid spaces `]X[_{P′} → ]X[_P`. Moreover, for every closed tube radius `λ ∈ |K^×|^ℚ` with `λ < 1` sufficiently close to 1, `u_K` restricts to an isomorphism of the closed tubes `[X]_{P′,λ} → [X]_{P,λ}`.

*Hypotheses.*

- `X` need not be smooth; `P` and `P′` need not be smooth; only étaleness of `u` near `X` is used.
- The tube depends only on an open formal subscheme containing `X`, so `P` and `P′` may be shrunk to opens containing `X`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Replace `P` and `P′` by opens containing `X` so that `X` is closed in both, `u` is étale and `P′ ×_P X → X` is an isomorphism (an étale map with a section is an open immersion near the section). Since tubes are local on `P` (the generic fibres of an affine covering form an admissible covering), assume `P = Spf A` and `P′ = Spf A′` affine (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.1), p. 39).
2. Let `f_1`, …, `f_r ∈ A` lift equations of `X` modulo the maximal ideal of `O` and `a ∈ m_K` nonzero. The closed tube of radius `λ = |`a`|^{1/n}` is the affinoid with algebra A`{T}/(f_i^n − aT_i) ⊗ K`, and the same presentation with `A′` describes `[X]_{P′,λ}` (Berthelot (1.1.9)). It therefore suffices that `A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) → A′[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i)` is an isomorphism for all `m, n`.
3. The ideal generated by the `f_i` in `A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i)` is nilpotent; `A′[T]` is étale over `A[T]` and the two rings agree modulo that nilpotent ideal `((A/I)[T] ≅ (A′/IA′)[T])`. An étale algebra which becomes an isomorphism modulo a nilpotent ideal is an isomorphism (formal étaleness), so each map is an isomorphism; passing to the limit over `m` gives the closed-tube statement, and the open tube is the admissible union of the closed tubes as `λ → 1`.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (1.3.1) Proposition and its proof, pp. 39–40.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.2](#rd-3-2) *The tube `]T[_P` of a locally closed subscheme*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; Mathlib `Algebra.FormallyEtale`.

**Checks.**

- Square root near 1: for `p` odd, `P = P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩` with `u(t) = t²` and `X = {t = 1}: u` is étale and `u_K` maps the residue disc `{|t − 1| < 1}` isomorphically onto `{|s − 1| < 1}`, the inverse being the binomial series of `(1 + (s − 1))^{1/2}`, whose coefficients are p-integral.
- Non-example: for the projection `P × Spf O⟨x⟩ → P` with `X` embedded by the zero section, `u` is smooth but not étale, and the tube of `X` upstairs is the product of `]X[_P` with an open unit disc, not isomorphic to `]X[_P`.
- With `P′ = P` and `u` the identity the statement is the identity of `]X[_P` (degenerate case).

<a id="rd-3-10"></a>

### RD.3.10 Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a `k`-scheme, `i : X ↪ P` and `i' : X ↪ P'` immersions into formal `O`-schemes and `u : P' → P` a morphism smooth in a neighbourhood of `X` with `u∘i' = i`, of relative dimension `n` near `X`. Then `u_K : ]X[_{P'} → ]X[_P` is a fibration in open unit polydiscs: there is an affine covering `(P_i)` of `P` and isomorphisms `]X[_{P'} ∩ u_K^{-1}(P_{i,K}) ≅ (]X[_P ∩ P_{i,K}) × D(0,1^-)^n` commuting with the projections. Consequently `Ru_{K*} Ω^•_{]X[_{P'}/]X[_P} ≃ O_{]X[_P}` (Poincaré lemma on open polydiscs and Theorem `B`), which gives Berthelot's Proposition 1.

*Hypotheses.* `u` need only be smooth near `X; P, P'` need not be smooth.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Locally on `P'`, choose `t_1`..`t_n ∈ Γ(P', O)` vanishing on `X` whose differentials form a basis of `Ω_{P'/P}` near `X`; then `P' → P ×_O Â^n_O` is étale near `X` and maps `X` into the zero section.
2. For an étale morphism inducing an isomorphism on `X` the tubes are isomorphic (Hensel/infinitesimal lifting on each residue class); the tube of the zero section of `Â^n` over `P` is `]X[_P × D(0,1^-)^n`.
3. Proved in Berthelot 96-03, Théorème (1.3.2), p. 40 (and the remark after it for closed tubes of radius `λ → 1`): assume `X` closed in `P` and `P′, P′` smooth over `P`, and the conormal sheaf of `X` in `P′ ×_P X` free on an affine covering; sections `t_1`, …, `t_n` lifting a regular sequence of generators give an étale map from `P′` to the relative formal affine space `P × Â^n` near `X`, sending `X` to the zero section; by [§RD.3.9](#rd-3-9) the tube of `X` in `P′` is the tube of the zero section, which is `]X[_P × D(0, 1^−)^n`. The Poincaré-lemma consequence follows as there.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (1.4) Lemme 1, p. 13, and Introduction, p. 8.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.2](#rd-3-2) *The tube `]T[_P` of a locally closed subscheme*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.2 *Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the `M̃`*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.4 *Kiehl's Theorem `B` on quasi-Stein spaces*; [§RD.3.9](#rd-3-9) *Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes*.

**Checks.**

- `X = a` point `x ∈ A^1_k, P = Â^1_O, P' = Â^2_O → P` the first projection: `]x[_{P'} = ]x[_P × D(0,1^-)` (a residue polydisc).

### RD.3.11 Étale morphisms proper over the closure of `X` induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods

**Theorem.** Let `X ⊆ Y` be an open immersion of `k`-schemes of finite type, `i: Y → P` and `i′: Y′ → P′` closed immersions into formal `O`-schemes of finite type, `v: Y′ → Y` and `u: P′ → P` morphisms with `u∘i′ = i∘v` and `v` restricting to the identity on `X ⊆ Y′` (`X` open in `Y′`). Let `X̄` be the closure of `X` in `P′ ×_P Y`. If `u` is étale on a neighbourhood of `X` and the restriction of `v` to `X̄` is proper, then `u_K` induces an isomorphism from a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_{P′}` in `]Y′[_{P′}` onto a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_P` in `]Y[_P`.

*Hypotheses.*

- Properness of `v` on the closure of `X` is essential: it is used to show that the closure of the relevant analytic domain is finite over `P_K`.
- The étaleness of `u` is required only near `X; P` and `P′` may be singular along `Y ∖ X` and `Y′ ∖ X`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Reduce to `v` proper with `v^{-1}(X) = X` by replacing `Y′` with `X̄` ([§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) (d)); localise on a finite affine covering of `P`, and on a finite covering of `X`, so that `P = Spf A, X = D(g) ∩ Y`, and the standard neighbourhoods are built from `U_η = {|g| ≥ η}`; after the base change `P_1 = Spf A{T}/(f_i^q − aT_i)` one may assume `[Y]_λ = P_K` (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.5), pp. 42–43).
2. Write `P′ ×_P Y = Y′ ∪ D`; only the restriction over `X` is disjoint, since `X` is open and closed in `P′ ×_P X` (`u` étale with a section over `X`). Choose `μ < 1` with `P′_K ∖ ]Y′[ ⊆ [D]_μ` and then `λ_0 < 1` with `P′_K ∖ ]D[_μ ⊆ [Y′]_{λ_0}`; by the maximum principle, for each `λ ≥ λ_0` there is `η < 1` with `[Y′]_λ ∩ [D]_μ ∩ U′_η = ∅`, so `T_K = [Y′]_λ ∩ U′_η` is open and closed, hence a closed analytic subspace of `U′_η`.
3. By the Jacobian criterion the non-smooth and non-étale loci of `T_K → P_K` are closed analytic subsets missing `]X[_{P′}` (where [§RD.3.9](#rd-3-9) applies), so after enlarging `η` the map `T_K → U_η` is étale; after one more base change `T_K` is closed in `P′_K`, its schematic closure `T` in `P′` has special fibre inside `Y′`, hence is proper over `P` because `v` is proper.
4. By the comparison of formal and rigid properness `T_K → P_K` is proper, hence finite since it is étale (quasi-finite and proper implies finite), given by a coherent `O_{P_K}`-algebra `𝓇`. The map `O_{P_K} → 𝓇` is an isomorphism over `]X[_P`, and its kernel and cokernel are supported on closed analytic subsets missing `]X[_P`, so it is an isomorphism over `U_η` for `η` close to 1; thus `T_K ∩ U′_η → U_η` is an isomorphism, which gives the required strict neighbourhoods.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (1.3.4)–(1.3.5) Théorème and its proof, pp. 41–44; Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, *Cohomological descent of rigid cohomology for étale coverings*, 2.10.2 Proposition, p. 85.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.9](#rd-3-9) *Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; AdicSpacesPartII §R0.9 *Maximum modulus principle for K-affinoid algebras*; AdicSpacesPartII §R0.16 *Jacobian criterion for closed subspaces of smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(ii))*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.6 *Separatedness, properness and partial properness of a formal model versus its generic fibre (Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.18)*; AdicSpacesPartII §R0.14 *Quasi-finite and proper equals finite (Huber 1.5.5)*; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

**Checks.**

- For the identity formal morphism the Jacobian matrix in the normal directions is empty and its determinant is 1; the tube comparison reduces to the identity.

- Degenerate case: `Y′ = Y` and `u = id` give the identity on any strict neighbourhood.
- Open immersion: if `u` is the inclusion of an open formal subscheme `P′ ⊆ P` containing `Y` and `Y′ = Y`, the strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[_{P′}` and in `]Y[_P` coincide.
- Non-example showing properness is needed: `P = Spf O⟨t⟩, Y = A^1_k, X = G_m = Y ∖ {0}, P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩` the open formal subscheme over `X, Y′ = X` and `v` the inclusion, which is not proper. Then `]Y′[_{P′} = {|t| = 1} = ]X[_P`, which is not a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_P` in the closed unit disc `]Y[_P`, because the covering of the closed disc by the annulus `|t| = 1` and the open disc `|t| < 1` is not admissible.
- For the identity map with `Y=A¹` and `X=G_m`, the union `Y∪{0}=Y` is valid; `Y⊔{0}` is not `Y`. Disjointness applies after restriction over `X`.

<a id="rd-3-12"></a>

### RD.3.12 Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms

**Theorem.** Let `(X,Y,P)` and `(X,Y′,P′)` be frames, with a smooth formal map `u:P′→P` near `X` and a map `v:Y′→Y` identical on `X`. Require `v` restricted to the closure of `X` in `P′×_P Y` to be proper. Choose sections `t₁`,…,`t_d` of the ideal of `Y′` in `P′` whose classes form a basis over `X` of the relative conormal sheaf. The coordinate morphism `ψ:P′→P×Â^d` is étale near `X` and induces an isomorphism between cofinal strict-neighbourhood systems. A cofinal system has the form `⋃_n(([Y]_(λ_n)∩U_(η_n))×D(0,λ_n⁺)^d)`, with `λ_n,η_n` increasing to one. Over the tube `]X[_P` the fibre is the open unit polydisc; this is not a fixed open-disc product over every point of a strict neighbourhood. The resulting pullback gives the overconvergent de Rham and coefficient comparisons.

*Hypotheses.* The proper-closure, smoothness and relative conormal-coordinate hypotheses above are required; localise on `X` to obtain the coordinates.

*Proof sketch.* Proved in Berthelot 96-03, Théorème (1.3.7) with (1.3.4)–(1.3.5), pp. 41–45. The properness hypothesis is that `v` restricted to the closure `X̄` of `X` in `P′ ×_P Y` is proper (for instance `v` proper); the local hypothesis is that sections `t_1`, …, `t_d` of the ideal of `Y′` in `P′` induce a basis, over `X`, of the conormal sheaf of `Y′` in `P′ ×_P Y` (Berthelot asks for the basis over `X` only; the properness condition is the one on `X̄`), which holds locally by (1.3.8)`(i)` when `P, P′` are affine, `Z = Y ∩ V(g)` and the conormal sheaf is free. Then the `P`-morphism `ψ: P′ → P × Â^d` defined by the `t_i` is étale near `X`, and [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) applied to `ψ` gives the isomorphism of strict neighbourhoods; (1.3.8)(ii) identifies a strict neighbourhood upstairs with `⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n}) × D(0, λ_n^+)^d` over the standard neighbourhood `V_{λ,η} = ⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n})`: a union of products whose polydisc radius `λ_n` tends to 1. Over a point of the tube `]X[_P` the fibre is the open polydisc `D(0, 1^−)^d`, but over a point of `V_{λ,η}` outside the tube it is a closed polydisc of radius `< 1`; the isomorphism "`V′ ≅ V × D(0,1^−)^n` over `V`" is to be read in this sense, which is what Berthelot proves and what its consequences (sections over strict neighbourhoods, the cohomology and isocrystal comparisons) use. (Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (2.3), p. 18, and (2.3) Théorème 1, p. 18; Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres, première partie*, Théorème 1.3.7 and Remarque 1.3.8, global pp. 44–45 (`I`, pp. 20–21).)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10) *Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*; [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) *Étale morphisms proper over the closure of `X` induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*.

**Checks.**

- For a formal projection with zero section, the cofinal neighbourhood is a union of products with closed-polydisc radii tending to one. At a point of `]X[` its fibre is the open unit polydisc; at a boundary point the radius can be strictly less than one.

<a id="rd-3-13"></a>

### RD.3.13 Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame

**Definition.** Let `(X, Y, P)` be a frame, `p_1, p_2 : ]Y[_{P×P} → ]Y[_P` the projections (`Y` embedded diagonally) and `j†` the functors on `]Y[_{P^m}`. An isocrystal on `X` overconvergent along `Z = Y ∖ X` (relative to `K`, realised on `P`) is a `j†O_{]Y[_P}`-module `E`, locally free of finite rank, with an isomorphism `ε : p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E` of `j†O_{]Y[_{P²}}`-modules satisfying the usual cocycle condition on `]Y[_{P³}` (and `ε` restricting to the identity on the diagonal). Morphisms are `j†O`-linear maps compatible with `ε`. Equivalently ([§RD.3.18](#rd-3-18)) it is a locally free module `M` with integrable connection `∇` on some strict neighbourhood `V` of `]X[_P` in `]Y[_P` whose Taylor series is induced by an analytic isomorphism `p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M` on a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_{P²}` in `]Y[_{P²}`, two such data being identified when they agree on a smaller strict neighbourhood. The category is denoted `Isoc(X, Y, P/K)` (`Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K)` after [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21)).

*Hypotheses.*

- The convergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism is real extra data without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12); with a Frobenius structure it is automatic (Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.5.7, quoted by Kedlaya).
- Coherent `j†O`-modules with such a stratification are automatically locally free (a coherent module with a connection on a smooth rigid space is locally free, Kedlaya Notes Remark 2.3; Kedlaya Finiteness Lemma 3.3.4 for dagger algebras).

The API:

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal`: `(E, ε)`: locally free `j†O_{]Y[_P}`-module with overconvergent stratification `ε : p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E` satisfying the cocycle condition.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.connection`: The integrable connection `∇` induced by `ε` on a strict neighbourhood.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.taylorIso`: The Taylor isomorphism `p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M` on a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_{P²}`.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.Hom`: Morphisms: germs of horizontal maps on strict neighbourhoods.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.tensor`: Tensor products, duals, internal Hom; the category is abelian, K-linear, rigid monoidal.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.unit`: The unit object `j†O_{]Y[}` with the canonical stratification.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.restrictStrictNbhd`: Restriction from `V` to a smaller strict neighbourhood `V'` is an isomorphism in the category.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback`: Pullback along morphisms of frames ([§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19)), with `id^* = id` and (uu')`^* ≅ u'^*u^*`.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.isLocallyFree_of_coherent`: A coherent `j†O`-module with overconvergent stratification is locally free.

*Proof sketch.* Well-defined as a category: the cocycle condition is the usual one for stratifications; morphisms are germs on strict neighbourhoods ([§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) intersections). Local freeness of coherent `j†O`-modules with connection is Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.3)(ii); uniqueness of `ε` and the cocycle condition are (2.2.7)`(i)` ([§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16)). The automatic convergence with Frobenius is Théorème (2.5.7) of the 96-03 preprint, cited by Kedlaya as [Be4]; it is [§RD.3.31](#rd-3-31) (affine case). (Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.1), p. 27; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Definition 2.4, p. 3.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) *Berthelot's functor `j†` of overconvergent sections*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.2 *Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the `M̃`*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.4 *Kiehl's Theorem `B` on quasi-Stein spaces*.

**Checks.**

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.dwork_taylor`: For `L_π` on `(A^1, P^1, P̂^1)`, the Taylor isomorphism of the section 1 is `exp π(t' − t)`, which converges on `{|t − t'| < 1}`, a strict neighbourhood of `]A^1[` in `]P^1[_{P̂^1×P̂^1}` (Berthelot 4.2.3 `b`).
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.unit_proper`: If `X = Y (Z = ∅)`, overconvergent isocrystals are convergent isocrystals on `X` realised on `]X[_P` (Berthelot 4.2.2: the category depends only on `X`).
- For `X = Y = Spec 𝔽_p` embedded as 0 in `Spf ℤ_p⟨t⟩, ]X[` is `|t| < 1`, whereas the generic fibre is `|t| ≤ 1; t = 1` lies only in the latter. Equality with the generic fibre requires `X` to be the entire special fibre.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.restriction_iso`: Two data on strict neighbourhoods `V ⊇ V'` agreeing on `V'` define the same object.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.convergent_not_overconvergent`: On `(A^1, P^1, P̂^1)`, the rank two module with `∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ Σ_k p^k t^{p^k − 1} dt` on the closed disc is a convergent isocrystal (even with Frobenius `F e_2 = e_2 − t e_1` for `t ↦ t^p`) but is not isomorphic to the restriction of any overconvergent isocrystal ([§RD.5.10](#rd-5-10)).
- The constant object `j†O` with `ε =` canonical identification; the Dwork isocrystal `L_π` on `(A^1, P^1, P̂^1)` (Berthelot 4.2.3): `M = O_V` with `∇(1) = π dt`, Taylor isomorphism `ε(1) = exp π(t' − t)`, converging on the diagonal tube `{|t − t'| < 1}`.

<a id="rd-3-14"></a>

### RD.3.14 Coherent `j†O`-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods

**Theorem.** In the setting of [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4): (a) `j†O_{]Y[}` is a coherent sheaf of rings, and coherent `j†O_{]Y[}`-modules form an abelian subcategory of all `j†O_{]Y[}`-modules stable under ⊗ and internal Hom. (b) Every coherent `j†O_{]Y[}`-module is isomorphic to `j†𝓮` for a coherent `O_V`-module `𝓮` on some strict neighbourhood `V`, and for coherent `𝓮, 𝓯` on `V, Hom(j†𝓮, j†𝓯) = colim_{V′ ⊆ V} Hom_{O_{V′}}(𝓮|_{V′}, 𝓯|_{V′})`; thus the category of coherent `j†O`-modules is the 2-colimit over strict neighbourhoods of the categories of coherent modules, and `E` is locally free of finite rank if and only if it is `j†𝓮` for a locally free `𝓮`. (c) The restriction functor from coherent `j†O_{]Y[}`-modules to coherent `O_{]X[}`-modules is exact and faithful.

*Hypotheses.* The 2-colimit in (b) is over the filtered set of strict neighbourhoods; two coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods define the same germ if they become isomorphic on a smaller strict neighbourhood.

*Proof sketch.*

1. (a): finite generation of kernels of maps `(j†O)^n → j†O` is checked on an admissible affinoid covering; on `W ∩ ]Z[` the kernel vanishes and on `W ∩ V` it is `j†` of the kernel of a map of coherent `O`-modules, by exactness of `j†` ([§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) (a)) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.9), p. 56).
2. (b): first, for each `λ < 1`, find `η` and coherent models on `V_λ = U_η ∩ [Y]_λ`, using that `[Y]_λ` is quasi-compact and that on affinoids with finite presentations the statement reduces to `E = j†O` (formula (2.1.1.5)); then build compatible models on `⋃_{n' ≤ n} V_{n'}` by induction along sequences `λ_n, η_n → 1` and glue on the standard strict neighbourhood `V_{λ,η}`, which the `V_n` cover admissibly; the Hom statement is proved the same way ((2.1.10), pp. 56–57, and the remark after it).
3. (c): a morphism `f = j†(g)` vanishing on `]X[` has image supported on a closed analytic subset missing `]X[`, which a smaller strict neighbourhood avoids ((2.1.11), p. 57); exactness is that of restriction to an open.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.1.9)–(2.1.11) with the remark after (2.1.10), pp. 56–57; Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, *Cohomological descent of rigid cohomology for étale coverings*, 2.9.1 Lemma, p. 84.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) *Berthelot's functor `j†` of overconvergent sections*; [§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) *`j†` is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on `X`*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.2 *Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the `M̃`*.

**Checks.**

- Affine space: the coherent `j†O`-modules on `P^n_K` for `X = A^n_k` correspond to finitely generated `K⟨t⟩†`-modules (Berthelot (2.5.2)`(i)` with `A = O[t]`).
- Faithful but not full: on the frame `(A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1)`, the injection `K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩` is the restriction functor on global sections of the free rank-one module; the element `Σ p^{⌊√n⌋} t^n` of `K⟨t⟩` shows `Hom(j†O, j†O) = K⟨t⟩†` is a proper subspace of `Hom(O_{]X[}, O_{]X[}) = K⟨t⟩`.
- Degenerate case: if `Z = ∅`, coherent `j†O`-modules are coherent `O_{]Y[}`-modules.

<a id="rd-3-15"></a>

### RD.3.15 Coherent `j†O`-modules glue along finite open coverings of `X`

**Theorem.** Let `X = X_1 ∪ … ∪ X_n` be a finite open covering, `j_i: X_i → Y` the inclusions and `j_i†` the corresponding functors on `]Y[_P`. (a) Given coherent (respectively locally free of finite rank) `j_i†O_{]Y[}`-modules `E_i` and isomorphisms `j_{i′}†E_i ≅ j_i†E_{i′}` satisfying the cocycle condition, there is a coherent (respectively locally free) `j†O_{]Y[}`-module `E`, unique up to unique isomorphism, with isomorphisms `j_i†E ≅ E_i` compatible with the given ones. (b) Given coherent `E, F` and maps `φ_i: j_i†E → j_i†F` with `j_{i′}†φ_i = j_i†φ_{i′}`, there is a unique `φ: E → F` with `j_i†φ = φ_i`. Hence `X′ ↦` {coherent `j_{X′}†O_{]Y[}`-modules} is a stack for the Zariski topology on `X` (`Y` and `P` fixed).

*Hypotheses.* The covering is finite; for a general Zariski covering of a quasi-compact `X` refine to a finite one.

*Proof sketch.* By [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) (b) each `E_i` is `j_i†𝓮_i` for a coherent `𝓮_i` on a strict neighbourhood `V_i` of `]X_i[`, and the gluing isomorphisms come from isomorphisms of models on strict neighbourhoods of `]X_i ∩ X_{i′}[` (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.12), p. 58). Shrink the `V_i` to standard neighbourhoods `V^i_{λ,η}` for a common pair of sequences; their union is the standard neighbourhood of `]X[` and they form an admissible covering of it ([§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) (b), (d)); after shrinking once more the isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, so the `𝓮_i` glue to a coherent `𝓮` on `V` and `E = j†𝓮` works; uniqueness and (b) follow from the Hom formula and the Čech sequence of [§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) (d). (Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.1.12) Proposition, p. 58.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) *Coherent `j†O`-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) *`j†` is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on `X`*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*.

**Checks.**

- Covering `G_m ⊂ P^1` by the two opens obtained by removing 1 and `−1` (`p` odd): a locally free module given on each piece and agreeing on the overlap glues to a locally free `j†O`-module.
- Degenerate case `n = 1`: the gluing datum is a single module and `E = E_1`.
- Morphisms: the identity maps on the pieces glue to the identity of `E` (uniqueness in (b)).

<a id="rd-3-16"></a>

### RD.3.16 Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients

**Theorem.** Let `(X, Y, P)` be as in [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) with a morphism `P → S` of formal `O`-schemes smooth on a neighbourhood of `X`, and let `E` be a coherent `j†O_{]Y[}`-module with an integrable connection `∇` relative to `S_K`. (a) `(E, ∇) ≅ j†(𝓮, ∇_0)` for a coherent `O_V`-module `𝓮` with integrable connection on some strict neighbourhood `V`; if `S = Spf O` then `E` is locally free of finite rank. (b) `∇` is overconvergent along `Z = Y ∖ X` — there is an isomorphism `ε: p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E` of `j†O_{]Y[_{P×_S P}}`-modules inducing the Taylor isomorphisms `ε_n` modulo the `(n+1)`-st power of the diagonal ideal for all `n` — if and only if there is an isomorphism `ε′: p_2^*𝓮 ≅ p_1^*𝓮` on a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_{P×P}` in `]Y[_{P×P}` inducing the Taylor isomorphisms of `∇_0`. (c) If `∇` is overconvergent, `ε` is unique, is determined by its restriction to `]X[_{P×P}`, and satisfies the cocycle condition on `]Y[_{P×P×P}`; a `j†O`-linear map `h: E → F` between overconvergent modules is compatible with the `ε` if and only if `h|_{]X[}` is horizontal; a section `s` satisfies `ε(p_2^*s) = p_1^*s` if and only if `s|_{]X[}` is horizontal; coherent sub-`j†O`-modules stable under `∇` and the corresponding quotients are again overconvergent. (d) Overconvergence can be tested on an open covering of `P` and on a finite open covering of `X`. (e) Coherent `j†O`-modules with integrable overconvergent connection form an abelian category with ⊗ and internal Hom, the forgetful functor to coherent `j†O`-modules is exact, the category is a full subcategory of coherent `j†O`-modules with integrable connection, and restriction to `]X[` is an exact faithful functor to coherent `O_{]X[}`-modules with convergent integrable connection.

*Hypotheses.*

- `K` has characteristic 0 (needed for (a) and for the description of connections by divided-power Taylor series).
- `P → S` is smooth only near `X`; by [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) and the Jacobian criterion the smooth locus of `P_K → S_K` is a strict neighbourhood of `]X[`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. (a): apply [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) (b) to `E` and to the Taylor isomorphisms on the first-order neighbourhoods in the double and triple products; local freeness of a coherent module with connection in characteristic 0 is the classical argument (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.3), p. 60).
2. (b): if `ε′` exists, `ε = j′†(ε′)` using that `j†` commutes with the projections and the diagonal ([§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) (b)); conversely write `ε = j′†(ε′)` on a standard strict neighbourhood and show that `ε′` induces the Taylor isomorphisms after shrinking: the kernel of restriction to `]X[` of sections of `𝓮` has support a closed analytic subset missing `]X[`, avoided by `U_η` for `η` near 1 ((2.2.6), pp. 61–62).
3. (c): by faithfulness of restriction to the tube ([§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) (c)) reduce to `Y = X`; cover the closed tubes `[X]_{P²,λ}` by products `W × D(0, λ^+)^m` (weak fibration theorem, [§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10)), and use injectivity of `M ⊗_A` A`{τ} → M ⊗_A` `A[[τ]]` to see that `ε` is determined by its Taylor expansion; subobjects use flatness of the projections on the smooth locus, a strict neighbourhood ((2.2.1), pp. 58–59; (2.2.7), pp. 62–63).
4. (d): `ε's` obtained on an open covering of `P` glue by uniqueness ((2.2.8), p. 63); for a finite covering of `X` apply [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) (b) to the maps `p_2^*E → p_1^*E` ((2.2.11), pp. 63–64). (e) follows from (c), [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) (a) and (c) ((2.2.9), (2.2.10), p. 63).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.2.1)–(2.2.11) with the remark after (2.2.11), pp. 58–64.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10) *Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations*; [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) *Coherent `j†O`-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) *Coherent `j†O`-modules glue along finite open coverings of `X`*; [§RD.3.6](#rd-3-6) *`j†` is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on `X`*; AdicSpacesPartII §R0.9 *Maximum modulus principle for K-affinoid algebras*; AdicSpacesPartII §R0.16 *Jacobian criterion for closed subspaces of smooth spaces (Huber 1.6.9(ii))*; CrystallineCohomology §CR.1.3 *Modules with integrable connection and their de Rham complexes*.

**Checks.**

- For the zero connection on a line, the Taylor transition is the identity on every product tube, so it satisfies the same coordinate criterion in every smooth chart.

- Dwork: on `(A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_O)` with `K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p`, the module `j†O` with `∇(1) = −π dt` is overconvergent: its Taylor isomorphism is multiplication by `exp(−π(t′ − t))`, analytic on the strict neighbourhood `|t′ − t| < 1` of the diagonal tube (Berthelot (2.2.15)(ii)(a), (1.2.4)(iv)).
- Non-example: `j†O` with `∇(1) = −dt` on the same frame is not overconvergent, not even convergent: its Taylor series `exp(−(t′ − t))` converges only for `|t′ − t| < p^{−1/(p−1)} < 1`.
- Subobjects: the image of a horizontal map between overconvergent modules is overconvergent by (c), so the category is abelian.

<a id="rd-3-17"></a>

### RD.3.17 The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection

**Theorem.** Assume `P` and `S` affine, `Z = Y ∩ V(g)` for one `g ∈ Γ(P, O_P)`, and `t_1`, …, `t_m ∈ Γ(P, O_P)` such that `dt_1`, …, `dt_m` is a basis of `Ω^1_{P/S}` near `X`; on a strict neighbourhood of `]X[` these give a basis of `Ω^1_{P_K/S_K}` with dual derivations `∂_1`, …, `∂_m`. Let `(𝓮, ∇_0)` be a coherent module with integrable connection on a strict neighbourhood `V` and `(E, ∇) = j†(𝓮, ∇_0)`; write `∂^{[k]} = ∂^k / k!` for multi-indices `k`, and `U_η = {x ∈ P_K : |g(x)| ≥ η}`. Then `∇` is overconvergent if and only if for every `λ < 1` in `|K^×|^ℚ` there is `η < 1` in `|K^×|^ℚ` with `[Y]_λ ∩ U_η ⊆ V` such that `‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0` as `|k| → ∞` for every `e ∈ Γ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η, 𝓮)`, for a (any) Banach norm on this finite module over an affinoid algebra. When `Z = ∅` (`X` closed in `P`), a connection on a coherent `O_{]X[}`-module is convergent if and only if `‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0` for every `λ < 1` and every `e ∈ Γ([X]_λ, 𝓮)`.

*Hypotheses.*

- Divided powers `∂^k/k!` need characteristic 0.
- The criterion is coordinate-dependent in form but the conclusion is not; any other étale coordinates give the same answer (Guo–Reinecke, Remark 2.13).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Necessity: by [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (b), `ε = j′†(ε′)` on a strict neighbourhood `V′ ⊇ V_{λη} := [Y]_{P²,λ} ∩ p_1^{-1}(U_η)`; on `[Y]_{P²,λ}` the conditions `|1 ⊗ g| ≥ η` and `|g ⊗ 1| ≥ η` agree for `η > λ`. By Berthelot's remark (1.3.8)(ii) (strong fibration theorem applied to `p_1`), `V_{λη} ≅ ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η) × D(0, λ^+)^m` with coordinates `τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1` (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.13), pp. 64–65).
2. Expanding `θ(e) = ε′(p_2^*e) = Σ_k θ_k(e) ⊗ τ^k` with `‖θ_k(e)‖ λ^{|k|} → 0` (Lemma (2.2.12): finite modules over A`{τ}` expand uniquely in `τ`-series), compatibility of `ε′` with the Taylor isomorphisms modulo the powers of the diagonal forces `θ_k(e) = ∂^{[k]} e` ((2.2.4.1)).
3. Sufficiency: for a sequence `λ_i → 1` and corresponding `η_i`, define `θ(e) = Σ_k ∂^{[k]} e ⊗ τ^k` on `V_{λ_i η_i}`; it is semilinear, so gives a linear map `p_2^*𝓮 → p_1^*𝓮` inducing the Taylor isomorphisms, with inverse `Σ_k (−1)^{|k|} τ^k ⊗ ∂^{[k]} e`; these glue by the uniqueness argument of [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (c) to an isomorphism on the standard strict neighbourhood `V_{λ,η}` ((2.2.13)(ii), p. 66). The case `Z = ∅` is (2.2.14).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.2.12)–(2.2.14) and Exemples (2.2.15), pp. 64–67; Guo–Reinecke, *A prismatic approach to crystalline local systems*, Definition 2.12 and Remark 2.13, p. 15.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.12](#rd-3-12) *Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.2 *Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the `M̃`*.

**Checks.**

- Dwork: for `∇(1) = −π dt` on `A^1 ⊂ P^1 (K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p)`, on the chart `Spf O⟨t⟩`, where `Z` is empty, `∂^{[k]}1 = (−π)^k/k!` has absolute value `p^{−s_p(k)/(p−1)} ≤ 1` (`s_p` the digit sum), so the connection is convergent there. Overconvergence along `∞` is checked on the chart `Spf O⟨s⟩, s = 1/t`, with `g = s` and `U_η ∩ [Y]_λ = {η ≤ |s| ≤ 1}`: there `∇(1) = π s^{−2}` ds, the Taylor series of 1 is `exp(π τ/(s(s + τ)))` with `τ = s′ − s`, and expanding `π τ/(s(s + τ)) = (π/s²) Σ_{j≥0} (−1)^j τ^{j+1}/s^j` and using `|π^n/n!| ≤ 1` gives `‖∂_s^{[k]}`1`‖ ≤ η^{−2k}` on that annulus; so `‖∂_s^{[k]}`1`‖ λ^k → 0` once `η² > λ`, and the connection is overconvergent. Computing only on the chart at 0, where `Z` is empty, would test convergence and not overconvergence.
- Kummer: for `∇(1) = a dt/t` on `G_m ⊂ P^1` with `a ∈ ℤ_p, ∂^{[k]}1 = binom(a, k) t^{−k}` with `|binom(a, k)| ≤ 1`, so on `{η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η}` the norms are `≤ η^{−k}` and `λ^k η^{−k} → 0` for `η > λ`: overconvergent.
- Non-examples: for `∇(1) = −dt, ‖∂^{[k]}1‖ = |1/k!| = p^{v_p(k!)}` and `λ^k p^{v_p(k!)} → ∞` for `λ > p^{−1/(p−1)}`; for `a = 1/p` in the Kummer example `|binom(1/p, k)| = p^{k + v_p(k!)}` is unbounded, so neither is even convergent.

<a id="rd-3-18"></a>

### RD.3.18 Stratifications versus connections with overconvergent Taylor series

**Lemma.** For a frame `(X, Y, P)`, the functor `(E, ε) ↦ (E|_V, ∇)` is an equivalence between overconvergent isocrystals in the stratification form ([§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13)) and locally free modules with integrable connection on strict neighbourhoods `V` of `]X[_P` in `]Y[_P` whose formal Taylor isomorphism `ε(1 ⊗ m) = Σ_q (1/q!) ∇(D)^q(m) ⊗ τ^q` (`τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1` for local coordinates `t_i` on `P` near `X`) is induced by an analytic isomorphism `p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M` on a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_{P²}` in `]Y[_{P²}`.

*Hypotheses.* `P` smooth near `X` with local coordinates `t_1`..`t_n`; the projection `]X[_{P²} → ]X[_P` is locally a fibration in open unit polydiscs, and the diagonal closed immersion `]X[_P → ]X[_{P²}` is its centre section ([§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10)).

*Proof sketch.*

1. `ε ↦ ∇`: restrict `ε` to the first-order infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal (Berthelot 4.1).
2. `∇ ↦ ε`: the Taylor series defines `ε` on the formal completion of the diagonal; the convergence hypothesis says it is induced by an analytic isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood; the cocycle condition holds formally, hence analytically since the tube of the diagonal is a polydisc fibration over `]X[` ([§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10)) and analytic functions on open polydiscs are determined by their Taylor expansion along the centre section (Berthelot 4.1, 4.2.1).
3. Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.6) (overconvergence via an isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube) and (2.2.13) (the coordinate criterion) prove this lemma; see [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (b) and [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.1), p. 27, and (4.1), p. 25.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.10](#rd-3-10) *Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17) *The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection*.

**Checks.**

- Dwork: `∇(1) = π dt` gives `Σ_q (1/q!) π^q (t' − t)^q = exp π(t' − t)` (Berthelot 4.2.3).
- For `X=𝔸¹_k` and `P=Spf O⟨t⟩`, the diagonal section has `t₂−t₁=0`; the projection has open-disc coordinate `t₂−t₁`.
- The trivial connection has the identity Taylor isomorphism and satisfies the cocycle condition on the triple product.

<a id="rd-3-19"></a>

### RD.3.19 Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames

**Construction.** For a morphism of frames `(w, v, u) : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P)` the pullback `u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X', Y', P'/K)` sends `(E, ε)` to `(j'†u_K^* E, (u×u)^*ε)`, using that `u_K` maps strict neighbourhoods of `]X'[` into strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` ([§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3)); in connection form it is the usual pullback of modules with connection. It is compatible with composition up to canonical isomorphism, with ⊗ and duals, and (for Frobenius structures) with Frobenius pullbacks.

*Hypotheses.* The functor depends on `(w, v, u)`; [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) shows that for fixed `(w, v)` it is independent of `u` up to canonical isomorphism.

The API:

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullbackFunctor`: `u^*` for a morphism of frames.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_id`: `id^* ≅` id.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_comp`: `(u∘u')^* ≅ u'^* ∘ u^*` canonically, satisfying the associativity coherence.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_tensor`: `u^*(E ⊗ F) ≅ u^*E ⊗ u^*F; u^*` preserves duals and the unit.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_connection`: In connection form `u^*` is the pullback of modules with connection on strict neighbourhoods.

*Proof sketch.* Pullback of stratifications along `u × u : ]Y'[_{P'²} → ]Y[_{P²}`; strictness of neighbourhoods by [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) (pullback API); locally free modules pull back to locally free modules. (Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.1), p. 27.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) *Berthelot's functor `j†` of overconvergent sections*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*.

**Checks.**

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_unit`: `u^*(j†O_{]Y[_P}) ≅ j'†O_{]Y'[_{P'}}`.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_dwork`: For the Frobenius lift `t ↦ t^p` of `P̂^1`, the pullback of `L_π` has `∇(1) = πp t^{p−1} dt` (Berthelot 4.2.3 `c`).
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_comp_test`: For composable frame morphisms the canonical isomorphism (uu')`^* ≅ u'^*u^*` is the identity on underlying modules with connection.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_not_equiv_nonsmooth`: Pullback along the frame morphism ({0}, {0}, `Spf O`) `→ (A^1, P^1, P̂^1)`, which is not smooth, is not an equivalence: `L_π` and the unit object both pull back to the unit object on the point, but `L_π` ≇ `O` since its only candidate horizontal sections `c·exp(−πt)` converge only on `|t| < 1`, not on a strict neighbourhood.
- Pullback along the identity is the identity; pullback of the unit object is the unit object.

<a id="rd-3-20"></a>

### RD.3.20 Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction

**Lemma.** Let `f, g : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P)` be two morphisms of frames inducing the same morphisms `X' → X` and `Y' → Y`. For an overconvergent isocrystal `(E, ε)` on `(X, Y, P)`, the pullback of `ε` along `(f, g) : ]Y'[_{P'} → ]Y[_{P×P}` defines an isomorphism `χ_{f,g} : g^*E ≅ f^*E` of overconvergent isocrystals; `χ_{f,f} = id` and `χ_{f,g}∘χ_{g,h} = χ_{f,h}`.

*Hypotheses.* `(f, g)` maps `X'` into the diagonal image of `X`, hence `]X'[_{P'}` into `]X[_{P×P}`, and strict neighbourhoods into strict neighbourhoods ([§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3)).

*Proof sketch.* Pull back the stratification along `(f, g)`; the cocycle identity for `ε` on `]Y[_{P³}` pulled back along `(f, g, h)` gives the transitivity (standard crystal formalism; local analogue: Kedlaya overview Remark 4.1.9 for annuli). Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.17), pp. 67–68: the isomorphism `χ` is `h_K^*(ε)` for `h = (u, u′): P′ → P ×_S P`, horizontal, with the transitivity (2.2.17.3) from the cocycle condition on the triple product; uniqueness of `ε` ([§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (c)) makes it canonical. (Kedlaya, *Local monodromy of p-adic differential equations: an overview*, Remark 4.1.9, p. 17; Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Definition 4.2.3, p. 26.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19) *Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; [§RD.3.2](#rd-3-2) *The tube `]T[_P` of a locally closed subscheme*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*.

**Checks.**

- For `f = g` the isomorphism is the identity; for two Frobenius lifts `f, g` of `P̂^1` inducing `t ↦ t^p` mod `π, χ_{f,g}` on `L_π` is multiplication by `exp π(g(t) − f(t))`.

<a id="rd-3-20a"></a>

### RD.3.`20a` Zariski gluing of local frame coefficients without Frobenius

**Theorem.** For a fixed frame `(X,Y,P)`, coherent `j†O`-modules with integrable overconvergent connection, and their horizontal morphisms, satisfy effective descent for finite Zariski coverings of `X` with `Y` fixed. For frames `(X,X,P)`, coherent modules with convergent connection satisfy the same descent for finite open coverings of `X`. Tensor products, internal Hom and pullbacks of these local coefficients commute with restriction and with gluing. These local equivalences and the uniqueness of morphism gluing give effective descent in the Čech categories of local frames, including when `Y` has no global embedding.

*Hypotheses.* `X` and `Y` are of finite type; the formal embeddings are smooth near `X`. No Frobenius structure is assumed. Transition isomorphisms are horizontal and satisfy the cocycle condition.

*Proof sketch.* Apply [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) to glue coherent modules and their morphisms. Glue the connections and their Taylor isomorphisms on product frames; integrability, the cocycle and overconvergence are local by [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16). For `Y=X`, tubes of the opens give an admissible covering of `]X[`, so the same argument glues convergent connections. On intersections of different embeddings use diagonal product frames and the transitive comparison maps of [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20); refinement gives descent for the resulting Čech categories.

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie*, (2.2.11) and its remark, p. 64; (2.3.3)`(i)`, p. 72.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) *Coherent `j†O`-modules glue along finite open coverings of `X`*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19) *Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames*; [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) *Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction*.

**Checks.**

- The one-open covering gives back the original module with connection.
- On the two standard affine opens of `ℙ¹`, constant coefficients with identity transition glue to the unit convergent coefficient.
- Three rank-one transition scalars whose product on a triple overlap is not 1 fail the cocycle condition and do not glue.

<a id="rd-3-21"></a>

### RD.3.21 Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals

**Theorem.** (a) If `(id_X, id_Y, u) : (X, Y, P') → (X, Y, P)` is a morphism of frames with `u` smooth in a neighbourhood of `X`, then `u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X, Y, P'/K)` is an equivalence of categories. (b) For two frames `(X, Y, P_1), (X, Y, P_2)` with the same `(X, Y)`, the projections from the diagonal frame `(X, Y, P_1 ×_O P_2)` are smooth near `X`, and the composite equivalences `E_{12} := (p_2^*)^{-1}∘p_1^*` are canonical: independent of choices up to unique isomorphism and satisfying `E_{23}∘E_{12} ≅ E_{13}`. Hence `Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) := Isoc(X, Y, P/K)` depends only on `(X ⊂ Y)` up to canonical equivalence, is local on `Y`, and is functorial in `(X ⊂ Y)`. The same holds with Frobenius structures ([§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25)).

*Hypotheses.*

- `P, P_i` smooth near `X`; no hypothesis at the points of `Z` (Berthelot 2.3 remark).
- For `Y` without a global embedding into a formal scheme smooth near `X`, the category is defined by gluing along a Čech covering by frames ([§RD.3.24](#rd-3-24)).

*Proof sketch.*

1. If `u` has a section `s : P → P'` over `(X, Y)`, then `s^*` and `u^*` are quasi-inverse: `s^*u^* =` (us)`^* = id` and `u^*s^* =` (su)`^* ≅ id^*` by [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) (su and `id_{P'}` induce the same maps on `X, Y`).
2. Work with the cofinal neighbourhood systems of [§RD.3.12](#rd-3-12) and the étale auxiliary map `ψ:P′→P×Â^d`. After refinement, [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) compares strict neighbourhoods with those of the product frame. Its zero section and [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) give local quasi-inverses, which glue by [§RD.3.20a](#rd-3-20a). No product with one fixed open unit polydisc over boundary points is asserted (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (2.3.1), pp. 68–69).
3. (b) The diagonal immersion `Y → P_1 × P_2` is a closed immersion and the projections are smooth near `X` since `P_i` are; canonicity and the cocycle from [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) ('méthode `du` plongement diagonal', Berthelot 1.5).
4. The diagonal comparison is Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)`(i)`, p. 69; gluing without a global embedding is [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.1), p. 27; Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Remark 4.2.4, p. 26.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) *Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction*; [§RD.3.12](#rd-3-12) *Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms*; [§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19) *Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*; [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) *Étale morphisms proper over the closure of `X` induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) *Coherent `j†O`-modules glue along finite open coverings of `X`*; [§RD.3.20a](#rd-3-20a) *Zariski gluing of local frame coefficients without Frobenius*.

**Checks.**

- Two embeddings of affine space: `(A^n, P^n, P̂^n)` and `(A^n, P^n, P̂^n ×_O P̂^n)` (diagonal) give canonically equivalent categories; see [§RD.3.42](#rd-3-42) for two different compactifications.
- For `X` smooth affine with lift `A` and two choices of presentation, the equivalence transports the `(σ,∇)`-module over `A† ⊗ K` realised in one presentation to the other by the Taylor isomorphism (Kedlaya Finiteness Remark 4.2.4: 'homotopy equivalences').

- At boundary points the cofinal radii vary. A single open-unit-polydisc product over an entire strict neighbourhood is not a consequence of the strong fibration theorem.

<a id="rd-3-22"></a>

### RD.3.22 Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback

**Construction.** Let `X ⊆ Y` be an open immersion of `k`-schemes of finite type over a formal `O`-scheme `S` of finite type. Choose a finite open covering `(Y_α)` of `Y` and closed immersions `Y_α → P_α` into formal `S`-schemes smooth near `X_α = X ∩ Y_α`; put `Y_{αβ} = Y_α ∩ Y_β` embedded diagonally in `P_{αβ} = P_α ×_S P_β`, with projections `p_{αβ}, q_{αβ}`. The category `Isoc(X, Y/S)` consists of families `(E_α, φ_{αβ})` with `E_α` a coherent `j†O_{]Y_α[}`-module with integrable overconvergent connection and `φ_{αβ}: p_{αβ,K}^* E_α ≅ q_{αβ,K}^* E_β` horizontal isomorphisms on `]Y_{αβ}[_{P_{αβ}}` satisfying the cocycle condition on `]Y_{αβγ}[_{P_α×P_β×P_γ}`; morphisms are compatible families. (a) Up to canonical equivalence it does not depend on the covering or on the `P_α`, and equals `Isoc(X, Y, P/S)` when a global `P` exists. (b) For any immersion of an open `U ⊆ Y` into a formal `S`-scheme `T` (not necessarily smooth), each `E` has a realisation `E_T` on `]U[_T`: locally `E_T = u_K^* E_P` for an `S`-morphism `u: T → P` to a smooth embedding of `U` restricting to the identity on `U`, independent of `P` and `u` up to canonical isomorphism, with canonical horizontal transition isomorphisms `u_K^* E_T ≅ E_{T′}` for `S`-morphisms `u: T′ → T`, satisfying transitivity. (c) For a commutative diagram (`X′ ⊆ Y′` over `S′`) `→` (`X ⊆ Y` over `S`) given by `v: Y′ → Y` over `S′ → S`, there is a pullback functor `v^*: Isoc(X, Y/S) → Isoc(X′, Y′/S′)`, realised by `u_K^*` for any lift `u` of `v` between embeddings, independent of `u` up to canonical isomorphism, with `(v ∘ v′)^* ≅ v′^* ∘ v^*` canonically.

*Hypotheses.*

- Frames exist locally: every affine open of `Y` embeds as a closed subscheme of a formal affine space over `S`, which is smooth.
- In (b) for `O` a discrete valuation ring, `T` may be any formal `S`-scheme in which `U` is defined by an ideal of definition (Berthelot (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph): the lift `u: T → P` is built successively on the thickenings `Spec O_T/𝓲^{i+1}` by formal smoothness of `P`.

The API:

- `IsocDagger.ofGluingData`: An object of `Isoc(X, Y/S)` from overconvergent modules `E_α` on local frames and horizontal transition isomorphisms `φ_{αβ}` satisfying the cocycle condition.
- `IsocDagger.realisation`: The realisation `E_T`, a coherent `j†O_{]U[_T}`-module with integrable connection, for an immersion of an open `U ⊆ Y` into a formal `S`-scheme `T`.
- `IsocDagger.realisation_transition`: For `u: T′ → T` compatible with the immersions, a horizontal isomorphism `u_K^* E_T ≅ E_{T′}`, transitive for composable `u`.
- `IsocDagger.gluing_equivalence`: Changing the covering or the local embeddings gives a canonical equivalence of gluing categories, compatible with realisations.
- `IsocDagger.ofFrame_equivalence`: When a global frame `(X, Y, P)` exists, the gluing category is canonically equivalent to `Isoc(X, Y, P/S)` of [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13).
- `IsocDagger.pullback`: The pullback `v^*` along `v: (X′ ⊆ Y′/S′) → (X ⊆ Y/S)`, realised by `u_K^*` for any lift `u`.
- `IsocDagger.pullback_comp`: Canonical isomorphisms `(v ∘ v′)^* ≅ v′^* ∘ v^*` and `id^* ≅` id, satisfying the usual coherence.
- `IsocDagger.horizontalSections`: The module `Γ((X, Y)/S, E)` of horizontal sections, independent of the realisation used to compute it.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Independence of `P` on a fixed covering: two choices `P_α, P′_α` are compared through the diagonal embedding into `P_α ×_S P′_α` and the equivalences of [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) along the two projections; the transition data match because the canonical isomorphisms of [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) satisfy the transitivity relation (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.17.3), (2.3.2)`(i)`, pp. 67–70).
2. Independence of the covering (left to the reader by Berthelot, (2.3.2)(iii), p. 71): given two coverings with embeddings, pass to the common refinement `Y_α ∩ Y′_β` embedded in `P_α ×_S P′_β`; restriction along the two projections gives equivalences from each gluing category to the refined one, because on each piece they are the equivalences of [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21), and the cocycle data correspond since the Taylor isomorphism of an overconvergent module is unique ([§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (c)) and the comparison isomorphisms are transitive. Refining twice gives the compatibility needed for a canonical equivalence.
3. Realisations: choose locally a closed immersion of `U` into a smooth formal `S`-scheme `P` and lift `U → P` to `u: T → P` by formal smoothness on the nilpotent thickenings; set `E_T = u_K^* E_P`; two choices `(P, u), (P′, u′)` are compared through `P ×_S P′` and [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20), which yields independence and the transition isomorphisms ((2.3.2)(ii), (2.3.2.1), pp. 70–71).
4. Pullback: if `v` extends to `u: P′ → P` use `u_K^*`; otherwise replace `P′` by `P ×_S P′` with the graph embedding, whose projection to `P` extends `v`; canonicity again comes from [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) ((2.3.2)(iv), pp. 71–72).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.3.2)`(i)`–(iv) and (2.2.17), pp. 67–72.

- `IsocDagger.gluing_globalFrame`: For `Y = P^1_k` with its two standard affine charts and `X = G_m`, the gluing category is equivalent to `Isoc(G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O/K)`.
- `IsocDagger.gluing_single`: For the covering of `Y` by `Y` itself with one embedding `P`, the forgetful functor `(E, φ) ↦ E` is an isomorphism of categories onto `Isoc(X, Y, P/S)`: the cocycle condition forces `φ` to restrict to the identity on the diagonal, and a horizontal isomorphism with that restriction is the Taylor isomorphism `ε` ([§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (c)); a datum with `φ ≠ ε` does not exist.
- `IsocDagger.realisation_product`: For `T = P ×_O Spf O⟨s⟩` with `U = Y` embedded by `s = 0` and the projection `u: T → P`, the realisation `E_T` is `u_K^* E_P`, the pullback to the product with the open unit disc.
- `IsocDagger.gluing_cocycle_needed`: On a covering by three opens, constant rank-one transition scalars `c_{αβ}` with `c_{αβ} c_{βγ} c_{γα} ≠ 1` on the triple overlap do not form a gluing datum.
- Global frame: for `Y = P^1_k` covered by its two standard affine lines embedded in `Â^1_O`, and `X = G_m`, the gluing category is canonically equivalent to `Isoc(G_m, P^1, P̂^1/K)` defined with the global frame.
- Cocycle condition matters: on a covering of `Y` by three opens, rank-one data with constant transition scalars `c_{αβ} ∈ K^×` whose product `c_{αβ} c_{βγ} c_{γα}` on the triple overlap is `≠ 1` do not define an object.

### RD.3.23 Independence of the compactification

**Theorem.** Let `j : X ↪ Y` and `j' : X ↪ Y'` be open immersions and `v : Y' → Y` a PROPER morphism with `v∘j' = j` and `v^{-1}(X) = j'(X)` (Kedlaya's formulation: `f^{-1}(X) → X` an isomorphism). Then `v^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc†(X ⊂ Y'/K)` is an equivalence of categories, compatible with Frobenius structures. Consequently, for a proper `Y` containing `X` as an open subscheme, `Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K)` is independent of `Y` up to canonical equivalence (two compactifications are dominated by the closure of `X` in their product).

*Hypotheses.* Proper compactifications exist for separated finite type `X` by Nagata's theorem (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons Layer L2, *Nagata compactification over qcqs bases*); for quasi-projective `X` one may take a projective closure.

*Proof sketch.* Choose frames `Y ⊂ P` and `Y' ⊂ P'` with a morphism `u : P' → P` lifting `v` (possible locally); after dévissage and base changes on `P` inducing an admissible covering of a strict neighbourhood of `]X[_P`, reduce to the case where a section `P → P'` extends the section `X → P' ×_P X` given by `j'`; then replace `Y'` by the image of `Y` in `P'` and apply [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) (Berthelot, sketch of the proof of Théorème 2 in 2.4, applied to isocrystals in 4.2.2). Berthelot 96-03 Théorème (2.3.5), pp. 73–74. Reduction to `v` projective: Berthelot uses Raynaud–Gruson `I`, Corollaire 5.7.14 (p. 52: an `X`-admissible blow-up `Y″ → Y′` with `Y″ → Y` quasi-projective, hence projective); equivalently apply SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12 twice (`X`-admissible blow-ups `Y″ → Y` through `Y′` and `Y`‴ `→ Y′` through `Y″`) and use that equivalences of categories satisfy the two-out-of-six property. Projective case: the statement is local on `Y` (gluing, [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22)), so `Y` is affine with a closed immersion into `P` smooth near `X`; embed `Y′` in `P^N_P`, localise on `X` so that `X = Y′ ∩ D(s)` and the ideal of `X` in `D(s)` is generated by a regular sequence lifted to sections `t_i` of `O`(md); the zero scheme `T` of the `t_i` is étale over `P` at `X` and contains the closure of `X`, and [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) for `T → P` and `T² → P²` gives the equivalence. (Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.2), p. 27; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Lemma 2.6 and its proof, p. 3.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) *Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals*; [§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19) *Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; [§RD.3.11](#rd-3-11) *Étale morphisms proper over the closure of `X` induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.5](#rd-3-5) *Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems*; [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) *Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback*; SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.12 *Modifications are dominated by admissible blowups*.

**Checks.**

- `X = A^2, Y = P^2` and `Y' =` the blow-up of `P^2` at a point of the line at infinity: `v^*` is an equivalence although the boundaries `Z = P^1` and `Z'` (two rational curves) differ.
- `X = A^1, Y = P^1, Y' =` the closure of the diagonal in `P^1 × P^1` with `v` a projection: `v` is an isomorphism and `v^*` is the identity up to canonical isomorphism.

### RD.3.24 The category `Isoc†(X/K)` of a separated finite type `k`-scheme

**Definition.** For an open immersion `X ⊂ Y` of separated finite type `k`-schemes, `Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K)` is defined, when `Y` embeds into a formal `O`-scheme `P` smooth near `X`, as `Isoc(X, Y, P/K)` (independent of `P` by [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21)), and in general by gluing along a Zariski covering of `Y` by opens `Y_i` admitting such embeddings (a Čech/stack construction, local on `Y`). For `X` separated of finite type over `k, Isoc†(X/K) := Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K)` for some open immersion into a PROPER `k`-scheme `Y` (a compactification), independent of `Y` up to canonical equivalence by [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23). If `X` is proper, `Isoc†(X/K)` is the category of convergent isocrystals on `X`.

*Hypotheses.*

- Compactifications exist by Nagata's theorem (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons Layer L2, *Nagata compactification over qcqs bases*); frames exist Zariski-locally on `Y` (affine opens embed in formal affine spaces).
- `Isoc†(−/K)` is a stack for the Zariski and étale topologies on `X` (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.4, Definition 2.7), which is what makes the gluing well defined.

The API:

- `IsocDagger`: `Isoc†(X/K)`, defined through a compactification and Čech gluing of frames.
- `IsocDagger.ofFrame`: For a proper frame `(X, Y, P), Isoc†(X/K) ≃ Isoc(X, Y, P/K)` canonically.
- `IsocDagger.pullback`: `f^* : Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X'/K)` for any morphism `f : X' → X` of `k`-schemes, with `id^* ≅` id and (fg)`^* ≅ g^*f^*`.
- `IsocDagger.isStack`: `Isoc†` is a stack for the Zariski topology. For smooth `X`, overconvergent F-isocrystals additionally satisfy the étale descent of [§RD.3.50](#rd-3-50).
- `IsocDagger.monoidal`: K-linear abelian rigid monoidal category with unit `O_X^†`.
- `IsocDagger.proper_eq_convergent`: If `X` is proper, `Isoc†(X/K) ≃` convergent isocrystals on `X`.

*Proof sketch.* Choose a covering of `Y` by affine opens `Y_i` with frames `(X_i, Y_i, P_i)`; objects are families of overconvergent isocrystals on the frames of the `Y_i` together with gluing isomorphisms on the frames of `Y_i ∩ Y_j` (diagonal embeddings into `P_i × P_j`), satisfying the cocycle condition; independence of the covering by refinement and [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) (Berthelot §1.5, p. 14, by gluing local frame categories). The gluing construction and its independence of choices are [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)(iii), with the step Berthelot leaves to the reader supplied there); the Zariski stack property follows from the Frobenius-free local gluing of [§RD.3.20a](#rd-3-20a). Étale descent is established only with Frobenius structures on smooth `X` ([§RD.3.50](#rd-3-50)); the statement `IsocDagger.isStack` is for the Zariski topology. (Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Definition 2.7, pp. 3-4; Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.2.2), p. 27.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) *Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals*; [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) *Independence of the compactification*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons §L2; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`; [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) *Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback*; [§RD.3.20a](#rd-3-20a) *Zariski gluing of local frame coefficients without Frobenius*.

**Checks.**

- `IsocDagger.affineLine`: The Dwork isocrystal `L_π` defines an object of `Isoc†(A^1_{𝔽_p}/ℚ_p(π))` (Berthelot 4.2.3).
- `IsocDagger.point`: `Isoc†(Spec k/K)` is the category of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.
- `IsocDagger.proper_convergent`: For `X` proper, the restriction functor to convergent isocrystals is an equivalence.
- `IsocDagger.not_convergent_affine`: For `X = A^1` the restriction functor `Isoc†(A^1/K) → Isoc(A^1/K)` (convergent) is not essentially surjective: the extension of [§RD.5.10](#rd-5-10) is not in the image.
- `X = A^n: Isoc†(A^n/K)` is equivalent to the category of finite projective `K⟨t_1`..`t_n⟩†`-modules with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition ([§RD.3.32](#rd-3-32)).
- `X` proper: `Isoc†(X/K) =` convergent isocrystals (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.7).

### RD.3.25 Overconvergent F-isocrystals

**Definition.** Let `σ_K` be a Frobenius lift on `K` lifting the `q`-power map of `k (q = p^a)`. The Frobenius pullback `F^*` on `Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K)` is the composite of extension of scalars along `σ_K` and pullback along the relative `q`-power Frobenius of `(X, Y)` over `k` (realised on a frame by a lift `σ : P → P` of the `q`-power Frobenius compatible with `σ_K`, where such a lift exists, the result being independent of the lift by [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20)). An overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X` is an object `E ∈ Isoc†(X/K)` with an isomorphism `Φ : F^*E ≅ E`; morphisms commute with `Φ`. The category is F-`Isoc†(X/K)` (`F^a-Isoc†` when the power a is kept explicit). Concretely on a frame with Frobenius lift `σ` (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.2.3): a finite locally free `O_V`-module `E` on a strict neighbourhood `V` of `]X[`, with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition, and an isomorphism `F : σ^*E ≅ E` of modules with connection.

*Hypotheses.* The Frobenius structure forces the overconvergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism (Berthelot's unpublished Théorème 2.5.7, cited by Kedlaya), which is why Kedlaya's Definition 4.2.3 can leave it implicit; the condition is not automatic without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12).

The API:

- `FIsocDagger`: F-`Isoc†(X/K)`: objects `(E, Φ : F^*E ≅ E)`.
- `FIsocDagger.frobeniusPullback`: `F^* =` (relative `q`-Frobenius)`^* ∘ σ_K`-extension of scalars on `Isoc†(X/K)`.
- `FIsocDagger.forget`: The forgetful functor F-`Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X/K)`.
- `FIsocDagger.tensor`: Tensor products, duals, internal Hom and Tate twists `E(n)` (Frobenius multiplied by `q^{-n}`); abelian `K_0`-linear rigid monoidal `(K_0 = K^{σ_K})`.
- `FIsocDagger.pullback`: `f^*` for morphisms of `k`-schemes, commuting with `F^*`.
- `FIsocDagger.independent_of_lift`: On a frame, the category defined with a Frobenius lift `σ` does not depend on `σ` up to canonical equivalence.
- `FIsocDagger.pointFiber`: For `X = Spec 𝔽_q` and `K = W(𝔽_q)[1/p], q`-power Frobenius uses `σ_K = id` and gives finite-dimensional K-spaces with linear automorphism. Choosing p-power Frobenius instead uses the Witt Frobenius and gives Mathlib WittVector.Isocrystal `p 𝔽_q`; its carrier requires perfect residue field, while rank-one classification additionally requires algebraic closure.
- `FIsocDagger.localAtBoundary`: For a smooth curve `X ⊂ X̄` and `x ∈ X̄ ∖ X`, restriction to the boundary annulus gives a `(φ,∇)`-module over the Robba ring `R_{K}` in a local parameter at `x` (the local monodromy of `E` at `x`, RD.2).

*Proof sketch.* Existence of Frobenius lifts on frames: locally, for smooth affine pieces, by the lifting theorem for weakly complete algebras ([§RD.0.42](#rd-0-42)); globally `F^*` is defined by functoriality of `Isoc†` in `(X ⊂ Y)` (Berthelot 4.1-4.2). Independence of the lift: [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20). (Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Definition 4.2.3, p. 26; Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (4.1), p. 26.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.24](#rd-3-24) *The category `Isoc†(X/K)` of a separated finite type `k`-scheme*; [§RD.3.19](#rd-3-19) *Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames*; [§RD.3.20](#rd-3-20) *Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction*; [§RD.0.42](#rd-0-42) *Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth `O_K`-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)*; [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) *Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback*.

**Checks.**

- `FIsocDagger.dwork`: `L_π` with `Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)` is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on `A^1_{𝔽_p}; exp π(t^p − t)` converges on `|t| < p^{(p−1)/p²}` (check of coefficient valuations).
- `FIsocDagger.unit`: (`O^†_X`, id) is the unit object; `End(O^†_X) = K^{σ_K}` for `X` geometrically connected.
- `FIsocDagger.point_compat`: For `X = Spec k` with `k` algebraically closed, `O = W(k), q = p`: F-`Isoc†(X/K) ≃` WittVector.Isocrystal `p k` (Mathlib), and rank one objects are classified by Mathlib's `isocrystal_classification`.
- `FIsocDagger.twist`: The Tate twist `K(n)` on `Spec 𝔽_q` has Frobenius `q^{-n}`; it is not isomorphic to `K(0)` for `n ≠ 0` (slopes `−n` vs 0).
- `FIsocDagger.no_frobenius_example`: The module with integrable connection `O·e` on `A^1` with `∇e = e dt` is outside the convergent and overconvergent isocrystal categories (its Taylor exponential has radius `p^(−1/(p−1))<1`) and admits no Frobenius structure: its restriction to the boundary annulus at `∞` is not solvable ([§RD.2.41](#rd-2-41), in the local parameter 1/`t`).
- The unit F-isocrystal `O_X^†` with `Φ = id`; the Dwork F-isocrystal `L_π` on `A^1_{𝔽_p}` over `K = ℚ_p(π)` with `σ_K = id, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)` (Berthelot 4.2.3 `c`).
