### RD.3.42 Example: the frames `A^n ⊂ P^n` and `A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n` give equivalent categories

**Example.** Let `X = A^n_k` with the two compactifications `Y_1 = P^n_k` and `Y_2 = (P^1_k)^n` and frames `(X, Y_1, P̂^n_O), (X, Y_2, (P̂^1_O)^n)`. (a) In both frames the tube `]X[` is the closed unit polydisc `{|t_i| ≤ 1}`, and the polydiscs `V_λ =` {`|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}` for all `i`} `(λ < 1, λ → 1)` form a cofinal family of strict neighbourhoods, so `Γ(]Y_i[, j†O) = K⟨t_1`,..., `t_n⟩†` in both cases. (b) The equivalence `Isoc†(A^n ⊂ P^n/K) ≃ Isoc†(A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n/K)` of [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) is realised through the closure `Y_3` of the diagonal of `A^n` in `P^n × (P^1)^n`, whose projections to `Y_1` and `Y_2` are proper and are isomorphisms over `A^n`, with the frame `(X, Y_3, P̂^n × (P̂^1)^n)` mapping to both frames; on the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate it sends (`K⟨t_1`..`t_n⟩†, ∇(1) = π dt_1`) to itself.

*Hypotheses.* `n ≥ 1`; for `n = 1` the two compactifications coincide and the statement is the identity.

*Proof sketch.*

1. (a) In `P^n` with homogeneous coordinates `x_0`..`x_n` and `Z = {x_0 = 0}: ]Z[_λ = {|x_0| < λ max_i |x_i|}`, whose complement is `{|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, t_i = x_i/x_0` (Berthelot §2.1, p. 16, using the projective-coordinate inequalities). In `(P^1)^n, Z = ∪_i {t_i = ∞}` is cut out near a boundary point by the product of the coordinates `s_i = 1/t_i` with `|t_i| ≥ 1`, so the complement `W_λ` of `]Z[_λ` is {`|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}` for all `i`, and `|Π_{i∈I} t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}` for the set `I` of indices with `|t_i| ≥ 1`}; hence `W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n}`, and the two families are cofinal. Global sections: [§RD.3.8](#rd-3-8).
2. (b) The graph closure `Y_3 ⊆ Y_1 × Y_2` contains `X` as an open subscheme with `v_i^{-1}(X) = X` for both projections `v_i` (both are isomorphisms over `A^n`), so [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) applies to `v_1` and `v_2`; the diagonal frame is smooth over `O` ([§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) (b)).
3. Computation: under both identifications the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate `t_1` is the free rank one `K⟨t_1`..`t_n⟩†`-module with `∇(1) = π dt_1`, and its Taylor isomorphism `exp π(t'_1 − t_1)` converges on the diagonal tube `{|t_1 − t'_1| < 1}` (Berthelot 4.2.3 `b` for `n = 1`).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (2.1), p. 16, and (4.2.2), p. 27.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.21](#rd-3-21) *Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals*; [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) *Independence of the compactification*; [§RD.3.8](#rd-3-8) *Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*.

**Checks.**

- Test: strict neighbourhoods agree: for `λ < 1` the complement of `]Z_1[_λ` in `(P^n)^an` is exactly the polydisc `V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}`, and the complement `W_λ` of `]Z_2[_λ` in `((P^1)^n)^an` satisfies `W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n}` (for `n = 2` and `|t_1|, |t_2| ≥ 1, W_λ` is `{|t_1 t_2| ≤ λ^{-1}}`, strictly smaller than `V_λ`).
- Test: global sections of `j†O` in both frames equal `K⟨t_1`..`t_n⟩†` (the union over `λ` of the Tate algebras of the polydiscs of radius `λ^{-1}`).

### RD.3.43 Semicontinuity and purity of Newton polygons in families

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a noetherian scheme over a perfect field `k` of characteristic `p` and `E` a convergent F-isocrystal on `X` (for example the isocrystal of an F-crystal). (a) (Grothendieck–Katz) For every polygon `P` the set of points `x ∈ X` at which the Newton polygon of `E_x` lies on or above `P` is closed; the Newton polygon at a specialisation lies on or above the polygon at its generisation, with the same endpoints. (b) (de Jong–Oort) If `X` is irreducible, the locus where the Newton polygon differs from its value at the generic point is either empty or of pure codimension 1.

*Hypotheses.* Noetherian base; slopes use `v_p(p) = 1`, obtained from the uniformiser-normalised slopes of Layer RD.1 by division by `e = v_π(p)`; polygons are lower convex with fixed endpoints.

*Proof sketch.* (a) Reduce to a cyclic presentation of `∧^i` of a lattice and apply the semicontinuity of Newton polygons of characteristic polynomials of Frobenius matrices over a family (Katz, Theorem 2.3.1). (b) is de Jong–Oort's purity theorem; Kedlaya's Notes state both parts for convergent F-isocrystals with these hypotheses (Theorem 3.12). (Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, arXiv:1606.01321v6, Theorem 3.12; Katz, *Slope filtration of F-crystals*, Astérisque 63 (1979), Theorem 2.3.1; de Jong–Oort, *Purity of the stratification by Newton polygons*, `J`. Amer. Math. Soc. 13 (2000), Theorem 4.1.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.1.35](#rd-1-35) *Frobenius slopes and Newton (HN) polygons of `σ`-modules: generic slopes over `E` and `R^bd`, special slopes over `R`*.

**Checks.**

- On the `j`-line in characteristic `p` the isocrystal of `H¹` of the universal elliptic curve has Newton polygon with slopes 0, 1 at ordinary points and 1/2, 1/2 at the finitely many supersingular points: the jump locus has codimension 1.
- A constant isocrystal has empty jump locus.
- The jump is upward: the supersingular polygon (1/2, 1/2) lies above the ordinary one (0, 1), with the same endpoints.

<a id="rd-3-43a"></a>

### RD.3.43a Convergent Hartogs extension of a fixed-slope subobject

**Theorem.** Let `X` be smooth over a perfect field, `U⊂X` open with complement of codimension at least two, and `E` a convergent F-isocrystal with finite coefficient field. Restriction induces an isomorphism on morphisms between convergent F-isocrystals on `X`. If `S_U⊂E|_U` has rank `a`, locally free quotient and determinant of constant Frobenius slope, then `S_U` extends uniquely as a convergent sub-F-isocrystal of `E` with locally free quotient.

*Hypotheses.* The slope of the determinant is constant on each connected component. Frobenius, smoothness and codimension at least two are required; no overconvergence along `X∖U` is assumed.

*Proof sketch.* First prove the convergent Hartogs equality for functions on smooth formal lifts after deleting the codimension-two special-fibre locus. Apply it to horizontal Frobenius-equivariant Hom sections and glue to obtain full faithfulness. For rank one, iterate Frobenius and extend coefficients to twist the fixed slope to zero. The Katz–Crew correspondence, extended to finite coefficient fields by retaining the coefficient-field action, gives a p-adic local system on `U`. Extend each of its finite lattice quotients across `X∖U` by purity of branch locus, then recover the local system and the unit-root convergent object on `X`. Undo the twist and descend the coefficient extension by full faithfulness. For rank `a`, apply this to the determinant line in `∧^a E`. Extend its inclusion by Hartogs; the decomposability relations extend as equalities of sections. Horizontal morphisms of convergent isocrystals have locally constant rank on smooth lifts; the extended determinant inclusion therefore remains a line subbundle. The resulting Grassmannian section recovers the saturated rank-a subbundle and locally free quotient. This is the exterior-power argument of Notes Remark 5.2.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 5.1(c), Remark 5.2 and the proof of Theorem 4.1, pp. 8, 11–12; Stacks Tag 0BMB.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.33](#rd-3-33) *Convergent isocrystals*; [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent Frobenius structures*; [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) *Katz–Crew correspondence*; [§RD.1.37](#rd-1-37) *Exterior powers and slope twists*; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §1.8 *Purity of branch locus*; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.2 *Finite étale Galois categories and the étale fundamental groupoid*.

**Checks.**

- On `A²∖{0}⊂A²`, a constant slope-zero line and its inclusion in a constant rank-two object extend uniquely across the origin.
- For a common vertex of rank `a`, the determinant slope is the fixed vertical coordinate of that vertex; the hypothesis applies even when the other slopes vary.
- Codimension one is different: on `G_m⊂A¹`, a nontrivial Kummer unit-root object with tame monodromy at zero need not extend convergently across zero.


<a id="rd-3-44"></a>

### RD.3.44 Common Newton-vertex subisocrystal

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth variety over a perfect field `k` of characteristic `p`, with a convergent `F^n`-isocrystal `E` and a common Newton-polygon vertex of horizontal coordinate a at every geometric point. Then there is a unique convergent Frobenius subisocrystal of rank a whose slopes are the smallest a slopes at each point.

*Hypotheses.* Finite coefficient field, fixed `n≥1` and a fixed common break; use the convergent category, not merely a differential module or an arbitrary overconvergent subobject.

*Proof sketch.*

1. At the generic point use classical Dieudonné–Manin to select the initial slope block.
2. Katz's curve argument and Newton-stratification purity ([§RD.3.43](#rd-3-43)) construct the slope subobject on an open whose complement has codimension at least two. Its determinant has the constant slope given by the common vertex. Apply [§RD.3.43a](#rd-3-43a) to extend this convergent subobject across the residual locus.
3. A connection respects the block because its second fundamental map goes from lower slopes to higher slopes and the relevant Frobenius Hom is zero (Notes Remark 4.5). Uniqueness follows from the same slope separation.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2 and Remark 4.5, PDF pp. 8–9.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.43a](#rd-3-43a) *Convergent Hartogs extension of a fixed-slope subobject*; [§RD.3.37](#rd-3-37) *Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.1.32](#rd-1-32) *Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field*; [§RD.1.37](#rd-1-37) *Calculus of slopes: direct sums, tensor products, exterior powers, restriction of Frobenius, twists, Hom vanishing*; [§RD.3.43](#rd-3-43) *Semicontinuity and purity of Newton polygons in families*.

**Checks.**

- The subobject is connection-stable, not only Frobenius-stable at generic points.
- On a smooth surface, a common-vertex block already constructed off finitely many points extends across those points by RD.3.43a; Newton-polygon purity alone supplies no extension map.
- For `O⊕O(−1)`, the common vertex of rank one gives `O`; a vertex that occurs only generically does not satisfy the theorem.

<a id="rd-3-45"></a>

### RD.3.45 Dense-open global slope filtration

**Theorem.** For a convergent `F^n`-isocrystal on a smooth variety `X` over perfect `k`, there is a dense open `U` whose complement is a divisor such that on each connected component of `U` the Newton polygon is constant and the isocrystal has a unique filtration with isoclinic graded pieces of strictly increasing slopes.

*Hypotheses.*

- `X` is smooth of finite type; coefficients and `F^n` are fixed as in [§RD.3.44](#rd-3-44).
- An empty divisor is allowed; disconnected components are treated separately.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Upper semicontinuity of the Newton polygon and purity of the Newton-jumping locus ([§RD.3.43](#rd-3-43); Notes Theorem 3.12) give a dense open constant-polygon locus with complement of pure codimension one. On regular `X` this is the support of a divisor.
2. For each successive vertex use the common-vertex theorem, then pass to its quotient.
3. The first graded piece has the smallest slope. Frobenius-Hom vanishing gives compatibility and uniqueness; the result is global on `U` and distinct from the local Robba slope filtration of RD.2.

*Sources.* D’Addezio, *Parabolicity conjecture of F-isocrystals*, §2.2, p. 6; Xu–Zhu, *Bessel F-isocrystals for reductive groups*, Appendix A §A.2, PDF p. 64; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 3.12 and Corollary 4.2, PDF pp. 7–8.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.44](#rd-3-44) *Common Newton-vertex subisocrystal*; [§RD.3.37](#rd-3-37) *Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.43](#rd-3-43) *Semicontinuity and purity of Newton polygons in families*.

**Checks.**

- A constant slope-zero object permits `U=X`.
- A bare connection without Frobenius does not have this Newton filtration.

<a id="rd-3-46"></a>

### RD.3.46 The underlying vector bundle with connection of a convergent isocrystal on a smooth formal `O_K`-scheme

**Construction.** Let `𝔛` be a smooth formal scheme over `Spf O_K, O_K` possibly ramified over `W(k)`, with special fibre `𝔛_s` and rigid generic fibre `𝔛_η`, and let `E` be a convergent isocrystal on `𝔛_s/K_0, K_0 = W(k)[1/p]`. `(i) E` has an underlying vector bundle with flat connection `(E, ∇)` on `𝔛_η`: the realisation of `E` on the (not necessarily `W(k)`-smooth) formal scheme `𝔛`, in which `𝔛_s` is defined by an ideal of definition ([§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) (b)); the connection is relative to `K_0`, equivalently to `K`. (ii) If `E` underlies a crystalline F-isocrystal on `𝔛_s/W(k)`, then for every `W(k)`-model `Ũ` of an affine open `U ⊆ 𝔛` (`Ũ ⊗_{W(k)} O_K ≅ U`; such models exist for framed affines), `(E, ∇)|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{K_0} K`, the right side being given by [§RD.3.36](#rd-3-36) (d). The construction is exact, compatible with ⊗, duals and pullback along morphisms of smooth formal `O_K`-schemes.

*Hypotheses.*

- Over a ramified base `𝔛` has no Frobenius lift compatible with a lift of Frobenius on `O_K` in general; Frobenius structures are carried by `E` on the special fibre, not by the bundle.
- Framings (étale maps to `Spf O_K⟨x_1^{±1}`, …, `x_d^{±1}⟩`) exist on a basis of affine opens (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.10).
- Guo–Reinecke state `(i)` for convergent isocrystals on Ogus's convergent site of `𝔛_{p=0}`; by Berthelot (2.3.4) these are the convergent isocrystals defined by tubes, and tubes depend only on the reduced subscheme, so a convergent isocrystal on `𝔛_s` is the same datum.

The API:

- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle`: The vector bundle `E` on `𝔛_η` underlying a convergent isocrystal on `𝔛_s`, for `𝔛` smooth over `Spf O_K`.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingConnection`: Its flat connection relative to `K`.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_localModel`: For a `W(k)`-model `Ũ` of an affine open `U: (E, ∇)|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{K_0} K`.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_monoidal`: Exact, compatible with ⊗, duals and the unit.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_pullback`: Compatible with pullback along morphisms of smooth formal `O_K`-schemes.

*Proof sketch.* Realisation: for an affine open `U` with a closed immersion of `U_s` into a smooth formal `W(k)`-scheme `P`, lift `U_s → P` to `u: U → P` by formal smoothness along the ideal of definition, and put `E_U = u_K^* E_P` on `U_η = ]U_s[_U`; independence and gluing are [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) (b) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph, pp. 70–71). (ii): for a framed affine `U`, the unique `W(k)`-model `Ũ` with lifted framing (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.9) gives `u: U = Ũ ⊗ O_K → Ũ`, so `E_U = (E(Ũ)[1/p]) ⊗_{K_0} K` with its connection (Guo–Reinecke, Proposition 2.17, citing Ogus 1984, Remark 2.8.1, Theorem 2.15, Proposition 2.21). (Guo–Reinecke, *A prismatic approach to crystalline local systems*, Lemmas 2.9–2.10 and Proposition 2.17, pp. 14 and 16; Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.3.2)(ii), pp. 70–71.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) *Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback*; [§RD.3.33](#rd-3-33) *Convergent isocrystals `Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.36](#rd-3-36) *Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.7, smooth-lifting-from-level-zero *Smooth morphisms of the reduction lift to smooth formal morphisms (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Lemma 1.4(a))*.

**Checks.**

- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_unit`: The unit isocrystal has underlying bundle `(O_{𝔛_η}, d)`.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_unramified`: For `O_K = W(k)` and `𝔛 = Spf R` with a Frobenius lift, the underlying bundle of an F-isocrystal is `E(𝔛)[1/p]`, the bundle of [§RD.3.36](#rd-3-36) (d).
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_baseChange`: For `𝔛 = Ũ ⊗_{W(k)} O_K`, the underlying bundle is the base change `(E(Ũ)[1/p], ∇) ⊗_{K_0} K`.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_forgets_frobenius`: The unit object `O` and the Tate object `O(1)` have the same underlying bundle with connection `(O_{𝔛_η}, d)` but are not isomorphic as F-isocrystals: the bundle does not determine `Φ`.
- Unit: the underlying bundle of the unit isocrystal is `(O_{𝔛_η}, d)`.
- Unramified case: `O_K = W(k)` and `𝔛 = Ũ` give `E(𝔛)[1/p]` itself.

### RD.3.47 Unit-root F-isocrystals

**Definition.** Let `E` be a convergent or overconvergent `F^a`-isocrystal on `X`. `E` is unit-root if for every geometric point `x̄` of `X` all Frobenius slopes of the fibre `x̄^*E` are zero, i.e. the fibre has a basis `e_1`, …, `e_r` with `Φ(e_i ⊗ 1) = e_i` (Étesse §5.1); equivalently the fibre at every perfect point is isoclinic of slope 0. Unit-root objects form a full subcategory `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)^0` (respectively `F^a-Isoc†(X/K)^0`) stable under ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions, with no non-zero morphisms to or from isoclinic objects of non-zero slope. At a perfect point with `a = 1` and `K = W(k)[1/p]`, unit-root means that the Mathlib isocrystal has a `W`-lattice `L` with `Φ(L) = L`, equivalently a basis in which the matrix of `Φ` lies in `GL_r(W)`.

*Hypotheses.*

- Slopes are computed after pulling back to a perfect (or algebraically closed) point, where the Dieudonné–Manin classification applies.
- For overconvergent objects the condition is on the image in the convergent category; it is the same pointwise condition.

The API:

- `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot`: The predicate: every fibre at a geometric point has all Frobenius slopes 0.
- `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_iff_fibre`: `E` is unit-root iff each fibre at a perfect point admits a lattice stable under `Φ` on which `Φ` is bijective.
- `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.tensor`: Unit-root objects are stable under ⊗, duals and internal Hom, and contain the unit.
- `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.subquotient`: Subobjects and quotients of unit-root objects are unit-root.
- `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.extension`: Extensions of unit-root objects are unit-root.
- `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.pullback`: Pullback along any morphism preserves being unit-root.
- `FIsoc.hom_eq_zero_of_slopes_ne`: There are no non-zero morphisms between isoclinic objects of distinct slopes; in particular from unit-root objects to `O(n), n ≠ 0`.

*Proof sketch.* Fibres at perfect points are `F^a`-isocrystals over `K(Ω)` ([§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34)); over an algebraically closed point Dieudonné–Manin (CrystallineCohomology §CR.4.7; Mathlib's `isocrystal_classification` in rank one) decomposes them by slope, and slope 0 means a `Φ`-fixed basis (Étesse 2002 §5.1, p. 590; Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3, p. 6). Stability under subquotients and extensions and the vanishing of Hom between distinct slopes are Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3 and the remark after it (slopes are additive in exact sequences); the lattice characterisation at a point follows from Dieudonné–Manin. (Étesse, *Descente étale des F-isocristaux surconvergents et rationalité des fonctions `L` de schémas abéliens*, §5.1, p. 590; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Definition 3.3 and the following paragraph, p. 6; D'Addezio, *Parabolicity conjecture of F-isocrystals*, Definition 3.3.3, p. 11.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; CrystallineCohomology §CR.4.7 *Slope decomposition on the existing isocrystal carrier*; Mathlib `WittVector.Isocrystal`; Mathlib `WittVector.isocrystal_classification`.

**Checks.**

- `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_slopeZero_point`: At a perfect point, Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal `p k` 0 `(Φ = σ)` is unit-root: the lattice `W(k)` is `Φ`-stable with `Φ` bijective.
- `FIsoc.not_isUnitRoot_slopeOne`: StandardOneDimIsocrystal `p k` 1 `(Φ = pσ)` is not unit-root: every lattice `L` satisfies `Φ(L) = pL ≠ L`.
- `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_unit`: The unit object `(Φ = id)` is unit-root, and so is the zero object.
- `FIsoc.dwork_isUnitRoot`: The dual Dwork F-isocrystal `L_π^∨=L_(−π)` on `A^1` is unit-root: it has rank one and its Frobenius at the point 0 is `θ(0) = 1`. At the point 1 its Frobenius is `θ(1) = ζ_p`, a primitive p-th root of unity and so a unit but not 1; a test asserting `Φ = 1` at every Teichmüller point would be wrong.
- `FIsoc.tate_not_unitRoot`: `O(1)` is isoclinic of slope `−1` and not unit-root, although it has rank one.
- The dual Dwork F-isocrystal `L_π^∨=L_(−π) (∇(1) = −π dt, Φ = θ(t) := exp π(t − t^p), σ = id)` is unit-root: it has rank one, hence is isoclinic (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 3.5), and at the point 0 its Frobenius is `θ(0) = 1`. At the other `𝔽_p`-points the Frobenius is not 1: by Dwork's theorem `θ(1) = ζ_p` is a primitive p-th root of unity `(ζ_p ≡ 1 + π mod π²)` and `θ(x̂) = ζ_p^x` for the Teichmüller lift `x̂` of `x ∈ 𝔽_p`, a unit, consistently with slope 0. The tempting substitution `x̂^p = x̂` inside `exp π(t − t^p)` is not legitimate: `exp(πt)` and `exp(−πt^p)` diverge on `|t| = 1`, and only their product `θ` converges there.
- The Tate object `O(1)` is isoclinic of slope `−1`, hence not unit-root.
- For odd `p`, canonical `L_π` has multiplier `θ⁻¹` and eigenvalue `ζ_π⁻¹` at 1, whereas `L_π^∨` has multiplier `θ` and eigenvalue `ζ_π`. These distinct eigenvalues both have slope zero.

<a id="rd-3-48"></a>

### RD.3.48 Katz–Crew: unit-root F-isocrystals are lisse p-adic sheaves

**Theorem.** Let `k` be a perfect field containing `𝔽_q (q = p^a), K = W(k)[1/p]` with `σ` the Witt-vector Frobenius, and `X` a smooth separated `k`-scheme of finite type. Let `ℚ_q = W(𝔽_q)[1/p] ⊆ K`. The functor `V ↦ (V ⊗_{ℚ_q} O_{X/K}, 1 ⊗ σ^a)` is an exact fully faithful ⊗-functor from the category of étale `ℚ_q`-local systems on `X` to `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`, with essential image the unit-root convergent `F^a`-isocrystals; a quasi-inverse sends `E` to the étale sheaf of `Φ`-fixed horizontal sections. If `X` is connected with a geometric point `x̄`, unit-root convergent `F^a`-isocrystals are thus equivalent to continuous representations of `π_1^ét(X, x̄)` on finite-dimensional `ℚ_q`-vector spaces. For `a = 1` this is the equivalence of Kedlaya, Notes, Theorem 3.7; the version with `ℚ_q`-coefficients and `F^a`-structures is the one used in D’Addezio, proof of Proposition 3.3.4.

*Hypotheses.*

- `X` smooth; the field `k` perfect and containing `𝔽_q` so that the `F^a`-isocrystal category is `ℚ_q`-linear.
- Local systems are étale `ℚ_q`-local systems: the étale stackification of the isogeny category of `ℤ_q`-local systems (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.3, with `W(𝔽_q)`-coefficients).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Lattices: a unit-root convergent `F^a`-isocrystal is, locally on `X, M ⊗ ℚ` for a crystal `M` of finite locally free modules with `Φ: (F^a)^*M ≅ M` an isomorphism (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.3 records that unit-root objects come from crystals of locally free modules; for the convergent/crystalline translation use [§RD.3.36](#rd-3-36) (c)).
2. Katz's construction (the proofs are Crew 1987, Theorem 2.1, and Katz's Proposition 4.1.1): on `M/p^m` the equation `Φ(v) = v` is solved étale-locally, because the Lang map `g ↦ g^{−1} σ^a(g)` on `GL_r(W_m(k′))` is finite étale and surjective; the solutions form a locally constant sheaf `T_m` of free `W_m(𝔽_q)`-modules of `rank r`, and `T = lim T_m` is a `ℤ_q`-local system with `M ≅ T ⊗ O_crys` compatibly with `Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a`.
3. Conversely `T ↦ T ⊗ O_crys` with `Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a` is a unit-root `F^a`-crystal; on Hom-spaces both constructions identify `Hom(V, V′)` with the `Φ`-fixed horizontal sections of the internal Hom, which gives full faithfulness; pass to isogeny categories and stackify on both sides (rational local systems are étale-locally of the form `T[1/p]`), using that convergent `F^a`-isocrystals on smooth `X` form an étale stack (Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 2.1 and the remark after it).
4. For `X` connected, the étale `ℚ_q`-local systems are continuous `ℚ_q`-representations of `π_1^ét(X, x̄)` (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.3 with EtaleCohomologyFoundations §`F`.0.2).

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 3.7, p. 6, and Remark 3.10, p. 7, and Remark 2.3, p. 3; D'Addezio, *Parabolicity conjecture of F-isocrystals*, Proposition 3.3.4 and its proof, p. 11.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.47](#rd-3-47) *Unit-root F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.36](#rd-3-36) *Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)*; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.0.3 *Integral, isogeny and rational `ℤ_p`-local systems*; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §`F`.0.2; CrystallineCohomology §CR.1.2 *Rational crystals and nondegenerate F-crystals*; CrystallineCohomology §CR.4.7 *Slope decomposition on the existing isocrystal carrier*; Mathlib `WittVector.Isocrystal`; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`.

**Checks.**

- Point over `𝔽_p`: the F-isocrystal `(ℚ_p, Φ = u)` with `u ∈ ℤ_p^×` is unit-root and corresponds to the character of `Gal(F̄_p/𝔽_p)` sending the arithmetic Frobenius to `u^{−1}`: a `Φ`-fixed vector `v` of `K̂^{ur}` satisfies `u σ(v) = v`, so `σ(v) = u^{−1} v`.
- Non-example: `(ℚ_p, Φ = p)` over `𝔽_p` has no non-zero `Φ`-fixed vector over `K̂^{ur} (v_p(p σ(v)) = 1 + v_p(v))`, consistently with its slope 1.
- Over an algebraically closed point containing `𝔽_q`, the theorem is Dieudonné–Manin: unit-root `F^a`-isocrystals are `ℚ_q`-vector spaces tensored with `K`, and the unit has endomorphism field `K^{σ^a}=ℚ_q` (`ℚ_p` when `a=1`).

<a id="rd-3-48a"></a>

### RD.3.`48a` Descent of horizontal Frobenius-equivariant idempotents

**Theorem.** Let `A_0` be a smooth `k`-algebra with smooth lift `A`, weak completion `A†`, completion `Â` and a Frobenius lift. Let `N` be a finite projective `A†_K`-module with integrable overconvergent connection and invertible horizontal Frobenius. Every `Â_K`-linear idempotent `ê` of `N̂=N⊗Â_K` that is horizontal and Frobenius-equivariant is the scalar extension of a unique horizontal Frobenius-equivariant idempotent `e∈End_{A†_K}(N)`. Its image and kernel are finite projective `(σ,∇)`-modules, and their completions are the specified image and kernel of `ê`.

*Hypotheses.* Smooth reduction, the connection and the invertible Frobenius are required. Descent of isomorphism classes of projective modules alone does not descend their embeddings.

*Proof sketch.* This is a corollary of [§RD.5.8](#rd-5-8), preceding RD.3.49 in the proof order. Via the smooth-affine realisations of RD.3.29 and RD.3.34, fullness lifts the specified endomorphism `ê` to a horizontal Frobenius-equivariant endomorphism `e` of `N`. Faithfulness gives both uniqueness and `e²=e`. Split this idempotent on the finite projective module `N`; horizontality and Frobenius equivariance preserve its image and kernel. Scalar extension carries these actual summands to the specified image and kernel of `ê`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals*, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; Étesse, *Descente étale des F-isocristaux surconvergents et rationalité des fonctions `L` de schémas abéliens*, Théorème 6, p. 598, for the direct-summand conclusion.

*Needs:* [§RD.5.8](#rd-5-8) *Full faithfulness of restriction to convergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.29](#rd-3-29) *Smooth-affine realisation by dagger modules*; [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals on smooth formal lifts*; [§RD.3.28](#rd-3-28) *`(σ,∇)`-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *A dagger algebra and its completion: faithful flatness, points, completed local rings, reducedness and regularity, supremum norm*.

**Checks.**

- The zero and identity idempotents descend to 0 and 1, giving `N=0⊕N` and `N=N⊕0`.
- For overconvergent objects `M,P` and a convergent horizontal Frobenius-equivariant `h:M̂→P̂`, the specified graph projector `ê_h(m,p)=(m,h(m))` on `M̂⊕P̂` descends. Its lower-left entry is the unique overconvergent lift of `h`; the completion identification is retained.
- The first-coordinate projector on a direct sum of two overconvergent Kummer F-isocrystals descends with its specified image and kernel.
- For `A=ℚ_p⟨t⟩†, f=Σp^{⌊√n⌋}tⁿ` lies in `Â` but not A. The graph projector (x,y)↦(x,fx) on `Â²` cannot descend to A. With the trivial connection it is not horizontal, so it is excluded by the hypotheses.

<a id="rd-3-49"></a>

### RD.3.49 Étesse: convergent direct summands of overconvergent F-isocrystals are overconvergent

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth separated `k`-scheme of finite type. (1) If `E ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K)` and its image `Ê ∈ F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)` decomposes as `Ê ≅ E_1 ⊕ E_2`, then there are `E_1†, E_2† ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K)`, unique up to isomorphism, with `Ê_i† ≅ E_i` and `E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2†`. (2) If `E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2†` and `E′ ≅ E′_1† ⊕ E′_2†` are two such objects and `g: E → E′` is a morphism whose image `ĝ` is diagonal, `ĝ = φ ⊕ ψ`, then there are unique `f_i: E_i† → E′_i†` with `g = f_1 ⊕ f_2` and `ĝ = f̂_1 ⊕ f̂_2`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth; Frobenius structures are part of the data (the proof uses the Monsky–Washnitzer description of [§RD.3.31](#rd-3-31)).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Localise on `X` (Zariski stack, [§RD.3.40](#rd-3-40)), so `X = Spec A_0` smooth affine with lift `A` and Frobenius lift `F` on `A†`; by [§RD.3.31](#rd-3-31), `E` is a `(σ,∇)`-module `N` over `A†_K` and `Ê` corresponds to `N ⊗ Â_K` (Étesse 2002, §5.2, pp. 591–592).
2. After [§RD.5.8](#rd-5-8), descend the horizontal Frobenius-equivariant projector of the specified decomposition by its corollary [§RD.3.48a](#rd-3-48a). Define `M` and `P` as its image and kernel; their completed embeddings are the specified ones.
3. Horizontality and Frobenius equivariance restrict the structures to `M` and `P`. Uniqueness of the descended projectors makes these local decompositions compatible on overlaps, so they glue by [§RD.3.40](#rd-3-40). For (2), compose the given `g` with the descended inclusions and projections. Faithfulness makes its off-diagonal entries zero and identifies its diagonal entries with the specified completed morphisms.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Full faithfulness for overconvergent F-isocrystals*, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; Étesse, *Descente étale des F-isocristaux surconvergents et rationalité des fonctions `L` de schémas abéliens*, Théorème 6 and its proof, p. 598; Proposition 6 with Corollaries 1–2, p. 586; Propositions `9′` and `10′`, pp. 590–592.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.31](#rd-3-31) *Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence*; [§RD.3.40](#rd-3-40) *Zariski gluing of Frobenius structures on isocrystals*; [§RD.3.29](#rd-3-29) *On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with `A†_K`-modules*; [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.38](#rd-3-38) *Monsky–Washnitzer algebras are henselian along `π`; lifting of étale algebras and descent of projective modules*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *A dagger algebra and its completion: faithful flatness, points, completed local rings, reducedness and regularity, supremum norm*; [§RD.3.48a](#rd-3-48a) *Descent of horizontal Frobenius-equivariant idempotents*.

**Checks.**

- Degenerate splitting: `Ê = Ê ⊕ 0` lifts to `E ⊕ 0`.
- Kummer pair (`p` odd, `X = G_m`): the direct sum of the Kummer F-isocrystals with `a = 0` and `a = 1/(p−1)` is overconvergent, and its convergent decomposition lifts to the overconvergent decomposition.
- Non-example: a convergent subobject that is not a direct summand need not be overconvergent — the unit-root subobject of `H¹` of the universal elliptic curve on the ordinary locus ([§RD.5.10](#rd-5-10); Berthelot (2.3.9)(iii)).

<a id="rd-3-50"></a>

### RD.3.50 Étesse: étale descent for overconvergent F-isocrystals

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth separated `k`-scheme of finite type. (1) Every étale surjective morphism `f: Y → X` satisfies descent for overconvergent `F^a`-isocrystals: `f^*` induces an equivalence from `F^a-Isoc†(X/K)` to the category of objects of `F^a-Isoc†(Y/K)` with descent data relative to `f` (isomorphisms `p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E` on `Y ×_X Y` satisfying the cocycle condition on `Y ×_X Y ×_X Y`). (2) If `f: Y → X` is étale, dominant and separated, `F^a-Isoc†(X/K)` is the 2-fibre product of `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)` and `F^a-Isoc†(Y/K)` over `F^a`-`Isoc(Y/K)`: a convergent `F^a`-isocrystal on `X` whose pullback to `Y` is overconvergent is overconvergent, uniquely, and similarly for morphisms. (3) The analogous fibre-product statements hold for an extension of the base field `k ⊆ k′` (with `K ⊆ K′` as in Étesse 1.1) and for the combination of both. (4) A proper surjective generically étale morphism `f: Y → X` also satisfies descent for overconvergent `F^a`-isocrystals.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth and Frobenius structures present; the convergent descent results of Ogus (1984, Theorems 4.5 and 4.6) are used over a perfect closure of `k`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Base change to an algebraic closure `k′` of `k`: by Ogus's descent theorem for convergent F-isocrystals (Duke 1984, Theorems 4.5–4.6) the convergent `F^a`-isocrystal descends along `f′` (Étesse 2002, proof of Théorème 1, p. 593).
2. On a dense affine open `U = Spec A_0 ⊆ X` with an affine open `V = Spec B_0` of `Y` étale dominant over it, lift to `A† → B†` ([§RD.3.39](#rd-3-39)) and use the intersection description `A†_K = Â′_{K′} ∩ B†_K`: a module over `Â′_{K′}` with connection and Frobenius whose base change to `B̂′` comes from a `(σ,∇)`-module over `B†_K` comes from a unique `(σ,∇)`-module over `A†_K` (Étesse, Proposition 10, pp. 591–592, built on Propositions 2–9).
3. Glue the affine pieces: with a global frame through the equivalences of [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) and the gluing of coherent `j†`-modules ([§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15)); without one, along local frames ([§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22), Berthelot (2.3.2)(iii)); Frobenius structures glue by the same uniqueness (pp. 593–595).
4. (2), (3) are proved the same way (Théorèmes 2, `2′, 2″`, pp. 595–596); (4) combines Ogus's proper descent with (2) over a dense open where `f` is étale (Théorème 3, p. 596).

*Sources.* Étesse, *Descente étale des F-isocristaux surconvergents et rationalité des fonctions `L` de schémas abéliens*, Théorèmes 1, 2, `2′, 2″`, 3 and their proofs, pp. 592–596; Proposition 10, pp. 591–592.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.39](#rd-3-39) *Étale lifts of smooth affines: uniqueness after weak completion, Frobenius and differentials*; [§RD.3.31](#rd-3-31) *Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence*; [§RD.3.29](#rd-3-29) *On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with `A†_K`-modules*; [§RD.3.40](#rd-3-40) *Zariski gluing of Frobenius structures on isocrystals*; [§RD.3.22](#rd-3-22) *Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback*; [§RD.3.15](#rd-3-15) *Coherent `j†O`-modules glue along finite open coverings of `X`*; [§RD.3.34](#rd-3-34) *Convergent F-isocrystals `F^a`-`Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.23](#rd-3-23) *Independence of the compactification*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *A dagger algebra and its completion: faithful flatness, points, completed local rings, reducedness and regularity, supremum norm*; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`.

**Checks.**

- Kummer descent (`p` odd, `K ⊇ μ_{p−1}`): along the finite étale Galois cover `G_m → G_m, s ↦ s^{p−1} = t`, with group `μ_{p−1}`, descent data on the unit object of `G_m` correspond to characters of `μ_{p−1}`, and descend to the Kummer F-isocrystals on `G_m` with `∇(1) = (m/(p−1)) dt/t` and Frobenius `t^m`.
- Trivial cover: for `f = id` descent data are the identity and (1) is the identity functor.
- Zariski coverings are a special case, already covered by [§RD.3.20a](#rd-3-20a) without smoothness or Frobenius.

<a id="rd-3-51"></a>

### RD.3.51 Kummer isocrystals `K_a` on `G_m`

**Construction.** On the frame `(G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O)` with coordinate `t`, for `a ∈ ℤ_p` let `K_a` be the free `j†O_{P^1_K}`-module of rank one on a generator `e` with `∇(e) = a e ⊗ dt/t`. Global sections of `j†O` are the Laurent series `Σ_{n∈ℤ} c_n t^n` converging on some annulus `ρ < |t| < 1/ρ, ρ < 1` (written `K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†`), and the sections on the tube `]G_m[ = {|t| = 1}` form `K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩`. Then: `K_a` is an overconvergent isocrystal on `G_m; K_a ⊗ K_b ≅ K_{a+b}` and `K_a^∨ ≅ K_{−a}; K_a ≅ K_b` if and only if `a − b ∈ ℤ` (an isomorphism `K_b → K_a` is `e_b ↦ t^{b−a} e_a`); the horizontal sections of `K_a`, over the tube or over a strict neighbourhood, are `K·t^{−a} e` if `a ∈ ℤ` and 0 otherwise; the pullback along `t ↦ t^N` is `K_{Na}`; and, for the Frobenius lift `t ↦ t^p` with a compatible absolute p-Frobenius lift `σ_K` on `K`, `K_a` admits a Frobenius structure if and only if `(p − 1)a ∈ ℤ`, the structure being multiplication by `t^{(p−1)a}`.

*Hypotheses.*

- `a ∈ ℤ_p` is needed for convergence: for `a ∉ ℤ_p` the binomial coefficients `binom(a, k)` are unbounded and the connection is not even convergent.
- For Frobenius structures fix an isometric `σ_K:K→K` lifting the absolute p-power map of the residue field and extend it by `t↦t^p`; it fixes `a∈ℤ_p`. The identity-coefficient case applies when the residue field is `𝔽_p`.

The API:

- `Kummer.isoc`: For `a ∈ ℤ_p`, the rank-one overconvergent isocrystal `K_a` on `G_m` with `∇(e) = a e dt/t`.
- `Kummer.tensor`: `K_a ⊗ K_b ≅ K_{a+b}, K_0 ≅` unit, `K_a^∨ ≅ K_{−a}`.
- `Kummer.iso_iff`: `K_a ≅ K_b` iff `a − b ∈ ℤ`.
- `Kummer.horizontalSections`: `Γ(K_a)^{∇=0}` is one-dimensional (spanned by `t^{−a} e`) if `a ∈ ℤ` and zero otherwise, over the tube and over strict neighbourhoods.
- `Kummer.pullback_pow`: The pullback along `t ↦ t^N` is `K_{Na}`.
- `Kummer.frobenius_iff`: With the Frobenius lift `t ↦ t^p` and compatible `σ_K`, `K_a` has a Frobenius structure iff `(p − 1)a ∈ ℤ`, namely multiplication by `t^{(p−1)a}`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Overconvergence: by [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17) on the two affine charts (overconvergence is local on `P`, [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (d)), `∂^{[k]} e = binom(a, k) t^{−k} e` with `|binom(a, k)| ≤ 1`, so on `{η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η}` the decay `‖∂^{[k]}e‖ λ^k ≤ (λ/η)^k → 0` holds for `η > λ`; the chart at `∞` is the same with `−a`.
2. Tensor, dual and pullback are computed on generators; an isomorphism `K_b → K_a` sends `e_b` to `g e_a` with `t g′ = (b − a) g`, so `g = c t^{b−a}`, a unit of `K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†` exactly when `a − b ∈ ℤ`; horizontal sections are the case `b = 0`, where the Laurent coefficients satisfy `(n + a) g_n = 0`.
3. Frobenius: a horizontal `Φ: F^*K_a → K_a, F^*K_a` having `∇(1) = pa dt/t`, is multiplication by some `h` with `t h′ = a(p − 1) h`, so `h = c t^{a(p−1)}`, analytic and invertible on annuli near `|t| = 1` iff `a(p − 1) ∈ ℤ` (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.8)(iii)).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.2.15)(ii)(b), p. 67; (2.3.8)(iii), p. 76.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17) *The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*; Mathlib `PadicInt`.

**Checks.**

- For `K=W(𝔽_(p²))[1/p]`, identity on coefficients does not lift absolute p-Frobenius. Witt Frobenius does, fixes `a∈ℤ_p`, and gives the same criterion `(p−1)a∈ℤ` and multiplier `t^((p−1)a)`.

- `Kummer.zero_eq_unit`: `K_0` is the unit object `(j†O, d)`.
- `Kummer.one_iso_unit`: `K_1 ≅ K_0` via `e ↦ t e`, so isomorphism classes depend on a modulo `ℤ`.
- `Kummer.half_frobenius`: For `p` odd, `K_{1/2}` has the Frobenius structure given by multiplication by `t^{(p−1)/2}`.
- `Kummer.no_sections_nonintegral`: For `a ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ, K_a` has no non-zero horizontal section even on the tube `{|t| = 1}`.
- `Kummer.not_convergent_outside_Zp`: For `a = 1/p` the formula `∇(e) = a e dt/t` defines a module with connection on the annulus that is not convergent: `|binom(1/p, k)|` is unbounded.
- `K_0` is the unit; `K_1 ≅ K_0` through `e ↦ t e`.
- For `p` odd, `K_{1/2}` carries the Frobenius structure `t^{(p−1)/2}` (Kummer F-isocrystal of the double cover).

<a id="rd-3-52"></a>

### RD.3.52 A p-adic Liouville-type exponent: `p^n/(n + λ)` tends to 0 but not geometrically

**Lemma.** There is `λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ` such that the sequence `f_n = p^n/(n + λ), n ≥ 1`, satisfies `|f_n| → 0` while for no `ρ > 1` does `|f_n| ρ^n → 0` (equivalently limsup `|f_n|^{1/n} = 1`). Explicitly one may take `λ = −Σ_{k≥1} p^{m_k}` with `m_1 = 2, N_k = Σ_{j≤k} p^{m_j}` and `m_{k+1} = N_k − k`; this `λ` is not rational. Consequently the power series `Σ_{n≥1} f_n t^n` lies in the Tate algebra `K⟨t⟩` of the closed unit disc but not in its overconvergent subring `K⟨t⟩†` (nor in `K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†`).

*Hypotheses.* Any `p ≥ 2`; the choice of `m_k` only needs `v_p(N_k + λ)/N_k → 1`, with `v_p(N_k + λ) − N_k → −∞`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. The `m_k` increase strictly (`m_2 = p² − 1 ≥ 3` and `m_{k+1} ≥ p^{m_k} − k`), and `−λ` has infinitely many non-zero and infinitely many zero p-adic digits, so `λ ∉ ℤ` and `n + λ ≠ 0` for all `n`; since the gaps `m_{k+1} − m_k` tend to infinity, the digit expansion of `−λ` is not eventually periodic, so `λ ∉ ℚ`.
2. For `n = N_k: N_k + λ = −Σ_{j>k} p^{m_j}` has valuation `m_{k+1} = N_k − k`, so `|f_{N_k}| = p^{−k} → 0` but `|f_{N_k}| ρ^{N_k} = p^{−k} ρ^{N_k} → ∞` for every `ρ > 1`.
3. For `N_k < n < N_{k+1}` (with `N_0 = 0`): `n + λ = (n − N_k) + (N_k + λ)` with `0 < n − N_k < p^{m_{k+1}} ≤ p^{v_p(N_k+λ)}`, so `v_p(n + λ) = v_p(n − N_k) ≤ log_p n` and `|f_n| ≤ n p^{−n} → 0`. This construction realises the p-adic Liouville phenomenon referred to by Kedlaya (Notes, Remark 5.6).

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Remark 5.6, p. 13; Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.1.2.2), p. 49.

*Needs:* Mathlib `PadicInt`; Mathlib `Padic`; [§RD.0.38](#rd-0-38) *A function converging only on the closed unit disc separates completion from overconvergence*.

**Checks.**

- For `p = 2: m_1 = 2, N_1 = 4, m_2 = 3, N_2 = 12, m_3 = 10: |f_4| = 2^{−1}, |f_{12}| = 2^{−2}`, while `4 + λ ≡ 0` mod `2^3` and `12 + λ ≡ 0` mod `2^{10}`.
- Contrast: for `λ = −1`/2 (`p` odd), `v_p(n − 1/2) = v_p(2n − 1) ≤ log_p(2n)`, so `|f_n| ≤ 2n p^{−n}` and `Σ f_n t^n` converges for `|t| < p`: it is overconvergent. The numbers `n − 1`/2 are not all units (`p` divides `2n − 1` for `n = (p + 1)`/2); what matters is that `v_p(n + λ)` grows only logarithmically. In general `Σ f_n t^n` is overconvergent if and only if `limsup_n v_p(n + λ)/n < 1`, and no `λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ` has `|n + λ|` bounded below, because `ℕ` is dense in `ℤ_p`.
- Contrast: for a negative integer `λ` the sequence is undefined at `n = −λ`, and for an integer `λ ≥ 0` the series `Σ f_n t^n` is overconvergent `(v_p(n + λ) ≤ log_p(n + λ))`; so `λ ∉ ℤ` is required.

<a id="rd-3-53"></a>

### RD.3.53 Counterexample: without Frobenius, restriction from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is not full

**Example.** Let `λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ` be as in [§RD.3.52](#rd-3-52) and `h = Σ_{n≥1} p^n t^n ∈ K⟨t⟩†`. On `(G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O)` let `M` be the free `j†O`-module on `e_1, e_2` with `∇e_2 = λ e_2 ⊗ dt/t` and `∇e_1 = h e_2 ⊗ dt/t`, an extension `0 → K_λ → M → O → 0` of the unit object by the Kummer isocrystal `K_λ`. Then `M` is an overconvergent isocrystal on `G_m, Hom_{Isoc†(G_m/K)}(O, M) = 0`, and `Hom_{Isoc(G_m/K)}(O, M) = K·(e_1 + f e_2)` with `f = −Σ_{n≥1} p^n t^n/(n + λ)`. Hence the restriction functor `Isoc†(G_m/K) → Isoc(G_m/K)`, which is faithful, is not full, and the extension `M` splits in `Isoc(G_m/K)` but not in `Isoc†(G_m/K)`. No Frobenius structure exists on `M` (Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem with Frobenius would forbid this behaviour).

*Hypotheses.* The exponent `λ` must be a p-adic integer, so that `M` is overconvergent, and not an integer, so that the homogeneous equation has no solution; its Liouville property makes the particular solution `f` convergent but not overconvergent.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Overconvergence of `M`: on the chart at 0, `∂^{[k]}e_2 = binom(λ, k) t^{−k} e_2` and `∂^{[k]}e_1 = a_k e_2` with `a_k = (1/k) Σ_{n≥1} p^n binom(n + λ − 1, k − 1) t^{n−k}`, whose sup norm on `{η ≤ |t| ≤ 1}` is `≤ k η^{−k}` because `binom(n + λ − 1, k − 1) ∈ ℤ_p`; so `‖∂^{[k]}e‖ λ_0^k → 0` for `η > λ_0` and [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17) applies; the chart at `∞` (`s = 1/t`, where `h(1/s) = Σ p^n s^{−n}` is bounded by 1 on `|s| > 1/p`) is the same, and overconvergence is local on `P` ([§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) (d)). The connection is defined on the strict neighbourhood `{1/p < |t| < p}`.
2. Horizontal sections: `s = c e_1 + g e_2` is horizontal iff `c` is constant and `t g′ + λ g = −c h`, i.e. `(n + λ) g_n = −c h_n` for all `n ∈ ℤ`; as `λ ∉ ℤ` this forces `g = c f`.
3. Over the tube `{|t| = 1}` sections are Laurent series with coefficients tending to 0, and `f` qualifies ([§RD.3.52](#rd-3-52)), so `Hom_{Isoc}(O, M) = K(e_1 + f e_2)`; over strict neighbourhoods sections are overconvergent Laurent series and `f` does not qualify, so `c = 0` and `Hom_{Isoc†}(O, M) = 0`. Faithfulness of restriction is [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) (c).
4. A Frobenius structure on `M` would induce one on the sub-object `K_λ`, which needs `(p − 1)λ ∈ ℤ` (kummer-isocrystal), impossible since `λ ∉ ℚ` ([§RD.3.52](#rd-3-52)); the counterexample is constructed here, Abe's published counterexample (IMRN 2011) not being publicly accessible.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Remark 5.6, p. 13; Berthelot, *Cohomologie rigide et cohomologie rigide `à` supports propres. Première partie (version provisoire 1991)*, (2.3.9)`(i)`–(ii), p. 77.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.52](#rd-3-52) *A p-adic Liouville-type exponent: `p^n/(n + λ)` tends to 0 but not geometrically*; [§RD.3.51](#rd-3-51) *Kummer isocrystals `K_a` on `G_m`*; [§RD.3.17](#rd-3-17) *The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection*; [§RD.3.16](#rd-3-16) *Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on `P` and on `X`, stable under subquotients*; [§RD.3.14](#rd-3-14) *Coherent `j†O`-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods*; [§RD.3.33](#rd-3-33) *Convergent isocrystals `Isoc(X/K)`*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.3.37](#rd-3-37) *Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals*.

**Checks.**

- The map `Hom_{Isoc†}(O, M) = 0 → Hom_{Isoc}(O, M) = K` is injective (faithfulness) but not surjective.
- Replacing `λ` by an exponent with `v_p(n + λ) = O(log n)` (for instance `λ = −1`/2 with `p` odd, or any `λ ∈ (ℚ ∩ ℤ_p) ∖ ℤ`) makes `f` overconvergent and the two Hom-spaces agree; for the Liouville exponent of [§RD.3.52](#rd-3-52) one has `limsup_n v_p(n + λ)/n = 1`, so the failure is a Liouville phenomenon. No `λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ` keeps `|n + λ|` bounded below, so the relevant condition is the growth of `v_p(n + λ)`, not a lower bound.
- In the convergent category `M ≅ O ⊕ K_λ`, while in the overconvergent category the extension class of `M` is non-zero.
- At `s=p`, every term of `Σ_{n≥1}pⁿs^(−n)` is one, so it diverges; the rational function `p/(s−p)` has a pole. The strict inequality in the neighbourhood is necessary.

## Layer RD.4: Rigid cohomology, supports and comparison maps

This layer defines rigid cohomology and its variants before any finiteness statement: ordinary
cohomology `H_rig`, compact supports `H_c,rig`, closed supports `H_Z,rig`, with their functoriality,
excision and localisation sequences, Frobenius and its independence of the lift, finite étale
pushforward and finite flat base change. On a smooth affine it compares rigid cohomology with the
Monsky–Washnitzer de Rham cohomology of the dagger algebra, with or without Frobenius. It proves the
Gysin isomorphism for smooth closed pairs, builds log rigid cohomology with proper support for
semistable pairs, compares dagger and log dagger realisations with Berthelot's, and constructs the
constant-coefficient rigid–crystalline comparison map and its quasi-isomorphism for smooth proper
varieties, which the trace map of Layer RD.5 needs. It ends with Igusa theta cokernels.

<a id="rd-4-1"></a>

### RD.4.1 Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a `(σ,∇)`-module

**Definition.** For a `(σ,∇)`-module `M` over a dagger algebra A of MW-type, the Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology `Hⁱ(M)` is the `i`-th cohomology of the de Rham complex `0 → M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} → M ⊗ Ω^2_{A/K} → ⋯` with differentials `∇_i`. The Frobenius `F ⊗ ∧^i dσ` on `M ⊗ Ω^i` commutes with the differentials and induces a `σ_K`-semilinear endomorphism `F` of each `Hⁱ(M)` (K-linear when `σ_K = id`). `H⁰(M) = ker ∇` is the space of horizontal sections. When the special fibre of `A` has dimension one, `Ω^2_{A/K} = 0` and `H⁰(M) = ker ∇, H¹(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1), Hⁱ(M) = 0` for `i ≥ 2`. For `M = A` this is the cohomology `Hⁱ(A; K)` of Monsky–Washnitzer and van der Put.

*Hypotheses.* The output is a K-vector space with a semilinear endomorphism; no finite-dimensionality is built into the definition (it is [§RD.5.28](#rd-5-28), [§RD.5.39](#rd-5-39) and [§RD.5.76](#rd-5-76)).

The API:

- `SigmaNablaModule.mwH0`: `H⁰(M) = ker ∇` as a K-vector space (in general `Hⁱ(M)` for `i ∈ ℕ`).
- `SigmaNablaModule.mwH1`: `H¹(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1)` for curves (in general the `i`-th cohomology of the de Rham complex).
- `SigmaNablaModule.mwH1Frobenius`: The `σ_K`-semilinear endomorphism of `Hⁱ(M)` induced by `F ⊗ ∧^i dσ` (on `H¹` of a curve: `m ⊗ ω ↦ F(m) ⊗ μω`).
- `mwCohomology.map`: Morphisms of `(σ,∇)`-modules and pullbacks along Frobenius-compatible morphisms of dagger algebras induce maps on `Hⁱ; map_id` and `map_comp` hold and the maps commute with `F`.
- `SigmaNablaModule.mwCohomology_zero`: `H⁰(M) = ker ∇`, the horizontal sections.
- `mwCohomology_of_dim_one`: If the special fibre of `A` has dimension one then `H¹(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1)` and `Hⁱ(M) = 0` for `i ≥ 2`.
- `mwCohomology.frobenius_injective`: `F` is injective on each `Hⁱ(M)` (Kedlaya, Remark 3.4.4; [§RD.4.3](#rd-4-3)).
- `mwCohomology_trivial_zero`: If `Spec(A^int/πA^int)` is geometrically connected then `H⁰(A) = K` with `F = σ_K` (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 9.3.2, citing Monsky–Washnitzer, Theorem 7.1).

*Proof sketch.*

1. The de Rham complex is a cochain complex of K-vector spaces because `∇_{i+1} ∘ ∇_i = 0` (integrability); its cohomology is Mathlib's HomologicalComplex.homology of this complex.
2. The Frobenius of `M` and `∧^i dσ` give a morphism of complexes `σ^*(M ⊗ Ω^•) → M ⊗ Ω^•` by horizontality of `F`, hence the semilinear `F` on `Hⁱ(M)`.
3. In dimension one the complex has two terms, so `H⁰` and `H¹` are the kernel and cokernel of `∇`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Definition 3.4.1, p. 23; Put, *The cohomology of Monsky and Washnitzer*, Section 2.3, p. 36; Kedlaya, *Counting points on hyperelliptic curves using Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology*, Section 2, p. 3.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.28](#rd-3-28) *`(σ,∇)`-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *The module of (universally finite) differentials `Ω^1_A` of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivative*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product `A_1 ⊗†_B A_2`*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *Rational localisation `A⟨f/g⟩†` of a dagger algebra and its universal property*; Mathlib `HomologicalComplex.homology`; Mathlib `CochainComplex`; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *The overconvergent de Rham complex of a smooth dagger space, with coefficients in a module with integrable connection*.

**Checks.**

- `mwH1_multiplicativeGroup`: For `A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†` and `M = A`: the residue map `Σ a_n x^n dx/x ↦ a_0` induces an isomorphism `H¹(M) ≅ K`, and the standard Frobenius `σ(x) = x^q` acts on `H¹(M)` by multiplication by `q`.
- `mwH_affineLine`: For `A = K⟨x⟩†` and `M = A: H⁰(M) = K` (the constants) and `H¹(M) = 0`.
- `mwH_point`: For `A = K` (special fibre a point): `H⁰(M) = M` and `Hⁱ(M) = 0` for `i ≥ 1`.
- `mwH1_tateAlgebra_nonexample`: With the Tate algebra `K⟨x⟩` in place of `K⟨x⟩†` the cokernel of `d` is infinite dimensional: `Σ_n p^n x^{p^n − 1} dx` is a limit of exact forms but not exact; so the overconvergence in the definition cannot be dropped.
- For `A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†` and `M = A, H¹(M)` is one-dimensional, spanned by `dx/x`, and the standard Frobenius `x ↦ x^q` acts by `q`.
- For `A = K⟨x⟩†` and `M = A, H⁰(M) = K` and `H¹(M) = 0`.

### RD.4.2 The trace map on de Rham complexes for a finite flat morphism of dagger algebras

**Construction.** Let `f: R → S` be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with `S` finite and locally free of constant degree `n` over `R`. There is an `R`-linear morphism of complexes Tr: `Ω^•_{S/K} → Ω^•_{R/K}` with `Tr ∘ f = n·id` and `Tr(ω ∧ η) = ω ∧ Tr(η)` for `ω ∈ Ω^•_{R/K}, η ∈ Ω^•_{S/K}`; in degree 0 it is the algebra trace `S → R`.

*Hypotheses.*

- `R` and `S` are dagger algebras of MW-type (Monsky–Washnitzer's proof uses that dagger algebras are noetherian; Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
- `S` is finite and locally free over `R` of constant `rank n`.

The API:

- `deRhamTrace`: The `R`-linear morphism of complexes Tr: `Ω^•_{S/K} → Ω^•_{R/K}`.
- `deRhamTrace_comp_map`: `Tr ∘ f = n·id` on `Ω^•_{R/K}`.
- `deRhamTrace_wedge`: `Tr(ω ∧ η) = ω ∧ Tr(η)` (projection formula).
- `deRhamTrace_zero`: In degree 0, Tr is Mathlib's Algebra.trace `R S`.
- `deRhamTrace_frobenius`: For an étale morphism of the smooth reductions, compatible lifts give a cartesian relative Frobenius square, and trace commutes with Frobenius through finite-projective base change. Compatibility alone for a finite flat map does not suffice.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Over the fraction fields, `Ω^1_{S/K} ⊗ Frac(S) = Ω^1_{R/K} ⊗ Frac(S)` because `Frac(S)/Frac(R)` is finite separable (characteristic 0); define Tr on `Ω^i ⊗ Frac(S)` as the field trace `Frac(S) → Frac(R)` tensored with `Ω^i_{R/K}` (van der Put, Proposition 3.1).
2. Show Tr maps `Ω^i_{S/K}` into `Ω^i_{R/K}`: since `Ω^i_{R/K}` is projective and `R` normal, it suffices to check at height-one primes, where it follows from the discriminant description of differentials (van der Put, proof of Proposition 3.1, citing `R`. Berger).
3. Tr commutes with `d` because the field trace commutes with the derivation of the separable extension; `Tr ∘ f = n` and the projection formula hold by construction.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Proposition 3.2.6, p. 21; Put, *The cohomology of Monsky and Washnitzer*, Proposition 3.1, p. 38.

*Needs:* AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *The module of (universally finite) differentials `Ω^1_A` of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivative*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product `A_1 ⊗†_B A_2`*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *Rational localisation `A⟨f/g⟩†` of a dagger algebra and its universal property*; Mathlib `Algebra.trace`.

**Checks.**

- `deRhamTrace_degree_one`: For `f = id`, Tr is the identity.
- `deRhamTrace_frobenius_power`: For `S = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†` over `R = K⟨y,y^{-1}⟩† (y = x^q): Tr(1) = q, Tr(dx/x) = dy/y`, and `Tr(x^m dx/x) = 0` if `q ∤ m`.
- `deRhamTrace_algebraTrace`: In degree 0 the map agrees with Mathlib's Algebra.trace for the finite free extension.
- `deRhamTrace_not_retraction`: `Tr ∘ f` is multiplication by `n`, not the identity, when `n > 1`; dividing by `n` is what makes `Hⁱ(M)` a direct summand of `Hⁱ(f^*M)`.
- `deRhamTrace_frobenius_compatibility_nonexample`: For `y = x^q, σ_R(y) = y^q` and `σ_S(x) = x^q, Tr(σ_S(x)) = qy` but `σ_R(Tr(x)) = 0` for `q > 1`. The generic-fibre map is finite étale on `G_m`, but its reduction is radicial, so compatibility alone does not make trace commute with Frobenius.
- For `S = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†` over `R = K⟨y,y^{-1}⟩†` with `y = x^q: Tr(dx/x) = dy/y` and `Tr(1) = q`.
- On the affine disc with `y = x^q, Tr(dx) = 0` for `q > 1` and `Tr(x^{q−1}dx) = dy; dx/x` is not a regular form there.

<a id="rd-4-3"></a>

### RD.4.3 Cohomology injects under finite flat pullback, and Frobenius is injective on cohomology

**Lemma.** Let `f: R → S` be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with `S` finite locally free of constant positive `rank n` over `R`, and `σ` a Frobenius lift on `S` preserving `R`. For every `(σ,∇)`-module `M` over `R`, the map `Hⁱ(M) → Hⁱ(f^*M)` is injective and its image is the image of the canonical projector `(1/n)·f ∘` Tr on `Hⁱ(f^*M), n = deg(S/R)`. For a finite projective injective extension of varying rank, split `Spec R` into its constant-rank open-and-closed components and use the reciprocal of each positive rank on that component. In particular (applying trace to the relative Frobenius linearisation `A ⊗_{K,σ_K} K → A`, which is finite flat over the smooth reduction) the Frobenius `F` is injective on each `Hⁱ(M)`.

*Hypotheses.*

- `R, S` of MW-type (or one of the two Robba-ring situations of Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
- Constant positive `rank n`; characteristic 0, so `n` is invertible in `K`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Tensor the trace Tr: `Ω^•_S → Ω^•_R` ([§RD.4.2](#rd-4-2)) with `M` to get `Hⁱ(f^*M) → Hⁱ(M)` whose composite with `Hⁱ(M) → Hⁱ(f^*M)` is multiplication by `n`.
2. Since `n ≠ 0` in `K`, the first map is injective and `(1/n) f ∘` Tr is a projector onto its image.
3. Factor Frobenius into coefficient extension along `σ_K`, which is faithfully flat, followed by the finite-flat relative Frobenius lift of [§RD.0.42](#rd-0-42). Trace gives injection for the latter, and the Frobenius structure identifies the pullback module with `M`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Proposition 3.4.3, p. 24, and Remark 3.4.4, p. 24.

*Needs:* [§RD.4.2](#rd-4-2) *The trace map on de Rham complexes for a finite flat morphism of dagger algebras*; [§RD.4.1](#rd-4-1) *Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a `(σ,∇)`-module*; [§RD.0.42](#rd-0-42) *Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth `O_K`-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)*.

**Checks.**

- For `f = id, n = 1` and the trace projector is the identity.
- For `R = K × K` and `S = K × K × K` with `f(a,b) = (a,b,b)`, `Tr ∘ f = diag(1,2)` on `H⁰(R)`; no single scalar normalises it. Componentwise ranks 1 and 2 give a projector with the specified image.
- For `S = K⟨x⟩†` over `R = K⟨x^q⟩†, H¹(R) = 0 = H¹(S)`, and on `K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†` the Frobenius `q` on `H¹` is injective.

<a id="rd-4-4"></a>

### RD.4.4 Finite étale pushforward preserves Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology

**Theorem.** (a) For a finite étale morphism `f:R→S` of dagger algebras and a finite projective `S`-module `M` with integrable connection, restriction of scalars gives a finite projective `R`-module with connection and a canonical identity of de Rham complexes, hence `Hⁱ(M) ≅ Hⁱ(f_*M)` for every `i`. (b) Suppose also that `R,S` are the rational weak completions of smooth integral models and `f` lifts a finite étale map of their smooth special fibres. With compatible Frobenius lifts and invertible horizontal Frobenius on `M`, the induced Frobenius on `f_*M` has invertible linearisation, and the cohomology identity is F-equivariant. More generally this Frobenius assertion holds under (a) whenever the relative map `β:S⊗_{R,σ_R}R→S, s⊗r↦σ_S(s)f(r)` is an isomorphism. (c) Under the geometric model hypotheses of (b), finite étale pushforward also preserves Taylor overconvergence for coefficients without Frobenius, and the cohomology identification holds with compact supports.

*Hypotheses.* Generic-fibre finite étaleness suffices for (a). In (b) invertibility of `β` is required; finite étaleness of the integral models supplies it by RD.3.39. Part (c) uses finite étaleness of the smooth special-fibre map and its compatible weak lifts.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Because `f` is étale, `S⊗_R Ωⁱ_{R/K}≅Ωⁱ_{S/K}`; tensoring with `M` identifies the de Rham complexes.
2. In (b), RD.3.39 identifies the relative Frobenius map `β` with an isomorphism. It identifies `σ_R^*(f_*M)` with `f_*(σ_S^*M)`; restriction of the invertible linearised Frobenius on `M` then gives invertible Frobenius on `f_*M`. The differential identity intertwines these structures.
3. Étale base change of differential modules uses Mathlib’s `tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale` and Tau Ceti’s basis transport. For (c), extend the finite special-fibre map to compatible compactifications and cofinal strict neighbourhoods as in RD.3.41. Finite pushforward is coherent and exact on these analytic pieces; transporting the Taylor isomorphism gives Taylor overconvergence. Proper pushforward along the finite map identifies the supported complexes. The algebraic identity of differentials alone supplies only (a).

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Proposition 3.4.5, p. 24; Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, *Cohomological descent of rigid cohomology for étale coverings*, §§7.3–7.4, pp. 148–152, and Theorem 9.1.1, p. 168.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.39](#rd-3-39) *Relative Frobenius and differentials for étale weak lifts*; [§RD.3.41](#rd-3-41) *Finite étale pushforward on frames and coefficients*; [§RD.4.1](#rd-4-1) *Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a `(σ,∇)`-module*; AdicSpacesPartIV §§F1.2–F1.4 *Dagger algebras, fringe presentations and tensor products*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *Differentials of dagger algebras*.

**Checks.**

- Pushing the trivial module forward along `y=x^N` on `K⟨x,x⁻¹⟩†`, with `p∤N` and standard compatible Frobenius lifts, gives a rank-`N` Frobenius module with `H¹` one-dimensional; its special-fibre map is finite étale.
- For `f=id`, both complexes and their Frobenius structures are identical. For a disjoint union of two identity covers the pushforward and cohomology are the direct sums of two copies.
- For `R=ℚ_p⟨y,y⁻¹⟩†`, `S=ℚ_p⟨x,x⁻¹⟩†`, `y=x^p` and `σ_R(y)=y^p, σ_S(x)=x^p`, the generic map is finite étale but its reduction is inseparable. For `M=S` with trivial connection and Frobenius `σ_S`, the `R`-basis `1,x,…,x^(p−1)` maps to `1,y,…,y^(p−1)` in `R·1`, so the linearisation has rank one. Part (a) holds, while (b) excludes this failure of invertibility.

### RD.4.5 Berthelot's functor `j†` and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame

**Construction.** Use the functor `j†` of [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) and its strict-neighbourhood realization of [§RD.3.7](#rd-3-7). For `E ∈ Isoc†(X,Y/K)` realised by `E_V` with integrable connection on a strict neighbourhood `V` of `]X[_P`, define `DR†(E) = j†(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V)`. Its hypercohomology on `]Y[_P` is the frame cohomology `Hⁱ((X,Y,P)/K,E)`. For a morphism of frames `u`, pullback of coefficients and differential forms gives a canonical derived morphism `DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P′}(u^*E)`, compatible with composition.

*Hypotheses.*

- Strict neighbourhoods in Berthelot's sense ([§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3)); the colimit may be taken over any cofinal system, for instance the `U'_λ =` {`x ∈ ]Y[` : some `|f_i(x)| ≥ λ`}, `f_i` lifting equations of `Z, λ → 1^`-.
- The frame need not have `Y` proper for `DR†(E)` and frame cohomology; properness of `Y` is imposed in [§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10).

The API:

- `cohomology_jDagger`: `H^*(]Y[, j†F) = H^*(V, j†F)` for any strict neighbourhood `V` (Berthelot (2.5) a)).
- `overconvergentDeRham`: The complex `DR†(E) = j†(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V)` of sheaves of K-vector spaces on `]Y[_P`.
- `frameCohomology`: `Hⁱ((X,Y,P)/K, E) := Hⁱ(]Y[_P, DR†(E))`, the hypercohomology.
- `overconvergentDeRham.map`: For a morphism of frames `u`, the canonical morphism `DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P'}(u^*E)` of (2.2.1); compatible with composition of frame morphisms.
- `overconvergentDeRham_affine`: If `Y` is the closure of a smooth affine `X` with a smooth lift, the global sections of `DR†(E)` form the de Rham complex `M_E ⊗ Ω^•_A` of the dagger algebra ([§RD.3.32](#rd-3-32)).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Define `j†F` as the colimit of `j_{V*}j_V^{-1}F`; since the strict neighbourhoods form a filtered system, `j†` is an exact functor on sheaves of abelian groups (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Proposition 2.7.2).
2. `j†F` depends only on the restriction of `F` to any strict neighbourhood `V`, and `H^*(]Y[, j†F) = H^*(V, j†F)` (Berthelot (2.5) a)).
3. For `E` realised on `V` with connection `∇` ([§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13)), `E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V` is a complex of sheaves on `V` (differential forms on the rigid space `V`, supplied by AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.36); apply `j†`.
4. For a morphism of frames `u`, the canonical maps `j†F → u_*j'†u^{-1}F` composed with `u^{-1}Ω^•_{]Y[_P} → Ω^•_{]Y'[_{P'}}` and an injective resolution give (2.2.1).

*Sources.* Berthelot, *Géométrie rigide et cohomologie des variétés algébriques de caractéristique `p`*, (2.2), pp. 16–17, and (2.5) a), p. 19; Kedlaya, *Finiteness of rigid cohomology with coefficients*, Definition 4.3.1, p. 27; Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Section 2.2, p. 12.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.1](#rd-3-1) *Frames `(X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)`*; [§RD.3.2](#rd-3-2) *The tube `]T[_P` of a locally closed subscheme*; [§RD.3.3](#rd-3-3) *Strict neighbourhoods of `]X[` in `]Y[`*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.2 *Dagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebra*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.3 *The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modules*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.9 *The module of (universally finite) differentials `Ω^1_A` of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivative*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product `A_1 ⊗†_B A_2`*; AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.4 *Rational localisation `A⟨f/g⟩†` of a dagger algebra and its universal property*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid generic fibre*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.3 *The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field*; AdicSpacesPartIII §R2.4 *Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf`; Mathlib `DerivedCategory`; [§RD.3.4](#rd-3-4) *Berthelot's functor `j†` of overconvergent sections*; [§RD.3.7](#rd-3-7) *Exactness of `j†` on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of `j_{λ*}`*.

**Checks.**

- `jDagger_of_proper`: If `X = Y` then `j†F = F` for every sheaf `F`, and `DR†(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}`.
- `jDagger_affineLine_sections`: For the frame `(A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_{O_K}): Γ`(`]P^1[, j†O`) is the ring `K⟨x⟩†` of power series converging on some disc `|x| ≤ ρ` with `ρ > 1`.
- `jDagger_restrict_tube`: For every sheaf `F` on `]Y[_P, (j†F)|]X[_P = F|]X[_P`, and the natural map `F → j†F` is the unit of the restriction to strict neighbourhoods.
- `convergent_deRham_affineLine_nonexample`: Without `j†`, the de Rham complex of the closed unit disc `]A^1[ = Sp K⟨x⟩` has infinite-dimensional `H¹` (Berthelot (1.5), Remarque), so `DR†` cannot be replaced by the de Rham complex of the tube.
- If `X = Y` (`Z` empty) then `j† = id` and `DR†(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}`.
- For `X = A^1_k ⊂ Y = P^1_k ⊂ P = P̂^1: Γ(]Y[, j†O) = K⟨x⟩†`, series converging on some disc `|x| ≤ ρ` with `ρ > 1`.
