### RD.6.58 p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals

**Definition.** An element `α ∈ K^alg` has slope `s ∈ Q` if `|α| = |q^s|`, i.e. `v_q(α) := v_p(α)/v_p(q) = s`. An overconvergent F-isocrystal `E` on an `𝔽_q`-scheme `X` has slopes in `[r, s]` if for every closed point `x` of degree `d` the eigenvalues of `F_x` on `E_x` have slopes in [dr, ds]. For an endomorphism, take the Newton slopes of its characteristic polynomial ([§RD.1.35](#rd-1-35)) using `v_p`, then divide by `a = v_p(q)`; if the polygon uses `v_π`, divide instead by `e · a`, where `e = v_π(p)`.

*Hypotheses.* `K^alg` with its p-adic absolute value extending that of `K`; `q = p^a`, `a > 0`, and `e = v_π(p) > 0`.

The API:

- `slope`: `v_q(α) := v_p(α)/v_p(q)` for `α ∈ (K^alg)^×`.
- `HasSlopesIn`: `E` has slopes in `[r, s]` (pointwise, normalised by degree).
- `slope_mul`: slope`(αβ) =` slope `α +` slope `β`; slope`(q) = 1`.
- `hasSlopesIn_tateTwist`: `E(n)` has slopes in `[r − n, s − n]` iff `E` has slopes in `[r, s]`.
- `slopes_eq_newton`: The slopes per degree at `x` are the `v_p`-Newton slopes of `F_x` divided by `a · deg x`; for `v_π`-Newton slopes divide by `e · a · deg x`.
- `hasSlopesIn_const`: `O_X` has slopes in [0, 0].

*Proof sketch.* Slopes of eigenvalues are read off the Newton polygon of the characteristic polynomial ([§RD.1.35](#rd-1-35)); the normalisation divides p-adic valuations by `a = v_p(q)` and uniformiser valuations by `e · a`. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.7, p. 52; *Slope filtrations revisited*, Remark 2.1.11, p. 7.)

*Needs:* [§RD.1.35](#rd-1-35) *Frobenius slopes and Newton (HN) polygons of `σ`-modules: generic slopes over `E` and `R^bd`, special slopes over `R`*; [§RD.6.2](#rd-6-2) *Fibres and the linear Frobenius at a closed point*; Mathlib `padicValRat`.

**Checks.**

- `slope_ordinary`: For `T^2 − 3T + 7` over `𝔽_7` the roots have slopes 0 and 1 (the Newton polygon at 7 has slopes 0 and 1).
- `slope_supersingular`: For `T^2 + 7` over `𝔽_7` both roots have slope 1/2.
- `slope_const`: `O_X` has slopes in [0, 0].
- Ramified coefficients `π² = p`, `q = p`: a `π`-eigenline has `v_π`-slope 1 and `q`-slope `1/2`. For `q = p²` the same eigenline has `q`-slope `1/4`.
- `slope_not_weight`: Slope and weight differ: the roots of `T^2 − 3T + 7` both have complex absolute value `√7` (weight 1) but slopes 0 and 1; slope is not determined by weight.
- Ordinary elliptic curve over `𝔽_7 (a_7 = 3)`: slopes 0 and 1 on `H¹`; supersingular `(a_7 = 0)`: slopes 1/2, 1/2.

<a id="rd-6-59"></a>

### RD.6.59 Constant rank-one F-isocrystals (twists)

**Definition.** Let `X` be a separated `𝔽_q`-scheme of finite type with structure map `f : X → Spec 𝔽_q, K` with residue field `𝔽_q` and `σ_K = id`, and `c ∈ K^×`. The constant F-line `L_c` on `X` is `f^*` of the rank-one object `(K, c)` on `Spec 𝔽_q`: the unit isocrystal `O_X` with Frobenius structure `c·Φ_O`, where `Φ_O : F^*O_X ≅ O_X` is the canonical one. For `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K)` write `E(c) := E ⊗ L_c` (Abe's 'twist by `χ'`). Tate twists are the special case `L_{q^{-n}} = O_X(n)` ([§RD.6.3](#rd-6-3)). For `c` in a finite extension `K'` of `K, L_c` is defined after extending scalars to `K'`.

*Hypotheses.* `σ_K = id` (so the linear `q`-Frobenius is defined, [§RD.6.1](#rd-6-1)); `c ∈ K^×` or in a finite extension `K'`.

The API:

- `constantFLine`: `L_c := f^*(K, c)` for `c ∈ K^×`.
- `constantFLine_fibreFrobenius`: `F_x(L_c) = c^{deg x}` at every closed point `x`.
- `constantFLine_mul`: `L_c ⊗ L_d ≅ L_{cd}, L_1 ≅ O_X` and `L_c^∨ ≅ L_{c^{-1}}`.
- `constantFLine_tate`: `L_{q^{-n}} ≅ O_X(n)`, the Tate twist of [§RD.6.3](#rd-6-3).
- `twist_cohomology`: `Hⁱ_{rig}(X/K, E(c)) ≅ Hⁱ_{rig}(X/K, E)` with linear Frobenius multiplied by `c`, and likewise with compact supports.
- `constantFLine_iso_iff`: For `X` geometrically connected and nonempty, `L_c ≅ L_d` iff `c = d` (compare Frobenius on `H⁰_rig = K`).
- `constantFLine_pullback`: `g^*L_c ≅ L_c` for every `𝔽_q`-morphism `g : Y → X`.

*Proof sketch.* Pullback along `f` of the object `(K, c)` of F-`Isoc†(Spec 𝔽_q/K)`, which is a one-dimensional K-space with linear Frobenius `c` ([§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) over a point). Tensor products of F-isocrystals multiply Frobenius structures, so `(E ⊗ L_c)` has Frobenius `Φ_E ⊗ c` and `L_c ⊗ L_d = L_{cd}`. (Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Section 6, definition of a twist and of `E(χ)`, and Remark 6.2 (ii), p. 7; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Lemma 9.14 and Corollary 9.15, p. 25; Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proofs of Theorem 6.5.1 and Theorem 6.6.2, pp. 48 and 50.)

*Needs:* [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.3](#rd-6-3) *Tate twists of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.1](#rd-6-1) *The linear `q`-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over `𝔽_q`*; [§RD.6.2](#rd-6-2) *Fibres and the linear Frobenius at a closed point*; [§RD.4.18](#rd-4-18) *The Frobenius on rigid cohomology*.

**Checks.**

- `constantFLine_point_frobenius`: On `X = Spec 𝔽_{q^2}` (a point of degree 2 over `𝔽_q`) and `c = 3, F_x(L_3) = 9`.
- `constantFLine_one`: `L_1 = O_X`.
- `constantFLine_tate_compat`: `L_q = O_X(−1)`: on `H²_{c,rig}(A^1/K) ≅ K(−1)` the twisted Frobenius of `O ⊗ L_q` is `q^2`, that of `O_X(−1) ⊗ O = q·q`.
- `constantFLine_not_unit_iso`: For `c ≠ 1, L_c` ≇ `O_X` on a geometrically connected `X`: Frobenius on `H⁰_rig(X/K, L_c) = K` is `c`, not 1, although `L_c` and `O_X` have the same underlying isocrystal.
- At a closed point `x` of degree `d, F_x(L_c) = c^d`.
- `L_1 = O_X` and `L_q = O_X(−1)`.
- Cohomology: `Hⁱ_{(c),rig}(X/K, E(c)) = Hⁱ_{(c),rig}(X/K, E)` with Frobenius multiplied by `c`.

<a id="rd-6-60"></a>

### RD.6.60 A rank-one F-isocrystal is isoclinic and a constant twist makes it unit-root

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a connected smooth `𝔽_q`-scheme and `E` a convergent or overconvergent F-isocrystal of rank 1 on `X/K (σ_K = id)`. There is `s ∈ Q` such that at every closed point `x` the eigenvalue of `F_x` has `q`-adic valuation `v_q = v_p/v_p(q)` equal to `s·deg(x)`. Hence, after replacing `K` by a finite extension containing an element `c` of `q`-adic valuation `s, E(c^{-1}) = E ⊗ L_{c^{-1}}` is unit-root (slope 0 at every point).

*Hypotheses.* `X` connected and smooth over `𝔽_q` (rank-one specialisation needs only connectedness and the constancy of the endpoint of the Newton polygon).

*Proof sketch.* Grothendieck specialisation: the Newton polygon at a specialisation lies above that at the generisation, with the same endpoint ([§RD.2.3](#rd-2-3) in the local form; Crew 1992 Proposition 1.2 globally). For rank 1 the polygon is a single segment whose endpoint is its slope, so the slope is the same at every point. Choose `c` in a finite extension of `K` with `v_q(c) = s` (a root in `K^alg` of a suitable power of `q`, so a finite extension suffices); then `F_x(E(c^{-1})) = F_x(E)·c^{-deg x}` has valuation 0 ([§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59)). (Crew, *F-isocrystals and their monodromy groups*, Proposition 1.2, p. 433; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Remark 3.5, p. 6; Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Proof of Lemma 6.1 `(i)`, p. 7.)

*Needs:* [§RD.2.3](#rd-2-3) *The special Newton polygon lies above the generic one, with the same endpoint*; [§RD.6.58](#rd-6-58) *p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals*; [§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59) *Constant rank-one F-isocrystals (twists)*; [§RD.1.36](#rd-1-36) *Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root `σ`-modules over `R, R^bd` and `E`*.

**Checks.**

- The Tate object `O(−1)` has slope 1; `O(−1)(q^{-1}) = O` is unit-root.
- The Dwork isocrystal `L_π` is unit-root (Frobenius at points is a root of unity), `s = 0`.

<a id="rd-6-61"></a>

### RD.6.61 Unit-root F-isocrystals and p-adic representations (Katz, Crew, Tsuzuki)

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically connected `𝔽_q`-scheme with `K` of residue field `𝔽_q` and `σ_K = id`, and fix a geometric point `x̄`. (a) (Katz, Crew; [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) with its `Q_q`-coefficients extended to `K`) There is an equivalence of tensor categories between continuous representations `ρ : π_1(X, x̄) → GL_n(K)` (each stabilises an `O_K`-lattice, `π_1` being compact) and unit-root convergent F-isocrystals ([§RD.3.47](#rd-3-47)) on `X/K`; under it, at a closed point `x` the linear Frobenius `F_x` is conjugate to `ρ(Frob_x)` for the geometric Frobenius `Frob_x`. (b) (Tsuzuki) When `X` is a curve with smooth compactification `X̄`, a unit-root convergent F-isocrystal is overconvergent along `X̄ − X` if and only if `ρ` has finite local monodromy, i.e. `ρ(I_y)` is finite for the inertia group `I_y` at every `y ∈ X̄ − X`; for rank one this is due to Crew. The functor in (b) is fully faithful and its essential image is closed under subquotients.

*Hypotheses.*

- `X` smooth and geometrically connected over `𝔽_q`; in (b) `X` is a curve.
- Inertia groups at the points at infinity and the arithmetic/geometric fundamental-group sequence are taken from EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§`F`.0.2, `F`.0.A2 and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.1.2.

*Proof sketch.*

1. (a) For `K = Q_q` this is [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) (`k = 𝔽_q, q`-power Frobenius structures, which are `Q_q`-linear): `V ↦ (V ⊗ O, 1 ⊗ σ)`, with quasi-inverse the Frobenius-fixed horizontal sections (Katz; Crew 1992 Theorem 1.3). For a finite extension `K` of `Q_q` with `σ_K = id`, apply it to the underlying `Q_q`-objects with their K-action, as in Kedlaya's Notes Theorem 9.4. Normalisation: over `Spec 𝔽_q` the quasi-inverse is `V = (M ⊗ K̂^ur)^{F ⊗ σ = 1}`, on which the arithmetic Frobenius acts as `1 ⊗ σ = F^{-1} ⊗ 1`, so `F_x` is `ρ` of the geometric Frobenius; this normalisation is checked on `Spec 𝔽_q` as above.
2. (b) is local at the points at infinity: on the Robba ring at `y`, a unit-root `(σ, ∇)`-module over the bounded Robba ring has finite local monodromy by [§RD.2.27](#rd-2-27), and [§RD.2.26](#rd-2-26) (b) identifies such modules with the representations of the local Galois group with finite local monodromy; conversely finite local monodromy means the module is quasi-constant at `y`, hence overconvergent by [§RD.2.17](#rd-2-17).
3. Full faithfulness of (b) follows from (a) since overconvergent morphisms are in particular convergent ones and the restriction functor is faithful ([§RD.5.8](#rd-5-8) covers the unit-root case).

*Sources.* Crew, *F-isocrystals and their monodromy groups*, Theorems 1.3 and 1.4, p. 434; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorems 3.7 and 3.9, pp. 6-7, and Theorem 9.4, p. 22.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.37](#rd-3-37) *Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.5.8](#rd-5-8) *Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem: overconvergent F-isocrystals embed fully faithfully into convergent ones*; [§RD.2.27](#rd-2-27) *Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root `(σ,∇)`-modules have finite local monodromy*; [§RD.2.17](#rd-2-17) *Quasi-unipotent `∇`-modules are overconvergent*; [§RD.1.36](#rd-1-36) *Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root `σ`-modules over `R, R^bd` and `E`*; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§`F`.0.2, `F`.0.A2 and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.1.2; [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) *Katz–Crew: unit-root F-isocrystals are lisse p-adic sheaves*; [§RD.3.47](#rd-3-47) *Unit-root F-isocrystals*; [§RD.2.26](#rd-2-26) *Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root `(σ,∇)`-modules over `E†` have finite local monodromy, and correspond to representations with finite local monodromy*.

**Checks.**

- The trivial representation corresponds to `O_X`.
- The Artin–Schreier character of `u^p − u = x` on `π_1(A^1)` (finite image, wildly ramified at `∞` with finite inertia image) corresponds to the Dwork isocrystal `L_π`, which is overconvergent.
- A p-adic character of `π_1(G_m)` of infinite image on inertia at `∞` (e.g. from the `ℤ_p`-extension of Artin–Schreier–Witt type) gives a unit-root convergent F-isocrystal that is not overconvergent.

<a id="rd-6-62"></a>

### RD.6.62 Geometric class field theory for curves over finite fields

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over `𝔽_q`, with Jacobian `J`, and `x̄` a geometric point. (a) Every connected finite abelian étale cover of `X ⊗ 𝔽̄_q` is pulled back from an étale isogeny onto `J` along an Abel–Jacobi map over `𝔽̄_q`. (b) The Frobenius coinvariants of `π_1^ab(X ⊗ 𝔽̄_q)` are `J(𝔽_q)`, hence finite. Geometric and arithmetic Frobenius give the same coinvariants.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth, proper and geometrically connected over a finite field; an Abel–Jacobi base point exists over `𝔽̄_q` and after a finite extension of `𝔽_q`.

*Proof sketch.* The Abel–Jacobi map identifies the geometric abelian fundamental groups of `X` and `J`; connected finite abelian étale covers therefore come from étale isogenies of `J`. On the inverse limit of the étale torsion groups of `J`, taking coinvariants under Frobenius gives the kernel of `1−F` on `J`, namely `J(𝔽_q)`. Lang's theorem makes `1−F` an isogeny, so its kernel is finite; replacing `F` by `F⁻¹` leaves its image subgroup unchanged.

*Sources.* Serre, *Groupes algébriques et corps de classes*, Hermann (1959), Chapitres `V`–VI (proper curves and Jacobians); Katz–Lang, *Finiteness theorems in geometric classfield theory*, Enseign. Math. (2) 27 (1981), 285–319, Theorem 1 and §§1–2.

*Needs:* ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.3.7 (Lang’s theorem); TauCetiRoadmap JacobianChallenge Layer `F`; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§`F`.0.2, `F`.0.A2 and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.1.2.

**Checks.**

- `X = P^1: J = 0, π_1^ab(P^1 ⊗ 𝔽̄_q) = 0`, coinvariants trivial.
- `X` an elliptic curve `E: π_1^ab(E ⊗ 𝔽̄_q) = ∏_ℓ T_ℓE` (with the p-part from the étale p-torsion), and the Frobenius coinvariants are `E(𝔽_q)`, of order `q + 1 − a`.
- Properness is necessary: on `G_m/𝔽_p` the Artin–Schreier covers `y^p−y=t^m` for positive `m` prime to `p` give infinitely many independent Frobenius-invariant `𝔽_p`-characters of the geometric group. Its Frobenius coinvariants are therefore infinite.

<a id="rd-6-63"></a>

### RD.6.63 Katz–Lang finiteness of the geometric abelian fundamental group

**Theorem.** Let `X̄` be a smooth proper geometrically connected scheme over a finite field `𝔽_q`. Then the image of `π_1(X̄ ⊗ F̄_q)^ab` in `π_1(X̄)^ab` is finite. In particular, every continuous character of `π_1(X̄)` is of finite order on the geometric fundamental group.

*Hypotheses.* `X̄` smooth, proper and geometrically connected over `𝔽_q` (Katz–Lang allow the perfection of an absolutely finitely generated field).

*Proof sketch.* For a curve `X̄` with Jacobian `J` (Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge, Layer `F`: Abel–Jacobi and its universal property), abelian étale covers of `X̄ ⊗ F̄_q` are pulled back from isogenies onto `J`; a character of the arithmetic group `π_1(X̄)` restricts on the geometric part to a Frobenius-invariant character, which factors through the Frobenius coinvariants of the geometric abelian group, and these are finite because `1 −` Frobenius is an isogeny of `J` with kernel `J(𝔽_q)` (Lang). The general case is Katz–Lang, Theorem 1, as restated by Crew 1992 Theorem 1.6; the curve case above is the one used in [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66). The identification of geometric abelian covers with isogenies of the Jacobian (geometric class field theory for curves over `𝔽_q`) is [§RD.6.62](#rd-6-62). (Crew, *F-isocrystals and their monodromy groups*, Theorem 1.6 and the proof of Corollary 1.5, pp. 434-435; Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Proof of Lemma 6.1 `(i)`, p. 7.)

*Needs:* EtaleCohomologyFoundations §§`F`.0.2, `F`.0.A2 and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups §IG.1.2; TauCetiRoadmap JacobianChallenge Layer `F`; [§RD.6.62](#rd-6-62) *Geometric class field theory for curves over finite fields*.

**Checks.**

- For `X̄ = P^1, π_1(P^1 ⊗ F̄_q)` is trivial and the image is trivial.
- For an elliptic curve `E/𝔽_q` the image of the geometric abelian fundamental group in `π_1(E)^ab` is isomorphic to `E(𝔽_q)` (the kernel of Lang's isogeny `1 −` Frobenius), a finite group of order `q + 1 − a_q`.

<a id="rd-6-64"></a>

### RD.6.64 Neutral Tannakian recognition theorem

**Theorem.** Let `K` be a field in a fixed universe, `(C, ⊗)` an essentially small K-linear rigid abelian symmetric monoidal category in that universe with `End(1) = K`, and `ω : C → Vec_K` an exact faithful K-linear symmetric monoidal functor (a fibre functor; `(C, ω)` is a neutral Tannakian category). Then (a) the functor on commutative K-algebras `S ↦ Aut^⊗(ω ⊗ S)` is represented by an affine group scheme `G = Spec(B)` over `K`; (b) `ω` lifts to an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories `C ≃ Rep_K(G)` compatible with the fibre functors, where `Rep_K(G)` is the category of finite-dimensional comodules over `B` (Tau Ceti's FGComoduleCat `K B`); (c) if `C` has a tensor generator `X` (every object is a subquotient of a finite sum of `X^{⊗a} ⊗ (X^∨)^{⊗b}`), then `G` is of finite type and `ω(X)` is a faithful representation, so `G` is a closed subgroup of `GL(ω(X))`.


This application adapter uses MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles §§6.1–6.3 for recognition and the
tensor-generator criterion. It supplies the finite-comodule and fibre comparison used in
[§RD.5.112a](#rd-5-112a), independently of the layer numbering.

*Hypotheses.*

- `K` any field; `C` essentially small in the coefficient universe, rigid abelian with `End(1) = K; ω` takes values in finite-dimensional vector spaces in that universe and is exact, faithful, K-linear and symmetric monoidal.
- The pinned Tau Ceti library supplies finite comodules over a coalgebra (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FGComoduleCat`), their symmetric and rigid monoidal structure over a commutative Hopf algebra over a field (`TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.instSymmetricCategory`, `TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.instRigidCategory`) and reconstruction from a given Hopf algebra (`TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor`: its points are the tensor automorphisms of scalar extension on its finite comodules, naturally in the value algebra).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Apply MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles §§6.1–6.2 to `(C, ω)`. Identify its finite right comodules over the supplied commutative Hopf algebra `B` with Tau Ceti's FGComoduleCat `K B`, preserving the symmetric tensor structure, duals and the marked fibre functor by a monoidal natural isomorphism.
2. Transport Tau Ceti's reconstruction TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor along this equivalence. For every commutative K-algebra `S`, this identifies the points of `G = Spec B` with `Aut^⊗(ω ⊗ S)`, compatibly with scalar extension in `S` and with the supplied representation equivalence.
3. Apply MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles §6.3 to the tensor generator `X`. The resulting representation on `ω(X)` gives the finite-type closed embedding in (c).

*Sources.* Deligne–Milne, *Tannakian categories*, Theorem 2.11, p. 21, with Lemma 2.13 and Propositions 2.14 and 2.16, pp. 22-24, and Definition 2.19 and Propositions 2.20-2.21, p. 25.

*Needs:* MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles §§6.1–6.3 *Neutral reconstruction, generation and finite type*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FGComoduleCat`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.instSymmetricCategory`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.instRigidCategory`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.RightRigidCategory`; Mathlib `FDRep`.

**Checks.**

- `C =` FGComoduleCat `K H` for a commutative Hopf algebra `H`, with the forgetful functor, recovers `G = Spec H` (TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor).
- For a finite group `Γ, Rep_K(Γ)` with the forgetful functor gives the constant group scheme `Γ` (compare Mathlib's Tannaka duality for finite groups, TannakaDuality.FiniteGroup).
- The category of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces with a nilpotent endomorphism (char `K = 0`) gives `G_a`.

<a id="rd-6-65"></a>

### RD.6.65 The tensor category generated by an overconvergent isocrystal is neutral Tannakian

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically connected `𝔽_q`-scheme (a curve, or more generally smooth), `x ∈ X(𝔽_q)`, and `M ∈ Isoc†(X/K)` (no Frobenius). Let `⟨M⟩` be the full subcategory of `Isoc†(X/K)` of objects isomorphic to subquotients of finite direct sums of `M^{⊗a} ⊗ (M^∨)^{⊗b}`, and `ω_x : ⟨M⟩ → Vec_K` the fibre at `x`. Then `(⟨M⟩, ⊗, ω_x)` is a neutral Tannakian category over `K` with tensor generator `M`, so by [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64) its group DGal`(M, x) := Aut^⊗(ω_x)` is a closed algebraic subgroup of `GL(M_x)` and `⟨M⟩ ≃ Rep_K`(DGal`(M, x)`). Under this equivalence, invariants of DGal`(M, x)` on `N_x` are `H⁰_rig(X/K, N)` (the largest constant subobject), and for `X` a smooth affine curve and `N` quasi-unipotent, coinvariants on `N_x` are `H²_{c,rig}(X/K, N)(1)` (Crew 1998 Corollary 9.6 and the remark after it).

*Hypotheses.*

- `X` smooth and geometrically connected with a rational point `x; Isoc†(X/K)` is abelian with the usual tensor structure and duals (RD.3).
- For the coinvariant description, `X` a smooth affine curve (Crew's setting) and `N` quasi-unipotent, hence strict (Crew 1998 Proposition 10.2; true when `N` underlies an F-isocrystal, RD.2).

*Proof sketch.*

1. `Isoc†(X/K)` is a K-linear rigid abelian tensor category: kernels and cokernels of horizontal maps of locally free modules with connection on a smooth lift are locally free ([§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13)), duals and internal Hom exist; `⟨M⟩` is a rigid abelian tensor subcategory.
2. `End(1) = H⁰_rig(X/K, O_X) = K` because `X` is geometrically connected ([§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10)).
3. `ω_x` is exact and faithful: pullback to a point with values in a perfect field is exact, and a horizontal map vanishing at one point of a connected `X` vanishes (Crew 1992, statement after 1.1.2 and 1.9).
4. Apply [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64) (c) with tensor generator `M ⊕ M^∨`.
5. Invariants: `N_x^{DGal}` corresponds to the largest constant subobject of `N`, which is `H⁰_rig(X, N) ⊗ O_X`; coinvariants via Poincaré duality on curves ([§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46); Crew 1998 Corollary 9.6).

*Sources.* Crew, *Finiteness theorems for the cohomology of an overconvergent isocrystal on a curve*, Remark after Theorem 9.5 and Corollary 9.6, p. 755; Crew, *F-isocrystals and their monodromy groups*, Section 1.1 and Introduction, pp. 429-432; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Definition 9.8, p. 23; Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.2.1, p. 42.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64) *Neutral Tannakian recognition theorem*; [§RD.3.13](#rd-3-13) *Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame*; [§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10) *Rigid cohomology `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46) *Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy*; [§RD.2.31](#rd-2-31) *The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): `(φ,∇)`-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent*.

**Checks.**

- `M = O_X`: DGal is trivial.
- `M = L_π` on `A^1` (with `x = 0`): DGal `= μ_p`.
- `M = K_a` on `G_m` with a of exact denominator `m`: DGal `= μ_m`.

<a id="rd-6-66"></a>

### RD.6.66 Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals have finite order up to a twist

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically connected curve over `𝔽_q` and `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K)` of rank 1. After a finite extension of `K` there are `c` and `n ≥ 1` with `E(c)^{⊗n} ≅ O_X` ([§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59)). Equivalently, the geometric monodromy group of `E` ([§RD.6.65](#rd-6-65)) is finite, contained in `μ_n`, and for every closed point `x, F_x(E)^n = c^{−n·deg x}`. The same conclusion holds for smooth geometrically connected schemes of finite type over `𝔽_q` in arbitrary dimension (Abe, Lemma 6.1 `(i)`); geometric connectedness is retained. On a disconnected smooth scheme the conclusion applies componentwise with separate constant twists.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth and geometrically connected over `𝔽_q; E` of rank 1 with Frobenius structure. Steps 1–4 give the curve case. In higher dimension use the alteration argument below.

*Proof sketch.*

1. By [§RD.6.60](#rd-6-60) there is a constant `c_1` with `E(c_1)` unit-root.
2. By [§RD.6.61](#rd-6-61), `E(c_1)` corresponds to a character `ρ : π_1(X) → O_{K'}^×` with finite local monodromy at each point of `X̄ − X`; let `m` be the lcm of the orders of the inertia images, so `ρ^m` is unramified and extends to `π_1(X̄)`.
3. By [§RD.6.63](#rd-6-63), `ρ^m` has finite order `N` on the geometric fundamental group; the restriction of `ρ^{mN}` to the arithmetic group factors through `Gal(F̄_q/𝔽_q) = Ẑ`, i.e. it is the character of a constant F-line `L_d`.
4. Hence `E(c_1)^{⊗mN} ≅ L_d` and `E(c_1 d^{−1/(mN)})^{⊗mN} ≅ O_X` after adjoining an mN-th root of `d` to `K`; the fibre formula follows from [§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59).
5. For smooth geometrically connected `X` of arbitrary dimension, use a generically étale alteration with a smooth compactification and normal-crossings boundary. Rank-one unipotent monodromy is constant, so the extension theorem [§RD.5.102](#rd-5-102) extends the unit-root object across the boundary. Katz–Crew [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) and Katz–Lang finiteness [§RD.6.63](#rd-6-63) then give the finite-order twist on that alteration. Over a dense open where the alteration is finite étale, its norm raises the tensor power by its degree; restriction to the dense open is fully faithful, so the trivialisation extends to `X` (Abe, proof of Lemma 6.1`(i)`, p. 7). Use semistable reduction [§RD.5.113](#rd-5-113), finite étale pushforward [§RD.3.41](#rd-3-41), and dense-open full faithfulness [§RD.5.112](#rd-5-112).

*Sources.* Crew, *F-isocrystals and their monodromy groups*, Corollary 1.5 and its proof, pp. 434-435; Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Lemma 6.1 `(i)` and proof, p. 7; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Lemma 9.14, p. 25; Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.1.2 and Corollary 6.1.3, p. 41.

*Needs:* [§RD.5.113](#rd-5-113) *Kedlaya's semistable reduction theorem for overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.5.112](#rd-5-112) *Restriction of F-isocrystals to a dense open is fully faithful, and closed under subquotients in the overconvergent case*; [§RD.5.102](#rd-5-102) *Kedlaya's extension theorem: constant monodromy is the obstruction to extending an overconvergent isocrystal*; [§RD.3.48](#rd-3-48) *Katz–Crew: unit-root F-isocrystals are lisse p-adic sheaves*; [§RD.3.41](#rd-3-41) *Pushforward of (overconvergent) F-isocrystals along finite étale morphisms*; [§RD.6.60](#rd-6-60) *A rank-one F-isocrystal is isoclinic and a constant twist makes it unit-root*; [§RD.6.61](#rd-6-61) *Unit-root F-isocrystals and p-adic representations (Katz, Crew, Tsuzuki)*; [§RD.6.63](#rd-6-63) *Katz–Lang finiteness of the geometric abelian fundamental group*; [§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59) *Constant rank-one F-isocrystals (twists)*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.65](#rd-6-65) *The tensor category generated by an overconvergent isocrystal is neutral Tannakian*.

**Checks.**

- `L_π` on `A^1: L_π^{⊗p} ≅ O_X, n = p, c = 1`.
- `K_a` on `G_m` with `a = b/(q − 1): K_a^{⊗(q−1)} ≅ O, c = 1`.
- `O(−1) = L_q`: twist by `c = q^{-1}, n = 1`.

- For `X=Spec 𝔽_q ⊔ Spec 𝔽_q` with Frobenius 1 and `p` on the two lines, a common twist would force `c^n=`(pc)`^n=1` and hence `p^n=1`. Separate componentwise twists are necessary.

### RD.6.67 Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals are `ι`-pure: the proof through curves

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth irreducible `𝔽_q`-scheme, `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K)` of rank 1 and `ι : K^alg → C` a field embedding. Then `E` is `ι`-pure of a single weight `w: |ι(F_x(E))| = q^{w·deg(x)/2}` for all closed points `x`. If `X` is a geometrically connected curve, `w = −2·log_q|ι(c)|` for the twist `c` of [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66).

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth irreducible over `𝔽_q; ι` arbitrary.

*Proof sketch.*

1. First reduce to geometrically connected `X`: if its constant field is `𝔽_{q^h}`, regard `X` over that field, use `F^h` and base `q^h`, and replace every degree `d` by `d/h`. The equality `q^{wd/2} = (q^h)^{w(d/h)/2}` preserves the weight. Extend coefficients to the selected constant-field factor as in [§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18).
2. Curves: by [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66), `F_x(E)^n = c^{−n deg x}`, so `|ι(F_x(E))| = |ι(c)|^{−deg x}` for all `x`.
3. General geometrically connected `X`: by Abe's Lemma 6.1 `(i)` (stated in [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66)) the same identity holds on `X`. Alternatively, through any closed point `x` pass a smooth curve `i : C → X` (Abe, proof of Corollary 6.3), and the weights at `x` and at a fixed base point agree once a single irreducible curve contains both; the statement in all dimensions is taken from Abe.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Corollary 6.1.4, p. 41; Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Lemma 6.1, p. 7, and proof of Corollary 6.3, p. 8.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18) *Rigid cohomology of `Spec 𝔽_{q^d}`*; [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66) *Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals have finite order up to a twist*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59) *Constant rank-one F-isocrystals (twists)*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.4 *`ι`-weights of nonzero elements of a coefficient field*.

**Checks.**

- On `Spec 𝔽_{q^h}`, a constant line whose `F^h`-eigenvalue is `q^h` has weight 2 over both bases; its degree is `h` over `𝔽_q` and 1 over `𝔽_{q^h}`.
- `L_π: |ι(ψ(Tr x))| = 1`, weight 0.
- `O(−1)`: weight 2.
- `K_a`: weight 0.

<a id="rd-6-68"></a>

### RD.6.68 Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals: constancy of a tensor power and `ι`-purity

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth irreducible `𝔽_q`-variety and `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K)` of rank 1. Then `(i)` there is `n ≥ 1` with `E^{⊗n}` constant on `X` (spanned by horizontal sections); (ii) `E` is `ι`-pure of some weight, for every `ι`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth irreducible over `𝔽_q; E` of rank 1.

*Proof sketch.* [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66) makes a constant twist unit-root and trivialises its geometric monodromy after finite étale pullback. [§RD.6.67](#rd-6-67) proves the pure weight by restriction to curves and descent; the argument on a dense open suffices and does not require an extension theorem for all coefficients. For geometrically irreducible `X, E^{⊗n}` is a constant differential line with scalar Frobenius `c`, so at a degree-`d` point `F_x(E)^n = c^d` and the weight is `(2/n)log_q|ι(c)|`. For irreducible `X` whose constant field is `𝔽_{q^h}`, apply this argument over that field using `F^h` and base `q^h`; every closed-point degree is a multiple of `h`, and the relative weight is unchanged. Without geometric connectedness, the horizontal-section space need not be a one-dimensional K-space. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.1.2, p. 41, and Corollary 6.1.4, p. 41.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10) *Rigid cohomology `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.6.66](#rd-6-66) *Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals have finite order up to a twist*; [§RD.6.67](#rd-6-67) *Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals are `ι`-pure: the proof through curves*.

**Checks.**

- The Dwork isocrystal: `L_π^{⊗p} ≅ O`, so `L_π` is `ι`-pure of weight 0.
- `K(−1) ⊗ L_π` is `ι`-pure of weight 2.

<a id="rd-6-69"></a>

### RD.6.69 `ι`-determinantal weights

**Definition.** For an absolutely irreducible `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K)` of `rank d` on a smooth irreducible `X`, the `ι`-determinantal weight is `(1/d)` times the `ι`-weight of the rank-one object `∧^d E` (well defined by [§RD.6.68](#rd-6-68)). For general `E` the `ι`-determinantal weights are those of its absolutely irreducible Jordan–Hölder constituents (after finite extension of `𝔽_q, k` and `K`, with the normalisation by the degree of the extension); `E` is purely of `ι`-determinantal weight `α` if all of them equal `α`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth irreducible over `𝔽_q; ι` fixed.

The API:

- `detWeights`: The multiset of `ι`-determinantal weights of `E`.
- `IsPurelyDetWeight`: All `ι`-determinantal weights equal `α`.
- `detWeight_rankOne`: For rank-one `E`, the determinantal weight is its `ι`-weight.
- `detWeight_of_isIotaPure`: If `E` is `ι`-pure of weight `w`, every determinantal weight is `w`.
- `detWeight_dual`: Determinantal weights of `E^∨` are the negatives of those of `E`.
- `detWeight_tensor`: Purely of weights `β, γ ⇒ E ⊗ F` purely of weight `β + γ` ([§RD.6.75](#rd-6-75)).

*Proof sketch.* `∧^d E` has rank one, hence is `ι`-pure of a single weight. Jordan–Hölder constituents of `(σ, ∇)`-modules exist (submodules closed under `F` and `∇` are direct summands as A-modules, Kedlaya Finiteness Lemma 3.3.4), and absolute irreducibility is attained after finite extension. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.1, p. 41.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.68](#rd-6-68) *Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals: constancy of a tensor power and `ι`-purity*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*.

**Checks.**

- `detWeight_const`: The determinantal weight of `O_X` is 0.
- `detWeight_zero`: The zero object has no determinantal weights.
- `detWeight_constituents`: For `E = K ⊕ K(−2)` on `Spec 𝔽_q` the determinantal weights are {0, 4}, not the average `2 = (1/2)·`weight`(∧^2 E)`: the definition uses constituents, not `E` itself.
- `detWeight_rankOne_compat`: For rank-one `E`, detWeights `E = {w}` where `E` is `ι`-pure of weight `w` ([§RD.6.68](#rd-6-68)).
- `E = O`: determinantal weight 0.
- `E = K ⊕ K(−2)` on `Spec 𝔽_q`: determinantal weights {0, 4}.

### RD.6.70 The global monodromy group `G_M`

**Construction.** Let `X` be a smooth irreducible affine `𝔽_q`-variety with a rational point `x, A` a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre `X`, and `M` an absolutely semisimple `(σ, ∇)`-module over A. Let `C_M` be the category of finite locally free A-modules with connection isomorphic (as modules with connection, without Frobenius) to subquotients of finite direct sums of tensor words `M^{⊗a} ⊗ (M^∨)^{⊗b}`, and `G_M ⊆ GL(M_x)` the affine group scheme `Aut^⊗(ω_x)` of tensor automorphisms of the fibre functor, embedded in `GL(M_x)`. Then `N ↦ N_x` is an equivalence `C_M ≅ Rep_K(G_M)` (Tannaka duality for the neutral Tannakian category `C_M` with fibre functor at `x`). For `n ≥ 1, W_n` is the semidirect product of `G_M` with the group generated by `F^n`, with deg : `W_n → Z`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth irreducible affine with `x ∈ X(𝔽_q); M` absolutely semisimple.

The API:

- `monodromyGroup`: `G_M ⊆ GL(M_x)`.
- `fibreFunctor`: `N ↦ N_x` on `C_M`.
- `tannakaEquiv`: `C_M ≅ Rep_K(G_M)`, by the neutral Tannakian recognition theorem [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64).
- `monodromyGroup_irreducible`: `N ∈ C_M` irreducible `⇒ G_M` acts irreducibly on `N_x`; if `N` is absolutely irreducible, so is this action.
- `monodromyGroup_trivial_on_constant`: `G_M` acts trivially on `N_x` for constant `N`.
- `weilGroup`: `W_n = G_M ⋊ ⟨F^n⟩` with degree map to nZ.
- `frobenius_normalises`: Conjugation by `F` preserves `G_M`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. `C_M` is a neutral Tannakian category over `K` with fibre functor `N ↦ N_x` (Hom spaces are finite-dimensional and commute with base extension).
2. Apply the adapter [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64) to this category and fibre: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles §§6.1–6.3 supplies recognition and the tensor-generator criterion, and the adapter preserves the marked fibre on Tau Ceti's finite-comodule carrier.
3. Irreducible `N ∈ C_M` give irreducible representations `N_x`; absolute irreducibility requires `N` to remain irreducible after coefficient extension; `G_M` acts trivially on constant objects.
4. `F` acts on `C_M` by `σ`-pullback, normalising `G_M`; this defines `W_n`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.2.1, p. 42, and §6.2, p. 42; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Definition 9.8, p. 23.

*Needs:* [§RD.3.25](#rd-3-25) *Overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.64](#rd-6-64) *Neutral Tannakian recognition theorem*; [§RD.6.65](#rd-6-65) *The tensor category generated by an overconvergent isocrystal is neutral Tannakian*.

**Checks.**

- `monodromyGroup_constant`: If `M` is constant then `G_M = {1}`.
- `monodromyGroup_dwork`: For `M = L_π` on `A^1, G_M = μ_p: L_π^{⊗p}` is constant while `L_π` is not.
- `monodromyGroup_twist_invariant`: `G_{M(1)} = G_M`: Tate twisting changes Frobenius, which is invisible to `C_M`; so `G_M` does not detect weights by itself.
- `monodromyGroup_rankOne`: For rank-one `M` with `M^{⊗n}` constant, `G_M ⊆ μ_n ⊂ GL_1`.
- For `M` constant, `G_M` is trivial.
- For `M = L_π` on `A^1` (with a rational base point), `G_M = μ_p`.

<a id="rd-6-71"></a>

### RD.6.71 Lie algebras of normalisers and a finite-index criterion in characteristic 0

**Lemma.** Let `G` be an affine algebraic group over a field of characteristic 0. (a) `G` is smooth and `dim G = dim Lie(G)`. (b) For closed subgroups `H ⊆ N` of `G, H` has finite index in `N` if and only if `Lie(H) = Lie(N)`. (c) For a closed subgroup `H, Lie(N_G(H)) ⊆ {X ∈ Lie(G) : [X, Lie(H)] ⊆ Lie(H)}` and `Lie(Z_G(H)) = Lie(G)^H`; for `H` connected these are the normaliser and centraliser of `Lie(H)` in `Lie(G)` restricted to `N_G(H)`° and `Z_G(H)`°.

*Hypotheses.* Characteristic 0 is needed for (a) and (b) (Cartier's theorem); see the last Check.

*Proof sketch.* (a) is Cartier's theorem; (b) follows since `H`° `= N`° iff their Lie algebras agree, by (a) and the correspondence between connected subgroups and their Lie algebras in characteristic 0; (c) by differentiating the conjugation action. (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 170 (2017), Theorem 3.23 (Cartier) and Chapter 10 (Lie algebras of subgroups, normalisers and centralisers); Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, GTM 21, §13 (characteristic 0 theory).)

*Needs:* TauCetiRoadmap ReductiveGroups Layer 2.

**Checks.**

- `H = μ_n ⊂ N = G_m` over `ℚ: Lie(H) = 0 ≠ Lie(N)`, and `H` has infinite index.
- `H = N`° `⊂ N`: equal Lie algebras and finite `index [N : N`°].
- Characteristic `p` non-example: over `𝔽_p` the subgroup scheme `μ_p` of `G_m` is not smooth and `Lie(μ_p) = Lie(G_m)`, although `μ_p` is finite.

<a id="rd-6-72"></a>

### RD.6.72 `N`/GZ is finite for an absolutely semisimple algebraic group

**Lemma.** Let `V` be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field `K` of characteristic 0 and `G ⊆ GL(V)` an algebraic subgroup acting absolutely semisimply on `V`, with normaliser `N` and centraliser `Z` in `GL(V)`. Then `N`/GZ is finite.

*Hypotheses.* char `K = 0; G` acts absolutely semisimply.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Base change to an algebraic closure. The normaliser permutes finitely many isotypical constituents; pass to the subgroup fixing them, then analyse each irreducible constituent and its multiplicity space.
2. Use reductivity of the image of an absolutely semisimple representation in characteristic zero and the nondegenerate trace pairing on its faithful semisimple Lie-algebra representation. This includes the central torus contribution.
3. For the Lie algebras, trace invariance shows that a normalising element orthogonal to `g` centralises `g`. Hence `n = g + z`. Smoothness in characteristic zero and the dimension comparison then make the algebraic quotient `N`/(GZ) finite. This is a quotient group scheme; it is not a claim about the quotient `N(K)/(G(K)Z(K))`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.2.2, p. 43, and Proof of Proposition 6.2.2, p. 43.

*Needs:* Mathlib `LieModule.isNilpotent_derivedSeries_of_traceForm_eq_zero`; Mathlib `LieModule.isNilpotent_iff_forall`; Mathlib `LieModule.traceForm`; [§RD.6.71](#rd-6-71) *Lie algebras of normalisers and a finite-index criterion in characteristic 0*.

**Checks.**

- `G = SL_2` on `K^2: N = GL_2 = G·Z`, so `N`/GZ is trivial.
- `G =` the diagonal torus in `GL_2` (semisimple action): `N`/GZ `≅ S_2`.

<a id="rd-6-73"></a>

### RD.6.73 Some power of Frobenius acts on `G_M` by an inner automorphism

**Lemma.** In the situation of [§RD.6.70](#rd-6-70), there is `n ≥ 1` such that conjugation by `F^n` on `G_M` is inner; consequently `W_n` splits as a product of `G_M` and `Z` (generated by a central element of positive degree), and some power of `F` respects the Jordan–Hölder decompositions of all `M^a ⊗ (M^∨)^b` simultaneously.

*Hypotheses.* `M` absolutely semisimple; `G_M` as constructed.

*Proof sketch.* Conjugation by `F` lies in the normaliser of `G_M` in `GL(M_x)`; by [§RD.6.72](#rd-6-72) its image in `N/(G_M·Z)` has finite order `n`, so `F^n ∈ G_M·Z` and `W_n ≅ G_M × Z`. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.2, p. 44.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.70](#rd-6-70) *The global monodromy group `G_M`*; [§RD.6.72](#rd-6-72) *`N`/GZ is finite for an absolutely semisimple algebraic group*.

**Checks.**

- For `M` constant, `G_M = 1` and `n = 1`.

<a id="rd-6-74"></a>

### RD.6.74 Determinantal weights via central elements of `W_1`

**Lemma.** For `N ∈ C_M` with its Frobenius structure: `N` is purely of `ι`-determinantal weight `α` iff for some (equivalently any) central element `z` of `W_1` of degree `m > 0`, every eigenvalue `λ` of `z` on `N_x` satisfies `|ι(λ)| = q^{mα/2}`.

*Hypotheses.* `M` absolutely semisimple; `N ∈ C_M`.

*Proof sketch.* Reduce to an absolutely irreducible `N` of rank `r>0`. By Schur, `z` acts on `N_x` by a scalar `λ`; on `P=det N` it acts by `λ^r`. By RD.6.69 the weight of `P` is `rα`. By [§RD.6.68](#rd-6-68), `P^{⊗l}` is constant for some `l>0`, so `z` and `F^m` agree there, and their actions on `P` differ by an `l`-th root of unity. Thus `P` has weight `rα` exactly when `|ι(λ^r)|=q^(mrα/2)`, equivalently `|ι(λ)|=q^(mα/2)`. Apply this to each absolutely irreducible constituent. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.2.3, p. 44, retaining the rank when passing to the determinant.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.73](#rd-6-73) *Some power of Frobenius acts on `G_M` by an inner automorphism*; [§RD.6.68](#rd-6-68) *Rank-one overconvergent F-isocrystals: constancy of a tensor power and `ι`-purity*; [§RD.6.69](#rd-6-69) *`ι`-determinantal weights*.

**Checks.**

- `N = O: z` acts by a root of unity times `F^m = 1`, weight 0.
- For `N=O(−1)⊕O(−1)`, `z=F^m` acts by `q^m`, giving determinantal weight 2; its determinant has weight 4 and scalar `q^(2m)`. Passing to the determinant doubles both exponents.
- For `N=O⊕O(−1)`, the eigenvalues `1,q^m` have different absolute values. There is no single determinantal weight, although the determinant has weight 2.

<a id="rd-6-75"></a>

### RD.6.75 Determinantal weights under finite pullback, tensor products and exterior powers

**Lemma.** Let `X` be smooth irreducible affine over `𝔽_q` and `E, F` overconvergent F-isocrystals on `X`. `(i)` For `f : Y → X` finite and dominant (hence surjective), with `Y` smooth irreducible, `E` is purely of `ι`-determinantal weight `α` iff `f^*E` is. (ii) If `E, F` are purely of determinantal weights `β, γ` then `E ⊗ F` is purely of weight `β + γ`. (iii) If `n(β)` is the total rank of the constituents of `E` of determinantal weight `β`, the determinantal weights of `∧^d E` are the numbers `Σ_β a(β)β` with `0 ≤ a(β) ≤ n(β)` and `Σ a(β) = d`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth irreducible affine over `𝔽_q`.

*Proof sketch.* All three follow from the characterisation by central elements of `W_1` ([§RD.6.74](#rd-6-74)): the eigenvalues of `z` on tensor products and exterior powers are products of eigenvalues, and pullback along finite maps changes `z` by a power (Crew, Proposition 5.7, as reproved by Kedlaya). (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.3, p. 45.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.74](#rd-6-74) *Determinantal weights via central elements of `W_1`*.

**Checks.**

- `E = K(−1), F = K(−2): E ⊗ F` has determinantal weight 6.
- Without dominance the reverse implication fails: restricting `O ⊕ K(−1)` to the empty scheme yields a zero object purely of every determinantal weight, while the original object has weights 0 and 2.

<a id="rd-6-76"></a>

### RD.6.76 Rankin squaring: fibres of `ι`-real isocrystals on curves are weakly mixed of weight `≤` the largest determinantal weight

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q, E` an `ι`-real overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X`, and `r` the largest `ι`-determinantal weight of `E`. Then every fibre `E_x` is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ r`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q; E ι`-real.

*Proof sketch.*

1. The trace formula ([§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23)) for `E^{⊗2i}, i ≥ 1`, gives `ι det(1 − tF | H¹_c(E^{⊗2i})) / ι det(1 − tF | H²_c(E^{⊗2i})) = ∏_x ι det(1 − t^{deg x}F_x | E_x^{⊗2i})^{−1}; H⁰_c = 0` on an affine curve.
2. Each local factor has nonnegative real coefficients since `Tr(F_x^n | E_x^{⊗2i}) = Tr(F_x^n | E_x^{⊗i})^2 ≥ 0` (`ι`-reality); so the radius of convergence of the left side is `≤ |ι(α)|^{−2i/deg x}` for every eigenvalue `α` of `F_x` (positive-coefficient series lemma, DeligneWeightsAndPurity §2.7).
3. The radius is `≥` the smallest `|ι|`-norm of eigenvalues of `F^{−1}` on `H²_c(E^{⊗2i})`; by Poincaré duality ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89)) these are eigenvalues of `F` on `H⁰_rig(E^{⊗−2i})(1)`, which is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ −2ir−2` (the twist `(1)` lowers weight by 2) by [§RD.6.75](#rd-6-75)(ii) and `H⁰ ↪` fibre.
4. Hence `|ι(α)| ≤ q^{deg(x)(ir+1)/(2i)}`; let `i → ∞`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Lemma 6.3.2, p. 45, and Proof of Lemma 6.3.2, p. 46.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) *`ι`-real and `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.75](#rd-6-75) *Determinantal weights under finite pullback, tensor products and exterior powers*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §2.7 *Lemma 3.5: factors of a product of positive power series converge at least as far*.

**Checks.**

- `E = O` on `A^1: r = 0` and all fibres have `F_x = 1` (weight `0 ≤ 0`).
- For `E=O` and `r=0`, `H⁰(E^{⊗−2i})(1)=K(1)` has weight `−2`, giving the `+1` in the exponent `(ir+1)/(2i)`.
- For a constant real line of weight `r`, the dual tensor power followed by `(1)` has weight exactly `−2ir−2`; the limiting fibre bound is `r`.

<a id="rd-6-77"></a>

### RD.6.77 Constituents of `ι`-real isocrystals on curves are `ι`-pure

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q`. The constituents of an `ι`-real overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X` are all `ι`-pure; in particular every irreducible `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X` is `ι`-pure of some weight.

*Hypotheses.* `X` a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q; E ι`-real (resp. irreducible `ι`-realizable).

*Proof sketch.*

1. For `β` a determinantal weight, let `E_β` be the sum of constituents of weight `β, n(γ)` the rank of those of weight `γ > β`, and `N = Σ_{γ>β} n(γ)`.
2. The highest determinantal weight of `∧^{N+1}E` is `β + Σ_{γ>β} n(γ)γ` ([§RD.6.75](#rd-6-75) (iii)), so by [§RD.6.76](#rd-6-76) `∧^{N+1}E` is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ β + Σ n(γ)γ`; an eigenvalue `λ` of `F_x` on `(E_β)_x` times the determinants of the higher constituents is an eigenvalue of `∧^{N+1}E`, giving `|ι(λ)| ≤ q^{β deg(x)/2}`.
3. The same for `E^∨` gives the reverse inequality; so `E_β` is `ι`-pure of weight `β`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Theorem 6.3.4, p. 46.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.76](#rd-6-76) *Rankin squaring: fibres of `ι`-real isocrystals on curves are weakly mixed of weight `≤` the largest determinantal weight*; [§RD.6.75](#rd-6-75) *Determinantal weights under finite pullback, tensor products and exterior powers*; [§RD.6.69](#rd-6-69) *`ι`-determinantal weights*; [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) *`ι`-real and `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals*.

**Checks.**

- `O` is pure of weight 0; the Dwork isocrystal (irreducible, `ι`-realizable) is pure of weight 0.

<a id="rd-6-78"></a>

### RD.6.78 The weight drop lemma

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q` and `E ι`-pure of weight `w`. Then `H¹_{c,rig}(X/K, E)` is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w + 2`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; `E ι`-pure of weight `w`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Apply `ι` to the trace formula ([§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23)): `∏_x ∏_α (1 − t^{deg x}ι(α))^{−1} = ι det(1 − tF | H¹_c) / ι det(1 − tF | H²_c)`.
2. `#X(𝔽_{q^n}) ≤ C q^n` (`X` contains a dense open finite étale over an open of `A^1`, by the geometric lemma of RD.5), so `Σ_x Σ_α |ι(α)||t|^{deg x} ≤ C' Σ_n q^n q^{nw/2}|t|^n` converges for `|t| < q^{−(w+2)/2}`; the Euler product converges absolutely and has no zeros there.
3. `H⁰_rig(X/K, E^∨)` is `ι`-pure of weight `−w` ([§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28)), so by Poincaré duality ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89)) `H²_c(E)` is `ι`-pure of weight `w + 2` and `det(1 − tF | H²_c)` has no zeros in `|t| < q^{−(w+2)/2}`.
4. Hence `ι det(1 − tF | H¹_c)` has no zeros there, i.e. `H¹_c` is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w + 2`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Lemma 6.4.1, p. 46–47, and §6.4, p. 46.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.5.7](#rd-5-7) *Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic*.

**Checks.**

- `E = O` on `G_m: H¹_c(G_m) = K` has weight `0 ≤ 2`.

<a id="rd-6-79"></a>

### RD.6.79 Local invariants of a pure isocrystal are weakly mixed of weight `≤ w`

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q` and `E ι`-pure of weight `w`. Then `H⁰_loc(X/K, E)` (horizontal sections at the points at infinity) is weakly `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; `E ι`-pure of weight `w`.

*Proof sketch.* The exact sequence `H⁰_rig(X/K, E) → H⁰_loc(X/K, E) → H¹_{c,rig}(X/K, E)` (Kedlaya (2.6.1), from the curve cohomology of RD.5) with `H⁰_rig` pure of weight `w` and `H¹_c` weakly mixed `≤ w + 2` ([§RD.6.78](#rd-6-78)) shows `H⁰_loc` is weakly mixed `≤ w + 2`. Applied to `E^{⊗n}` (pure of weight nw), at each boundary point separately, `H⁰_loc,x(E^{⊗n}) ⊇ H⁰_loc,x(E)^{⊗n}` is weakly mixed `≤ nw + 2`, so `H⁰_loc(E)` is weakly mixed `≤ w + 2/n` for all `n`. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.4.3, p. 47.)

*Needs:* [§RD.6.78](#rd-6-78) *The weight drop lemma*; [§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46) *Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*.

**Checks.**

- `E = O` on `G_m: H⁰_loc = K ⊕ K` (at 0 and `∞`), weight 0.

<a id="rd-6-80"></a>

### RD.6.80 Weight–monodromy purity at the points at infinity of a curve

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth affine curve over `𝔽_q, X̄` its smooth compactification, `E ∈` F-`Isoc†(X/K) ι`-pure of weight `β`, and `y ∈ X̄ − X`. After a finite étale cover and a finite extension of `K` and of `𝔽_q` (allowed by [§RD.2.32](#rd-2-32)), `E` is unipotent at a rational point `η` over `y`; let `(V_η, F, N)` be its fibre at `η`: the solution space of the nilpotent residue `N` with the Frobenius `F` of the generic fibre, with `NF = q_η·FN`. Let `M` be the monodromy filtration of `N` on `V_η`, centred at 0 (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §1.3). Then `gr^M_i V_η` is `ι`-pure of weight `β + i` for every `i`. Consequently the local invariants `ker N = H⁰_loc(E)` at `y` are `ι`-mixed of weights `≤ β`, and on `W := ker N` the filtration `W_i := ker N ∩ im N^i` has `W_i/W_{i+1} ι`-pure of weight `β − i`. This proves the conclusion of Kedlaya's Proposition 6.4.4 used by [§RD.6.81](#rd-6-81); the shortcut in Kedlaya's proof does not suffice (see *Corrections to the sources*).

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth affine curve over `𝔽_q; E ι`-pure of weight `β`; the local data `(V_η, F, N)` are well defined up to canonical isomorphism on `gr^M` (Crew 1998, 10.6).

*Proof sketch.*

1. `L`-function of the extension across `y` (Crew 1998 (10.7.1)-(10.7.2), the analogue of Deligne's (1.8.1.1)): the trace formula ([§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23)) and duality on curves ([§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46)) show that the reciprocal `ι det(1 − tF | H⁰(E ⊗ A(y)))^{-1}` has no pole in `|t| < q^{−(β+2)/2}`, i.e. the determinant has no zero there, so the weights of `F` on `ker N` are `≤ β + 2` (this is [§RD.6.78](#rd-6-78) in local form).
2. Applying this to tensor powers `E^{⊗k}` (pure of weight `kβ`), which contain `(ker N)^{⊗k}` in their local invariants, gives weights `≤ β + 2/k` for every `k`, hence `≤ β` (Crew 1998 10.7, [§RD.6.79](#rd-6-79)).
3. Deligne's argument (Weil II proof of 1.8.4): twist to `β = 0`, so `ker N` has weights `≤ 0`; for a primitive part `P_{−j} ⊂ gr^M_{−j}` of lowest weight the bound gives weights `≤ 0`; applying the same bound to `E ⊗ E` (whose monodromy filtration is the convolution of the two, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §2.6) and to the dual `E^∨` (weights `≥ 0` by symmetry) pins the weights of `P_{−j}` to exactly `−j`, using the properties (1.6.14) of the monodromy filtration under tensor products and duals.
4. The statements about `ker N` and `W_i` follow from the `sl_2`-structure of `gr^M: ker N` meets `gr^M_{−i}` exactly in the bottoms of the Jordan strings of `length i + 1`, which are `ker N ∩ im N^i` modulo `ker N ∩ im N^{i+1}`.

*Sources.* Crew, *Finiteness theorems for the cohomology of an overconvergent isocrystal on a curve*, 10.6-10.8, pp. 758-761; Deligne, *La conjecture de Weil. II*, (1.6.1), (1.6.13)-(1.6.14), pp. 165-171, and (1.8.1) and Théorème (1.8.4) with proof, pp. 175-176; Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.4.4, pp. 47-48.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.79](#rd-6-79) *Local invariants of a pure isocrystal are weakly mixed of weight `≤ w`*; [§RD.6.78](#rd-6-78) *The weight drop lemma*; [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46) *Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy*; [§RD.2.32](#rd-2-32) *Local monodromy theorem in finite étale form (the form used for finiteness of rigid cohomology)*; [§RD.2.16](#rd-2-16) *Unipotent `∇`-modules are the modules `V ⊗ R` with nilpotent residue*; [§RD.2.34](#rd-2-34) *The (`φ, N`, Gal)-module of logarithmic solutions (local monodromy representation)*; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles §1.3 *The monodromy filtration in an abelian category*; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §2.6; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.9 *Purity and weights under subobjects, quotients, extensions and direct sums*.

**Checks.**

- `E` unipotent with `N = 0: M` is concentrated in degree 0 and `V_η` is pure of weight `β`.
- A Tate-curve type degeneration with `V_η` of rank 2, `N ≠ 0` and `β = 1: gr^M_{−1} = ker N = im N` is pure of weight 0 and `gr^M_1` of weight 2.
- `Kl_{n+1}` at 0 (single block of size `n + 1`, weight `n`): `ker N` is one-dimensional of weight 0 ([§RD.6.97](#rd-6-97)).

### RD.6.81 Local invariants are strongly mixed: equal-characteristic local weight–monodromy

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve over `𝔽_q` and `E ι`-pure of weight `w`. Then `H⁰_loc(X/K, E)` is (strongly) `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w`; more precisely, at each point at infinity where `E` is unipotent with nilpotent residue `N`, the space `W = ker N` carries the F-stable filtration `W_i = W ∩ im N^i` with `W_i/W_{i+1} ι`-pure of weight `w − i`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth geometrically irreducible affine curve; `E ι`-pure of weight `w`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Pass to a finite cover and enlarge constants so that the module is unipotent at rational boundary points. Choose a constant nilpotent residue `N` on `V` with `NF = qFN`.
2. The conclusion for `W_i = ker N ∩ im N^i` is the weight-monodromy filtration statement of Weil II Proposition 6.4.4, pp. 47–48. The proof uses the nilpotent tensor/monodromy-filtration argument, for example the Jacobson–Morosov formalism cited there.
3. The printed shortcut does not justify its key containment: `(ker N) ⊗ V` is generally not killed by `N⊗1+1⊗N`. For a size-two Jordan block and a nonzero `w ∈ ker N, (N⊗1+1⊗N)(w⊗v)=w⊗`Nv can be nonzero. The weights must therefore be deduced from the weight-monodromy argument rather than from this containment.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Proposition 6.4.4, p. 47, and §6.4, p. 48.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.79](#rd-6-79) *Local invariants of a pure isocrystal are weakly mixed of weight `≤ w`*; [§RD.2.31](#rd-2-31) *The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): `(φ,∇)`-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent*; [§RD.2.13](#rd-2-13) *Unipotent `∇`-modules over the Robba ring*; [§RD.6.80](#rd-6-80) *Weight–monodromy purity at the points at infinity of a curve*.

**Checks.**

- If `E` is unipotent at the point with `N = 0`, then `W = V` and `W/W_1 = V` is `ι`-pure of weight `w`.
- Model degeneration: `V` of rank 2 with `N ≠ 0` and `E ι`-pure of weight 1 (`H¹` of a family of elliptic curves near a multiplicative fibre): `W = ker N = im N` is `ι`-pure of weight `0 = w − 1`, as for the `ℓ`-adic Tate curve.

<a id="rd-6-82"></a>

### RD.6.82 Normalising an `ι`-pure coefficient to weight zero

**Lemma.** Let `ι : K^alg → C` be a field embedding and `E ≠ 0` an overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X` that is `ι`-pure of real weight `w`. Choose a closed point `x` of degree `d` and an eigenvalue `α` of `F_x` on `E_x`, and let `c ∈ K^alg` with `c^d = α`. Then `|ι(c)| = q^{w/2}, c` lies in a finite extension `K'` of `K`, and `E(c^{-1}) = E ⊗ L_{c^{-1}}` ([§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59), over `K'`) is `ι`-pure of weight 0. For integer `w` one may instead use the Tate twist `E(w/2)` when `w` is even, or, after adjoining `√q`, take `c = (√q)^w` for integer `w` and twist by `L_{c^{-1}}`. The `ι`-realizability statement '`E ⊕ E^∨(−w)` is `ι`-real' needs a constant line `L_b` with `ι(b) = q^w` exactly: such `b` exists in `K^alg` when `w` is an integer `(b = q^w)` or more generally when `q^w ∈ ι(K^alg)`, for instance when `ι` is an isomorphism `K^alg ≅ C` (DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.5); for an arbitrary embedding `ι` and irrational `w` it need not exist. This gives the real-weight normalisation used by [§RD.6.83](#rd-6-83) and [§RD.6.85](#rd-6-85) (which only twist to weight 0), and restricts the real-weight realizability statement of [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) to the cases listed.

*Hypotheses.* `E ι`-pure of weight `w` (pointwise, [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28)); `X` nonempty.

*Proof sketch.*

1. `|ι(α)| = q^{wd/2}` by purity, so `|ι(c)| = |ι(α)|^{1/d} = q^{w/2}; c` is algebraic over `K`, so `K' = K(c)` is finite.
2. At a closed point `y` of degree `e`, the eigenvalues of `F_y` on `E(c^{-1})` are those of `E` multiplied by `c^{−e}` ([§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59)), of absolute value `q^{we/2}·q^{−we/2} = 1`.
3. For `ι`-reality of `E ⊕ (E^∨ ⊗ L_b)`: the eigenvalues of `E^∨ ⊗ L_b` at `y` are `b^e/β` for eigenvalues `β` of `E; ι(b^e/β) =` conj`(ι(β))` for all `β` of absolute value `q^{we/2}` iff `ι(b)^e = q^{we}`, which holds when `ι(b) = q^w`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Section 6.1, p. 40, and proofs of Theorems 6.5.1 and 6.6.2, pp. 48-50; Abe, *Langlands program for p-adic coefficients and the petites camarades conjecture*, Remark 6.2 (ii), p. 7.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.59](#rd-6-59) *Constant rank-one F-isocrystals (twists)*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) *`ι`-real and `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.4 *`ι`-weights of nonzero elements of a coefficient field*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.5 *Embeddings into `ℂ` extending a given embedding, and isomorphisms `ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ`*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.15 *Twists `V^{(b)}` and Tate twists `V(r)`*.

**Checks.**

- On `Spec 𝔽_q`, the constant line `F = (√q)^3` has weight 3: `c = (√q)^3` normalises it to weight 0, whereas `c = √q` leaves weight 2.
- `E = O(−1)` on `Spec 𝔽_q` (weight 2): `c = q, E(q^{-1}) = O`.
- `E` on `Spec 𝔽_3` with `F = 4` (weight `2·log_3` 4): `c = 4` and `E(4^{-1})` is trivial, although no Tate twist reaches weight 0.

### RD.6.83 Purity of `H¹` on the affine line via the Fourier transform

**Theorem.** Let `M` be an absolutely irreducible `(σ, ∇)`-module over `K⟨x⟩†` which is `ι`-pure of weight `w`, and suppose there is `d ≥ 0` such that for every finite extension `K'` of `K` and every a in its ring of integers: `dim H⁰_loc(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = dim H¹_loc(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = 0` and `dim H¹(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) = d (M' = M ⊗_K K')`. Then `H¹(M)` and `H¹_c(M)` are `ι`-pure of weight `w + 1`.

*Hypotheses.*

- `M` absolutely irreducible, `ι`-pure of weight `w`; the stated local and global dimension conditions for all twists `L_{ax}`.
- For the reduction to weight zero, `w` is an integer, or a constant F-line realising the real-weight normalisation is given ([§RD.6.82](#rd-6-82)).

*Proof sketch.*

1. Assume `π ∈ K` and `w = 0` (twist); then `M` and `M^∨` have complex-conjugate trace functions, and so do `M' ⊗ L_{ax}` and `(M')^∨ ⊗ L_{−ax}`.
2. With `H⁰_loc = H¹_loc = 0` the forget-supports map `H¹_c → H¹` is an isomorphism (exact sequence (2.6.1)); duality gives a perfect Frobenius-equivariant pairing `H¹(M' ⊗ L_{ax}) × H¹((M')^∨ ⊗ L_{−ax}) → K'(−1)`.
3. By [§RD.6.50](#rd-6-50), `M̂` and the transform of `M^∨` are absolutely irreducible `(σ, ∇)`-modules of `rank d; M̂` and the pullback of `M^∨̂` along `x ↦ −x` have conjugate trace functions, so their sum is `ι`-real.
4. By [§RD.6.77](#rd-6-77) (on `A^1`), each is `ι`-pure of a weight `j`; the pairing into `K(−1)` (weight 2) forces `j + j = 2`, so `j = 1`, and the fibre at `s = 0` is `H¹(M) ≅ H¹_c(M)`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Theorem 6.5.1, p. 48, and Proof of Theorem 6.5.1, p. 49.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.50](#rd-6-50) *The Fourier transform is an irreducible F-isocrystal under constant fibre cohomology*; [§RD.6.77](#rd-6-77) *Constituents of `ι`-real isocrystals on curves are `ι`-pure*; [§RD.6.44](#rd-6-44) *The Fourier transform agrees with the geometric Fourier transform*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.5.46](#rd-5-46) *Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy*; [§RD.6.82](#rd-6-82) *Normalising an `ι`-pure coefficient to weight zero*.

**Checks.**

- `M = L_{x^d}` with `p ∤ d ≥ 2` (absolutely irreducible, `ι`-pure of weight 0): the twists `L_{x^d + ax}` have `H⁰_loc = H¹_loc = 0` and `dim H¹ = d − 1` for all `a`, so `H¹(A^1, L_{x^d})` is `ι`-pure of weight 1, the rigid form of `|Σ_x ψ(x^d)| ≤ (d − 1)√q` ([§RD.6.85](#rd-6-85)).
- `M = O` fails the hypothesis at `a ≡ 0` mod `π (H⁰_loc ≠ 0)`, consistent with `H¹(A^1) = 0`.

<a id="rd-6-84"></a>

### RD.6.84 Rigid Weil II on the affine line

**Theorem.** Let `E` be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on `A^1_{𝔽_q}` which is `ι`-realizable and `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w`. Then `H¹_rig(A^1/K, E)` is `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w + 1`.

*Hypotheses.* `E ι`-realizable and (pointwise) `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w` on `A^1`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Enlarge `k` and reduce to `M` absolutely irreducible; by [§RD.6.77](#rd-6-77) `M` is `ι`-pure, of weight `w` after twisting.
2. Choose `N` as in [§RD.6.56](#rd-6-56) for `M` and `M^∨` and `n > N` prime to `p`; form `Q = f^*M^∨ ⊗ L_{sx^n}` over `K⟨s, x⟩†` and a localization A of `K⟨s, s^{−1}⟩†` over which `R^1 g_! Q_A` and `R^1 g_* Q_A` are `(σ, ∇)`-modules (generic pushforward theorem, RD.5).
3. [§RD.6.31](#rd-6-31) gives an F-equivariant injection `H¹_c(M^∨) ↪ H⁰_loc(R^1 g_! Q_A)`.
4. By [§RD.6.56](#rd-6-56) the fibres `M^∨ ⊗ L_{ax^n + cx}` satisfy the hypotheses of [§RD.6.83](#rd-6-83), so `R^1 g_! Q_A` is `ι`-pure of weight `−w + 1`; by [§RD.6.81](#rd-6-81) `H⁰_loc` of it is `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ −w + 1`, hence so is `H¹_c(M^∨)`.
5. Poincaré duality ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89)) gives `H¹(M) ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w + 1`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Theorem 6.5.3, p. 49.

**Checks.**

- `E = O: H¹(A^1) = 0`, trivially mixed of weight `≥ 1`.

### RD.6.85 Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over `𝔽_q, ι : K^alg ↪ C`, and `E` an `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal on `X`. (a) If `E` is (pointwise) `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w`, then for each `i, Hⁱ_{c,rig}(X/K, E)` is `ι`-mixed of weight `≤ w + i`. (b) If `X` is smooth and `E` is `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w`, then for each `i, Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)` is `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ w + i`. The hypothesis '`ι`-realizable' holds whenever `E` is a successive extension of `ι`-pure objects of integer weights (the global notion of the notes, Definition 10.2); for real weights the scalar-normalisation qualification of [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) applies. In particular constant coefficients are `ι`-realizable for every `ι`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` separated of finite type over `𝔽_q` (smooth in (b)); `E ι`-realizable; `ι` arbitrary.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Induction on `n = dim X`, then on `rank E`, for all `q` simultaneously.
2. (b) `⇒ (a)` by Poincaré duality ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89)); by excision ([§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19)) and induction, (a) reduces to `X` smooth affine of pure dimension `n`, and by duality again to (b) for `X` or any open dense subset.
3. Enlarge `K` and twist to `w = 0`; by the geometric lemma (RD.5) an open dense affine `U` is finite étale over `A^n`, and `Hⁱ(U, E) = Hⁱ(A^n, f_*E)` (finite étale pushforward, RD.4), so `X = A^n`; reduce to `E` irreducible by the long exact sequence.
4. Write `A^n = A^1 × A^{n−1}, f` the projection; over an open dense `W ⊂ A^{n−1}` the kernel `𝔽_0` and cokernel `𝔽_1` of the vertical connection are overconvergent F-isocrystals (generic pushforward theorem, RD.5); if `𝔽_0 ≠ 0` then `E = f^*𝔽_0` and induction applies; else `𝔽_0 = 0`.
5. `ι`-realizability of `𝔽_1`: choose `E'` with `E ⊕ E' ι`-real and semisimple; by the trace formula ([§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23)) the fibre traces of `𝔽_1 ⊕ 𝔽_1'` minus those of `𝔽_0'` are `ι`-real, so `𝔽_1` is `ι`-realizable.
6. By [§RD.6.84](#rd-6-84) on the fibres, `𝔽_1` is `ι`-mixed of weight `≥ 1`; by induction `H^{i−1}_rig(W, 𝔽_1)` is mixed `≥ i`; since `𝔽_0 = 0` the Leray sequence (Kedlaya Finiteness Proposition 7.4.1, RD.5) gives a Frobenius-equivariant injection `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E) ↪ H^{i−1}_rig(W/K, 𝔽_1)`, which gives (b) on `X` (Kedlaya prints `f_*E^∨` in place of `E` here; see *Corrections to the sources*).

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Theorem 6.6.2, p. 50, and Theorem 6.6.2 (b), p. 50; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 10.3, p. 27.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.84](#rd-6-84) *Rigid Weil II on the affine line*; [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) *`ι`-real and `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28) *Pointwise `ι`-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19) *The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology*; [§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10) *Rigid cohomology `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.4.12](#rd-4-12) *Rigid cohomology with compact supports `Hⁱ_{c,rig}(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.5.7](#rd-5-7) *Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic*; [§RD.5.52](#rd-5-52) *Generic pushforwards are `(σ,∇)`-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)*; [§RD.5.53](#rd-5-53) *The Leray long exact sequence for the projection `A⟨x⟩† → A`*; [§RD.5.88](#rd-5-88) *Compatibility of the Poincaré pairing with the two excision sequences*; [§RD.6.82](#rd-6-82) *Normalising an `ι`-pure coefficient to weight zero*.

**Checks.**

- `G_m`, constant coefficients: `H¹_c` weight `0 ≤ 0 + 1` and `H¹` weight `2 ≥ 0 + 1` ([§RD.6.29](#rd-6-29)).
- `P^1: H⁰` weight 0, `H²` weight `2 = 0 + 2` ([§RD.6.27](#rd-6-27)).

### RD.6.86 Purity of rigid cohomology of smooth proper varieties

**Theorem.** Let `X` be a smooth proper scheme over `𝔽_q` and `E` an `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal that is `ι`-pure of weight `w`. Then `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)` is `ι`-pure of weight `w + i` for every `i`. For constant coefficients `E = O_X, Hⁱ_rig(X/K)` is `ι`-pure of weight `i` for every embedding `ι : K^alg ↪ C`; hence every eigenvalue of `F` on `Hⁱ_rig(X/K)` is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value `q^{i/2}` (a Weil `q`-number of weight `i`).

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth and proper over `𝔽_q; E ι`-realizable, `ι`-pure of weight `w` (for constant coefficients: any `ι`).

*Proof sketch.*

1. `X` proper `⇒ Hⁱ_c = Hⁱ` ([§RD.4.12](#rd-4-12)).
2. [§RD.6.85](#rd-6-85) (a) gives weights `≤ w + i` and (b) (`X` smooth) gives weights `≥ w + i`; so every eigenvalue has `|ι(α)| = q^{(w+i)/2}`.
3. `O_X` is `ι`-pure of weight 0 and `ι`-realizable for every `ι` ([§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57)).
4. An element of `K^alg` that is `ι`-pure of weight `i` for every `ι` is algebraic over `Q` and a Weil `q`-number of weight `i` (DeligneWeightsAndPurity Layer DWP.0, bridge between `ι`-weights and Weil numbers).

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.6 (c) and following, p. 51–52, and §6.6, p. 52.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.85](#rd-6-85) *Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)*; [§RD.6.57](#rd-6-57) *`ι`-real and `ι`-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.4.12](#rd-4-12) *Rigid cohomology with compact supports `Hⁱ_{c,rig}(X/K, E)`*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.4 *`ι`-weights of nonzero elements of a coefficient field*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.7 *Eigenvalues, Weil purity and `ι`-weights of an invertible endomorphism*; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.6 *Algebraicity and Weil purity from `ι`-purity at every `ι`*.

**Checks.**

- `P^1: H⁰` weight 0 (eigenvalue 1), `H²` weight 2 (eigenvalue `q`).
- Ordinary `E/𝔽_7: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1` has `H¹` eigenvalues the roots of `T^2 − 3T + 7`, of absolute value `√7`; supersingular `y^2 = x^3 + x` over `𝔽_7`: roots of `T^2 + 7`, absolute value `√7`.

<a id="rd-6-87"></a>

### RD.6.87 Functional equation of the rigid Weil factors

**Lemma.** Let `X` be smooth proper of pure dimension `n` over `𝔽_q, P_i(t) := det(1 − tF | Hⁱ_rig(X/K))` and `b_i := deg P_i = dim Hⁱ`. Then `P_{2n−i}(t) = c_i · t^{b_i} · P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1})` with `c_i = (−1)^{b_i} q^{n b_i} / det(F | Hⁱ_rig(X/K))`. (Kedlaya prints `P_{2n−i}(t) = c t^j P_i(t^{−1})`, omitting `q^{−n}`; see *Corrections to the sources*.)

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth proper of pure dimension `n` over `𝔽_q`.

*Proof sketch.* Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré duality `Hⁱ × H^{2n−i} → K(−n)` ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89); `H_c = H` for proper `X`): the eigenvalues of `F` on `H^{2n−i}` are `q^n/α_j` for the eigenvalues `α_j` on `Hⁱ`, with multiplicity (`F` bijective, [§RD.6.14](#rd-6-14)). Then `P_{2n−i}(t) = ∏_j (1 − q^n t/α_j) = ∏_j (q^n t − α_j) / ∏_j (−α_j)`, and `∏_j (q^n t − α_j) = (q^n t)^{b_i} P_i(1/(q^n t))`; since `∏_j (−α_j) = (−1)^{b_i} det(F | Hⁱ)`, this is `c_i t^{b_i} P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1})`. (Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §6.6 (b), p. 52.)

*Needs:* [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.6.14](#rd-6-14) *Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology of a smooth variety*; [§RD.4.12](#rd-4-12) *Rigid cohomology with compact supports `Hⁱ_{c,rig}(X/K, E)`*.

**Checks.**

- `P^1 (n = 1, i = 0): P_2(t) = 1 − qt` and `c_0 t P_0`(1/(qt)) `= −q·t·`(`1 − 1`/(qt)) `= 1 − qt` with `c_0 = −q`; the printed form `c t^j P_0(1/t) = c(t^j − t^{j−1})` is never `1 − qt`.

### RD.6.88 The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve

**Lemma.** Let `X` be a smooth proper curve over `𝔽_q, D ⊂ X` a nonempty reduced finite closed subscheme and `Y = X − D`. There is a Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence `0 → H¹_rig(X/K) → H¹_rig(Y/K) → ⊕_{x ∈ |D|} H⁰_rig(x/K)^∨(−1) → H²_rig(X/K) → H²_rig(Y/K) → 0`, whose first map is restriction. If `D` meets every connected component of `X` (equivalently `Y` is affine), then `H²_rig(Y/K) = 0`.

*Hypotheses.* `X` smooth proper curve over `𝔽_q; D` reduced, finite, nonempty; `Y = X − D`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Compact-support excision for `D ⊂ X` ([§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19)): `0 → H⁰_c(Y) → H⁰(X) → H⁰(D) → H¹_c(Y) → H¹(X) → H¹(D) = 0 → H²_c(Y) → H²(X) → 0`, Frobenius-equivariant (`X` proper: `H_c = H; D` has dimension 0, [§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18)).
2. Dualise with Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré duality on the smooth curves `X` and `Y` ([§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89)): `H^j(Y) ≅ H^{2−j}_c(Y)^∨(−1), H^j(X) ≅ H^{2−j}(X)^∨(−1)`; the dual of `H⁰(D) → H¹_c(Y) → H¹(X) → 0` twisted by `(−1)` gives the displayed sequence (duality is natural for restriction/excision).
3. If `D` meets every component, `H⁰(X) → H⁰(D)` is injective (a horizontal section vanishing at a point of a connected component vanishes, [§RD.6.28](#rd-6-28)), so `H⁰_c(Y) = 0` and `H²(Y) = 0`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, §2.1, (2.1.2), p. 11, and §2.6, (2.6.1), p. 18.

*Needs:* [§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19) *The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18) *Rigid cohomology of `Spec 𝔽_{q^d}`*; [§RD.6.3](#rd-6-3) *Tate twists of overconvergent F-isocrystals*; [§RD.4.10](#rd-4-10) *Rigid cohomology `Hⁱ_rig(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.4.12](#rd-4-12) *Rigid cohomology with compact supports `Hⁱ_{c,rig}(X/K, E)`*; [§RD.5.88](#rd-5-88) *Compatibility of the Poincaré pairing with the two excision sequences*.

**Checks.**

- `X = P^1, D = {0, ∞}: 0 → 0 → H¹(G_m) → K(−1)^2 → K(−1) → 0`, so `H¹(G_m) ≅ K(−1) (F = q)`.
- `X = E` an elliptic curve, `D = {O}: H¹(E − O) ≅ H¹(E)`.

### RD.6.89 Constant coefficients on affine curves have `H¹_c` of nonnegative slopes

**Lemma.** Let `C` be a smooth affine curve over `𝔽_q` and `V` an F-isocrystal over `Spec 𝔽_q` (a finite-dimensional K-space with linear Frobenius) all of whose slopes are `≥ 0`, with pullback `V_C` to `C`. Then `H¹_{c,rig}(C/K, V_C)` has all slopes `≥ 0`. The vanishing asserted in Kedlaya's Lemma 6.7.2 for horizontally constant constituents fails (`O` on `G_m` has `H¹_c = K`); this lemma is the base case of [§RD.6.90](#rd-6-90).

*Hypotheses.* `C` smooth affine over `𝔽_q` with smooth compactification `C̄` and boundary `D = C̄ − C; V` of slopes `≥ 0`.

*Proof sketch.*

1. `H¹_{c,rig}(C/K, V_C) ≅ H¹_{c,rig}(C/K) ⊗_K V` with Frobenius `F ⊗ F_V` (constant coefficients; [§RD.5.94](#rd-5-94) with the point), and slopes of a tensor product are sums of slopes ([§RD.6.58](#rd-6-58)), so it suffices to treat `V = K`.
2. Excision for `D ⊂ C̄` gives `H⁰(C̄) → H⁰(D) → H¹_c(C) → H¹(C̄) → 0` ([§RD.6.88](#rd-6-88), [§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19)); the eigenvalues of `F` on `H⁰(D)` are roots of unity ([§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18)), of slope 0.
3. Extend constants to `𝔽_{q^h}` so that every geometric component of `C̄` is defined, and write the base change as a disjoint union of geometrically connected smooth proper curves `C̄_j`. On each component, `H⁰=K′` and `H²=K′(−1)` for the `q^h`-Frobenius `F^h`. Thus the trace formula gives `Z(C̄_j,t)=P_{1,j}(t)/((1−t)(1−q^h t))`. Its integral zeta series makes `P_{1,j}` integral; reversing this constant-term-one polynomial shows that all eigenvalues of `F^h` on `H¹(C̄_j)` are algebraic integers. Take the direct sum over components and use base change (RD.6.21). The eigenvalues become `α^h`, and `v_{q^h}(α^h)=v_q(α)`, so nonnegative slopes descend to `H¹(C̄)`.
4. The slopes of `H¹_c(C)` are those of the subquotients, hence `≥ 0`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Lemma 6.7.2 and its proof, p. 52; Kedlaya, *Notes on isocrystals*, Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.7, p. 22.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.21](#rd-6-21) *Finite extension of constants and Frobenius powers*; [§RD.6.22](#rd-6-22) *The canonical finite-field zeta function as a rigid L-function*; [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.6.88](#rd-6-88) *The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve*; [§RD.6.18](#rd-6-18) *Rigid cohomology of `Spec 𝔽_{q^d}`*; [§RD.6.58](#rd-6-58) *p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals*; [§RD.4.19](#rd-4-19) *The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology*; [§RD.5.94](#rd-5-94) *The Künneth formula with supports for smooth varieties (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.2))*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; Mathlib `Polynomial.reverse`; DeligneWeightsAndPurity §0.10 *The characteristic power series `det(1 − tF)` and traces of powers*.

**Checks.**

- For `C=ℙ¹∖{0,1,∞}`, the canonical zeta series is `(1−t)²/(1−qt)`. Its rigid expression has `H¹_c=K²` with Frobenius 1, so both slopes are 0.
- For `C=A¹_{𝔽_{q²}}` viewed over `𝔽_q`, the compactification has two geometric components. Over `𝔽_{q²}` they are two copies of `ℙ¹`; no constant extension makes their whole union geometrically connected. Before extension `F` permutes the two `H⁰` generators and acts as `q` times that permutation on `H²`; `H¹_c(C)=0`.

- `C = G_m: H¹_c = K` with `F = 1`, slope 0.
- `C = E − {O}` for an elliptic curve `E/𝔽_7` with `a_7 = 3: H¹_c ≅ H¹(E)` with slopes 0 and 1.

### RD.6.90 `H¹_c` of an isocrystal with nonnegative slopes on an affine curve has nonnegative slopes

**Lemma.** Let `C` be an affine curve over `𝔽_q` and `E` an overconvergent F-isocrystal on `C` with slopes in [0, `∞`). Then `H¹_{c,rig}(C/K, E)` has slopes in [0, `∞`).

*Hypotheses.* `C` affine curve over `𝔽_q; E` with nonnegative slopes.

*Proof sketch.*

1. Separate the horizontally constant constituents by exact sequences. Their `H¹_c` does not generally vanish: for `O` on `G_m` it is `K`. Its nonnegative slopes follow from the compactification exact sequence and the nonnegative-slope crystalline lattice of the smooth proper curve, including boundary-point permutation representations.
2. For an irreducible constituent with `H⁰(E)=H⁰(E^∨)=0`, duality gives `H²_c(E)=0` and compact support gives `H⁰_c(E)=0`. The trace formula then makes every power trace on `H¹_c` p-integral.
3. Power traces p-integral for all powers force all eigenvalues to have nonnegative valuation: the generating rational function `Σ Tr(F^n)t^n` has integral coefficients and no pole in `|t|<1`; a negative-valuation eigenvalue would give such a pole, with a nonzero multiplicity in characteristic zero.

*Sources.* Kedlaya, *Fourier transforms and p-adic 'Weil II'*, Lemma 6.7.2, p. 52.

*Needs:* [§RD.6.23](#rd-6-23) *The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius*; [§RD.6.58](#rd-6-58) *p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals*; [§RD.5.89](#rd-5-89) *Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)*; [§RD.6.89](#rd-6-89) *Constant coefficients on affine curves have `H¹_c` of nonnegative slopes*.

**Checks.**

- `E = O` on `G_m: H¹_c = K` with `F = 1`, slope 0.
